chunks.title: Corpus v3, replay driver and full-daemon test harness
chunks.goal: Extend tests/contracts/http_corpus.py (schema v2, 16 cases) to v3: HTTP, MCP tool calls through POST /api/mcp/{server_name}/tools/{tool_name} with the operator credential, WS messages and CLI invocations; seeded state; DB-delta assertions (normalized row diffs); side-effect captures (pg_notify channels, WS publishes, files_home writes); per-field normalizers. The recorder runs only against isolated Python daemons built from the worktree (temp state and ports, gobby_test hub) and refuses any other DATABASE_URL. Rust side: one shared test-support crate (replaces the four test-DB env vars); a full-daemon harness (gdaemon plus the Python worker from the worktree on temp ports); and a replay driver that extends crates/gdaemon/tests/http_contracts.rs beyond proxy-only, with per-family proxy, native or compare backends, a differential mode (same case on proxy and native, responses and DB deltas compared), a soak loop (corpus in seeded random order for N hours in Compare mode) and a summary over front-door-compare.jsonl via gdaemon compare-report. Proxy self-replay is the fixture-validity gate. The /api/admin/test/* seeding routes become a test-only harness feature, and their rows are dropped as non-product (D20). Guard: the harness asserts that DATABASE_URL names the isolated test hub (gobby_test at 127.0.0.1:60892) before it sets GOBBY_ALLOW_WORKTREE_DAEMON=1, and gives every harness run its own database, so the worktree-daemon override can never reach the live hub; the e2e harness's existing override (tests/e2e/test_daemon_lifecycle.py:427, test_composer_live_proof.py:159) moves behind the same guard. It starts after #25599 is fixed (start gate). The harness also provides the dormancy proof that every later chunk runs (D37): the full-daemon harness on code defaults replays every existing corpus unchanged, and a test selects another backend only through front_door.routes in its temporary home or a constructor parameter. It also gives the harness a loopback-only network mode for daemons started on restored copies of live data, which every cutover rehearsal uses: outbound connections other than loopback fail, proven by a test in which a fixture daemon's outbound connection to a non-loopback address fails. The map names no egress control that exists in the tree today, so this chunk chooses and proves the mechanism. The waiver match extends with the schema: surface_matches accepts only HTTP surfaces in both loaders today (scripts/parity_waivers.py:123-139; crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/waivers.rs:77-97), so a cited MCP, WS or CLI case would raise a WaiverError, and family plans carry entries on those surfaces. Schema v3 matches each case kind to its exact ledger key (MCP <server>:<tool>, MCP HTTP gobby:<tool>, MCP stdio gobby:<tool>, WS message <type>, CLI gobby <verb>), and the classify rule holds on all four kinds: a cited case asserts its native answer and an uncited one its recording (D84). The guard also accepts a rehearsal stack's gobby_test database on that stack's own port when a rehearsal profile names it (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:211-233), because every cutover rehearsal starts its daemons there; the live hub still fails it. The harness drops each run's database at teardown and, at its start, sweeps any database of its own name pattern whose pid is dead, as tests/fixtures/postgres.py:50-52 and 346-369 do for pytest, because the test hub's data sits on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27) that every chunk session's runs share.
engines: Rust replay, differential and soak driver
chunks.oracle: Existing: HTTP corpus v2 (16 cases), terminal_ws_golden (44), ws_envelope_golden and the runtime grant vectors must replay unchanged through the v3 driver; every new case must pass proxy self-replay. The loopback-only mode adds one case: an outbound connection to a non-loopback address fails. A fixture entry cited by one case of each kind replays as Waived on its native answer and fails on any other, and a citation whose surface differs from its case raises WaiverError on both engines. Inside a spawned session managed SRT fails every non-loopback connection by itself, so the loopback-only case proves nothing there: it carries a control in which the same connection succeeds with the mode off, and it runs through protocol step 6's route, outside the sandbox. A run's database is gone after its teardown, and a database left by a dead pid is swept at the next start.
chunks.size: L, 3 checkpoints (v3 schema and recorder; test support and full-daemon harness; differential, soak and compare-report). Python in scope: tests/contracts and e2e fixtures (~3K); new Rust test code ~5K.
chunks.registration: New dev-only test-support crate (publish=false) used as a dev-dependency; gdaemon tests/. No family registry, serve.rs, main.rs or migrations. Adding the member changes every binary's fingerprint, so this landing bumps gdaemon (D39). It also edits surface_matches in crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/waivers.rs and scripts/parity_waivers.py.
chunks.risks: Nondeterminism (timestamps, seq numbers, ordering) yields false diffs: normalizers are part of the schema, get adversarial review, and must not hide ordering bugs. Isolation: the harness must never reach the live daemon or its DB.

chunks.title: Hook-decision corpus, known-bad registry and regex audit
chunks.goal: Record the oracle for the top-friction engine before any port (Josh item 4). A hook-decision corpus: envelope in, normalized decision out (allow, block, injected context, variables set, side effects), produced by the Python hook pipeline and rule engine in an isolated daemon over (a) synthetic rule bodies that exercise engine features and synthetic envelopes per CLI adapter (claude, codex, droid, grok, agy), committed, and (b) real envelope shapes mined read-only from local CLI transcripts, kept local and never committed. On P, (b) is thin: A's transcripts are not on P and a managed run reads no other provider's root (docs/guides/sandboxing.md:238-243), so a session records what it found and goes on, because (a) covers every adapter and this chunk's oracle does not depend on (b). The known-bad registry (.gobby/plans/task-25341.md 2.1 rows {ref, entry, input, field, python_observed, correct}) for #24177, #24286, #24298 x5, #24299 x2, #24772, #25321 x2 and the unfiled uv lock/uv sync case, with every affected corpus case marked. A static audit of every bundled command_pattern and rule regex for Rust-regex incompatibility (backreferences, lookaround), each with its rewrite or an explicit engine decision. The regex audit covers the 76 lookaround and backreference matches in at least 10 bundled rule files (tool-hygiene/require-uv.yaml and worker-safety/no-force-push.yaml among them): each gets a proposed linear-time rewrite that both engines accept and an equivalence case, and a pattern with no equivalent goes to Josh (D33). No case asserts a bundled rule's behavior: bundled YAML is validated against the engine schema and loader only (Josh's 2026-10-27 ruling on #25256; s2-11 Decision 11), and the regex audit's equivalence cases test a pattern's rewrite on both engines, not a rule. The committed corpus has three layers, each schema-versioned with a manifest, a loader, a coverage check and a README that names the record and replay commands and the re-record obligation when the engine changes (s2-11 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4). Rule-pass cases (tests/contracts/rules/): synthetic definition_json rows with priority and project id, the session facts and pre-pass variables, the normalized event, an ordered script of every seam and external-effect call with its recorded result or failure, the helper family or observer the case exercises, and an expect block holding every HookResponse field _assemble_response fills, the eager variable delta, the staged on_receipt payload, the ordered effect log with the engine's workflow_audit_log and rule_eval metric writes, record_rule_evaluation's audit records and the outcome class (zero_match, matched_allow, mutating or block). The required scenarios are s2-11 1.1's: all 15 RuleEffect types and both delivery classes, ordering, aggregate blocking, the agent-scope, audience and active-rule filters, project scoping, a skipped parse failure, a condition error in a block and in a non-block rule, one failing call per seam kind, the blocking deadline, F4's rewrite recheck, every hardcoded behavior and every response field, one allow, one block and one seam-error case per helper family and per observer, and three event-sequence transitions. The exporter seeds rows through RuleDefinitionManager in the isolated test hub and runs RuleEngine.evaluate with each seam-backed helper, effect executor and direct store call the engine makes (WorkflowAuditManager, MetricsEventStore, CoordinationWaitManager, CompletionSubscriberManager, InterSessionMessageManager and ToolResultStore) wrapped in a pytest recorder, so no production Python changes. It also writes tests/contracts/rules/normalize_vectors.json from the normalizer entry points and every cross-module function of the modules RULE-N1 and RULE-N2 port, including src/gobby/hooks/_normalization_archives.py, _normalization_patch.py, _normalization_git_apply.py and tool_outcomes.py (GW-1's gcore port, which RULE-N2 reuses, D99), which s2-11 1.1 does not list, and appends the known-bad rows to it tagged known_bad. Adapter cases (tests/contracts/adapters/): one adapter call per case, a raw provider payload with its delivery origin and the expected HookEvent, or a HookResponse and the expected provider JSON, replayed from tests/fixtures/provider_contracts/ plus synthetic payloads, covering every hook type each of the five adapters accepts and every response field it emits, with node-origin no-file cases for Site rows 20 and 28-30 (s2-11 Site Disposition). Pipeline cases (tests/contracts/pipeline/): HookManager.handle with every collaborator call recorded and the real rule engine, one case per EventHandlers.get_handler_map entry and event type, session start for a new, resumed, cleared and compacted session, a node session missing its row, a deferred activation, a blocking webhook, a rule block that short-circuits the handler and one failing collaborator per collaborator kind. The regex audit also covers the rule files this repository keeps outside the bundled tree (.gobby/workflows/rules/), because they sync to the same rows on every restart (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:81): the lookbehind of quiet-hours.yaml:24 gets the same linear-time rewrite and equivalence case (D33, D77). The registry holds a Python defect shown below any one ledger surface, in a vector or in a flow across surfaces; a difference that one case shows on one exact surface takes a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry instead (D84). The hold-open resolve defect (#25708: no production code assigns _pending_interaction_manager, read at src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/_interaction_responses.py:84 and src/gobby/servers/websocket/session_control.py:129; only tests/servers/test_session_control.py:2116 sets it) is recorded by #25708's state when this chunk records. While it is open: two rows with ref #25708, on a host wired as production wires it. One has entry ChatInteractionResponsesMixin._handle_tool_approval_response, input a browser tool_approval_response for a pending hold-open wait, field the wait's outcome, python_observed unresolved until it times out, correct resolved. The other has entry SessionControlMixin._rebroadcast_pending_interactions, input a client reconnecting during that wait, field the pending frames it receives, python_observed none, correct one per pending interaction. If its fix has already wired the manager: no rows, and the hold-open cases record Python's resolve and rebroadcast as ordinary cases. If its fix lands after this chunk records: D18 applies, so its commit retires the rows and re-records the affected cases. If #25708 instead removes the path as unreachable: no rows, because Python then has no answer to record, and its commit retires any row already recorded. Its rule-pass cases also cover a before_tool and an after_tool event whose metadata sets _cli_internal_request, on which a synthetic rule in the progressive-discovery group is skipped and every other rule runs (src/gobby/workflows/engine/evaluation.py:582-588). The adapter corpus also covers source git, the guard's one event and both verdicts, because the route accepts a sixth source (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/hooks.py:85; tests/adapters/test_git_adapter.py).
engines: hook pipeline and rule engine (oracle only)
hook adapters and command normalization (oracle only)

Python's engine, normalizer functions, adapters and HookManager reproduce every case and vector of their layer.

chunks.goal: #25468 per .gobby/plans/task-25468.md (M1 8877284c44). 1.1: static inventory of every startup job and service owner, identity and error. 1.2: runtime census. 1.3: versioned private worker protocol (handshake; Rust-assigned generation and op IDs; fail-closed auth; a lost reply on an effectful call is an unknown outcome to reconcile, never blind-retry). Protocol changes are additive: HEAD's worker accepts every protocol version that a retained or pinned gdaemon speaks, with a test per version, because a restored gdaemon boots the Python worker from HEAD's checkout; old versions are removed only at S3-DELETE. 1.4: facade over GobbyRunner.create's five phases in a new src/gobby/worker/ package, plus the allow-listed domain-invocation op table (one registration line per op) that later chunks extend for single-owner services. The brief pins runner_lifecycle*.py (10 files, 3,839 lines, run_daemon in runner_lifecycle.py included), not the plan's runner_lifecycle_*.py glob; the needs-planning label is stale (M1 8877284c44), and the brief points at .gobby/plans/task-25468.md. #25582's criterion is met, so R0's session closes it with the review and validation attestations. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. The 65,536-byte request bound of .gobby/plans/task-25468.md (Decision 11) covers the handshake and construction commands. A domain op's request takes the hook route's 16 MiB bound (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/hooks/ingress.rs:25), because GW-2's preflight and after phase and CHAT-2's lifecycle op carry tool arguments and outputs that exceed 64 KiB (D81, D82); a request over it fails as any failed call does. Domain ops run concurrently on the worker's event loop, so an async op such as HOOK-3's Telegram question, bounded at 110 seconds, holds up no other op and resolves on the loop its pending-interaction manager uses. R0's session also closes #25468 after #25582, because D31's pass at chunk-task creation cannot close a parent whose child stays open. P0-HARNESS need not have landed when this chunk validates. If it has not, protocol step 6's harness and dormancy proof mean crates/gdaemon/tests/http_contracts.rs's proxy replay, the e2e lifecycle tests on their temp-port daemon (tests/e2e/test_daemon_lifecycle.py) and focused pytest of the runner modules, all on code defaults; CP-RUNNER-REVIEW's packet replays this chunk's fixtures on the harness in any case. The op table encodes an op's return value as canonical JSON: a dataclass through dataclasses.asdict with its class name under a _type key, a datetime or Path as its string form, and anything else fails the call as any failed call does. So a one-line registration on a function that returns a plain dataclass, such as read_composer (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:525) or send_keys_target_refusal (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:61-70, 169), needs no shim. The encoder also takes the shapes that registrations return or hold: an Enum as its value, a set or frozenset as a sorted list, and an exception instance returned as a value, such as IndeterminateWrite (src/gobby/terminals/runtime.py:137-142; src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:629), as its class name under _type plus its attributes. So recipient_policy's RecipientPolicy (src/gobby/agents/team_communications.py:26-28) and WriteCoordinator.write's WriteOutcome (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:196-232) also need no shim, and only a shape outside these fails the call. A registration line also names the decode of a parameter JSON cannot carry, a datetime from its ISO string or a dataclass from its fields, as record_composer_local_command's row_at (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:585-588), record_queued_submit's consumed_at (src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_base.py:236-246) and WriteRequest (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:74-94) need. A worker op binds no caller and no daemon-owned execution, so require_machine_owned returns at once (src/gobby/hub/caller_scope.py:54-69) and is_daemon_execution reads false (src/gobby/utils/session_context.py:134-146): a native route makes any caller ownership check before its op call.

chunks.title: R2: initialization and readiness
chunks.goal: #25470: Rust sequences the phase calls and exposes startup outcomes; Python constructs domain services only; content refusal happens before publishing; the config initial epoch precedes service construction; HTTP readiness stays distinct from recovery. Owns the startup-progress row. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. The worker's startup_content phase runs four steps in one call (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:62-88, 297-312): the bundled sync, the import of landed files, migrate_rule_delivery_dispositions and manager construction. R2 gives that phase's initialize body two optional members, sync_bundled and import_landed, each true when absent, so TPL's and PIPE-1's native steps can replace the first two at their cuts while the other two keep running, and a retained gdaemon that sends neither keeps the whole phase (D83). The bundled step runs today only in dev mode, and with sync_bundled false the phase still sets runner._dev_mode, because manager construction reads it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:72-77, 303). Python's route cannot serve the startup-progress row under the Rust runner: its tracker is created only inside run_daemon (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:154-155), which R0's facade never calls, so it would answer done true at once (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_health.py:399-407). So the row registers on SEAM-FAMILY's registry with an exact GET claim, selected by the compiled default that CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit flips, as R6's rows are, and the deactivation commit gives it back to Python's route. It answers Python's body from the Rust phase outcomes (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_startup.py::StartupTracker.to_dict, plus restart_recovery_pending), with no credential (src/gobby/servers/middleware/auth.py:43), and while the worker is still starting. From CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation its Rust path also runs Python's datastore readiness check natively, because only run_daemon calls it (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:212-214; src/gobby/runner_service_readiness.py:27-115): after R6's startup gate and before R3's other pre-spawn steps and the worker spawn, as Python runs the gate and then this check (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:183, 212), it requires PostgreSQL, Qdrant and FalkorDB through gcore's postgres, qdrant and falkor modules and its config resolvers (crates/gcore/src/config/resolve.rs:169, 182), with Python's 30-second deadline, 1-second retry, messages and test_mode skip, and a failure ends the start with Python's message as a failed step. R2 also builds gdaemon serve's no-worker start form on a hub, behind gdaemon's compiled backend default and dormant while that default starts the worker, so CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A activates it with no code of its own. Nothing else would apply or verify the schema from then on: Python's gobby start applies it under the singleton (src/gobby/cli/daemon_start.py:218; src/gobby/cli/utils_config.py:92-108), the runner verifies it (src/gobby/runner.py:449) and construction applies it with retries (src/gobby/runner_init/helpers.py:27, 107, 141-162), all in Python, while gclient opens no datastore connection (D69) and R6's restart re-executes gdaemon with no client in between. So under the singleton serve already holds (crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/pid_file.rs:50-94) and before any door admits, this form connects with Python's startup retry delays, runs SchemaRunner's apply and then verify_database_identity (crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:172, 276-297), in that order because verify refuses a pending migration, and upserts the _personal row (src/gobby/storage/projects.py:135-166) through a gobby-core function that V1B's gdaemon content-sync also calls. It then runs the three identity steps that init_storage runs at each start and nothing else would from commit A (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:200-208), through gobby-core functions that V1B's install identity and local API key steps also call: the machine row's upsert under the sole user, which refreshes the row and allocates its node ref (src/gobby/runner_init/helpers.py:126-138; src/gobby/storage/machines.py:115-150); the local API key's adoption, whose failure logs and the start continues (src/gobby/storage/api_keys.py:129-174); and ensure_system_session, which creates the root session that a cron session's parent and a system send name, and which AG-3's send also calls (src/gobby/storage/sessions/_constants.py:135-205; src/gobby/scheduler/executor.py:326; src/gobby/sessions/mailbox.py:279-280). It records this work as the startup-progress row's hub step, which V1A's gobby start prints. R6's gate, the readiness check and R3's other pre-spawn steps then run in that order, then R2's content phase with TPL's native sync and PIPE-1's native import, then the family start hooks, and only then do the doors admit, so a hook that must come before admission, as A1-CONFIG's first publish does, can. A hook with slow work runs it on its own task. A schema refusal, which StartRefusal makes exit 78 for a worker today (src/gobby/runner.py:449-451, 641-643), takes that exit's sticky state with no worker: gdaemon sets BackendStatus::Refused with the refusal text, starts no services, holds no database ownership and stays up (crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/backend.rs:228-237; crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:237-245), because launchd and systemd would relaunch a failed exit (src/gobby/install/shared/services/com.gobby.daemon.plist.j2:38-46; src/gobby/install/shared/services/gobby-daemon.service.j2:20-23). The doors then open in that state, the front door answers 503 backend_refused on every row (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:187-206), gobby start's poll prints the reason (src/gobby/cli/daemon_start.py:188-200), and only a full restart retries. A hub with no sole user takes the same state with Python's message, run gobby install to repair identity (src/gobby/storage/users.py:125-132). A connection that still fails after the retry delays ends the start nonzero, so the service manager relaunches it. A start hook's fatal error takes that state when a relaunch could not clear its cause, and that exit when one could (SEAM-FAMILY). SCHEMA-WINDOW's rule still covers a hub ahead, and CP-FINAL-CUT's drops and every later migration apply at the start they ship in. A family's start hook may also record a named step and its outcome on the startup-progress row, as Python's tracker does (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_startup.py::StartupTracker).

chunks.title: R3: ordered recovery
chunks.goal: #25471: Rust drives a durable, resumable recovery order (hook barrier; sessions, handoffs and wakes; agents and pipelines), and Python performs the domain transactions. Native families register their recovery steps in the same order. No replay or cron runs before its prerequisites, and retained backlog never blocks listener readiness. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. One recovery step runs inside a construction phase today: memory's interrupted dream-run reconcile in init_orchestration (src/gobby/runner_init/orchestration.py:861-874). In worker mode init_orchestration skips it, as Python's loops do not start in worker mode (R4), and R3's order calls it as a worker recovery entry point before any cron or dream admission. At CP-WAVE3-CUT MEM-3's native reconcile takes that slot and the Rust side stops calling the entry point (D4), because a Python worker start that still ran it would mark a live native dream run interrupted (memory 7.3). Its recovery order carries the hook barrier's outcome between steps, which Python holds in one local today (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:671-682). The barrier step has two entry points: the drain (drain_hook_inbox_barrier, src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py:39-46) and the classification that follows it (:47-164), which takes the drain's result fields as input, writes reconciliation_pending on each unresolved active run (the fence the agent-run step reads, src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:299-334) and returns the outcome. The session reconciliation step (src/gobby/events/wake.py:192-212) takes that outcome's excluded session ids and recovery-safe flag as arguments. So HOOK-3's native startup pass replaces only the drain entry point at CP-WAVE4-CUT, with no further Python edit, and AG-WAIT's native recovery takes the classification and the steps that consume it at CP-WAVE5-CUT (s2-11 D2.1). The lifecycle monitor's reclassification of fenced runs runs the same barrier and then the agent-run step for its fenced run ids (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:430-470), so whichever side runs its iteration calls these entry points until the same activations replace them. The feedback review store's orphaned-run mark in init_orchestration (src/gobby/runner_init/orchestration.py:774, src/gobby/feedback/storage.py:333) moves as that reconcile does: a worker recovery entry point runs it, and at CP-WAVE5-CUT AG-WAIT's native mark takes that slot, because a Python worker start that still ran it would mark a live native review interrupted. A native step may declare itself pre-spawn, which R3 runs before gdaemon spawns the worker for that start or respawn, so no Python request can race it, or once per process, which a backend respawn skips, because native work outlives the worker. Every other step runs at each whole start and each respawn. Three native owners take slots this way: AG-2's sandbox pass in the sandbox_reaping slot (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:714) from CP-WAVE2-CUT; CHAT-2's pending-interaction expire pass, pre-spawn, from CP-WAVE3-CUT; and PIPE-2's hub-only, once-per-process recovery in the pipeline_recovery slot (:749) from CP-WAVE4-CUT. Rust stops calling each Python entry point at that activation, and S3-DELETE deletes it (D4).

Until AG-3's native messaging activates, it sends them through an allow-listed worker op into Python's mailbox, which AG-3 replaces with its native send. Owns the restart, shutdown and lease-handoff rows (D68). They go Native in CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit, because from then on a proxied request stops nothing: R0's facade never calls run_daemon, so Python's routes would only write the shutdown marker and set flags that no code reads (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:40-60; src/gobby/runner.py:358-375; src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:315-319), and Python never calls Rust (D19). The rows register as one family on SEAM-FAMILY's registry with exact POST claims, and the compiled default that flips the runner flips this family, so the deactivation commit gives them back to Python's routes. OPTIONS stays proxied to Python's CORSMiddleware (src/gobby/servers/app_factory.py:202-209) until CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation commit claims it on these three paths and the shared CORS layer answers it, so no front-door handoff to Python remains here after that cut. Admission runs after the front door's authenticate and before any other check or effect, in this order. (1) A bearer that starts with gobby-agent-v1., read as the front door's authenticate reads it (a case-insensitive scheme and a trimmed token, crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/auth.rs:129-142), is refused by presence, unverified, even with a valid break-glass header: restart and shutdown answer 403 with Python's managed_activation_refused detail (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:99-112; tests/servers/routes/admin/test_managed_activation_refusal.py), and lease handoff answers Python's 401 route_not_permitted, because only the other two are in Python's agent matrix (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:131-133). (2) A resolved API key (x-gobby-key-id, crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/auth.rs:125-163) is an operator. (3) A loopback peer whose X-Gobby-Break-Glass header matches the break_glass file is an operator, through a constant-time verifier that this chunk adds to gobby-core (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:486-495; src/gobby/utils/break_glass.py:89-94) and SES-2 reuses. (4) A gobby_session cookie with the browser-testing. prefix is refused with 403 browser_authority_refused, whether or not it is live. This check comes before step 5 because GET /api/auth/status answers true for a live one (src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:81-87; src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:283-300). (5) Any other gobby_session cookie goes to a one-method cookie port. Its interim adapter sends Python's existing GET /api/auth/status to the worker with only that cookie (src/gobby/servers/routes/auth.py:194-198): true admits, false answers Python's 401 session_invalid body, and an unreachable worker, any other answer or a 5-second deadline answers the typed 503 and admits nothing. No second verifier is written (D3). AUTH binds the port to SEAM-CALLERS' verifier and these POST rows to its shared CORS layer (#24964) in CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation commit, and S3-DELETE removes the adapter. (6) Anything else answers 401 missing_auth with Python's body (src/gobby/servers/middleware/auth.py:77-187). Each handler then keeps Python's order, parameters, status values and bodies (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:128-338). Restart answers already_restarting from the moment another restart takes this gate until that restart's stop closes admission. Unless force is set, protected cron runs refuse with 409 restart_protected. Until CP-WAVE1-CUT the handler reads them from Python's existing GET /api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the admitted caller's own credentials, because only Python's scheduler holds its owner id (src/gobby/scheduler/scheduler.py:73, 120-130), and any answer but a 200, or a 5-second deadline, answers the typed 503 and stops nothing. That route answers in worker mode because a construction phase sets the runner getter (src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:272). CRON's guard replaces the read in CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation commit. Restart always runs the start proof, because force skips only the cron check and the guard, and a refusal answers 409 start_refused. It matters because a worker that refuses at boot is sticky: it exits 78, gdaemon stops retrying and releases database ownership, and the front door answers 503 backend_refused on every row until a full restart (src/gobby/runner.py:631-644; crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/backend.rs:228-237; crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:237-245; crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:187-205). The proof sits behind a one-method port with two bindings. Python runs it until then because its dirty-content, worktree, pin and SRT restage steps read the Python checkout, gdaemon holds only the backend's argv and no source root (crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/backend.rs:77-97; src/gobby/cli/daemon_start.py:238), and this chunk does not reach the config service that holds the sandbox flags. CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit re-binds the port to this chunk's Rust proof in crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/start_proof.rs, because after that commit the activated build calls no worker op. Under the same bound and with Python's messages it runs the node refusal; the installed-set check, whose identity probe and agreement this chunk builds in gobby-core for V1A's promotion core to reuse (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157); the installed gdaemon's schema plan and preflight, as Python runs them (src/gobby/storage/schema_contract.py:176-200), so SCHEMA-WINDOW's rule applies and a hub ahead by a destructive receipt refuses; and verify_srt_installation (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/verify.rs:128-131) when either sandbox flag, which the binding reads through A1-CONFIG's service, is on, and a failed read refuses. A failed read answers the typed 503, stops nothing and is never reported as zero. On accept the handler writes the shutdown marker with source lease_handoff and intent stop, starts this chunk's ordered stop and answers {"handoff": "accepted"}, and that marker is what makes gdaemon release the lease and exit (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lease.py:47-53). From CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A no worker exists to respawn, so restart closes admission, runs the whole ordered stop with restart intent, and gdaemon re-executes its own binary. That keeps its service-manager job, because launchd restarts it only on a failed exit (src/gobby/install/shared/services/com.gobby.daemon.plist.j2:38-42), and keeps the native terminals (docs/guides/admin-operations.md:369). backend_pid is then null, because no process exits. R7 becomes CP-RUNNER-CUT (#25475), and R-RETIRE closes the runner epic #25467 after that cutover's window. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. Its no-worker form covers the front door's fall-through under the same compiled default: dispatch forwards a path no family claims, whether under no prefix or under a prefix whose family does not claim it, because the longest claimed prefix wins (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:112-128, 131-147), and with no backend proxy::forward answers the typed 503, which a client reads as retry later (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/proxy.rs:43-66; crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/health.rs:38-44). So with the default off such a request, and a WS upgrade on such a path, which takes ws::splice today (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:231-241), answers 404 with Python's body {"detail":"Not Found"} after authentication, UI on or off, and logs its method and path, and AUTH's catch-all still answers first for a path under no family's prefix with UI serving on. For every migration above the floor, a test enforces the directive and filename pairing in both directions, and a content lint requires both for any statement outside D22's expand set, statements built inside DO blocks with EXECUTE format(...) included: DROP, RENAME, ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE, SET NOT NULL, DROP DEFAULT, ADD CONSTRAINT on an existing table, a unique index on an existing table, ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without a DEFAULT, DELETE, TRUNCATE, an UPDATE of a column that existed before the file, a REVOKE on an object that existed before the file, CREATE OR REPLACE of an existing function or trigger, and any statement the lint cannot classify. A GRANT or REVOKE on an object that the same file creates needs no marker of its own, because the repository's migrations revoke PUBLIC's privileges on each new table in the file that creates it (crates/gcore/assets/schema/migrations/470_validation_run_records.sql:26-29; crates/gcore/tests/catalog_manifest_freshness.rs:548-555 asserts that table has no PUBLIC grant). Files at or below the floor keep their names and bytes, 426_retire_legacy_wiki.sql included, because resolve_pending_migrations and verify_receipts match each receipt's filename and checksum exactly ('receipt mismatch for schema asset v{version}'; crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:231-291; crates/gcore/src/schema/verify.rs:468-527) and an applied migration is never edited (D22); the window judges only receipts above the code head, so their names never decide a rollback. (2) Every gate accepts a hub head newer than the code head when each receipt above the code head has a non-destructive filename and each receipt at or below it matches the embedded assets as today; a destructive receipt above the head still refuses and names its version and filename. schema_migrations already stores (version, filename, checksum) (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner.rs:329; resolve_pending_migrations in crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs), so no new column is needed. (3) The runner never applies or repairs a receipt above its own head. (4) The chunk inventories every gate that compares a hub head with a binary, a pin or a checkout, citing each from code: gdaemon's identity check, verify_database_identity (crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:276-297), with its version comparison (main.rs:286-291) and the exact SchemaRunner::verify call after it (main.rs:292-296), which every Python start runs through gdaemon schema verify (src/gobby/runner.py:448-451; src/gobby/storage/schema_contract.py:236-239), as sweep-test-schemas does (main.rs:166); validate_lineage (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:153-169); resolve_pending_migrations ('receipt v{version} has no matching embedded schema asset'); the Python hub-ahead check (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:267-274, 'live hub schema v{live} is newer than this checkout') with its four callers (src/gobby/cli/daemon_lifecycle.py:499, src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:232, src/gobby/cli/pack.py:368 and src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:94); the cutover preflight (src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:113-131; src/gobby/cli/cutover.py); GEN-ROLLBACK's restore preflight, which compares the retained gdaemon with its own stamp and never with the checkout pin; and any other the inventory finds, among them every gate that R2's Rust startup adds. Under the window, verify_receipts (crates/gcore/src/schema/verify.rs:468-527) accepts exactly the receipts above the head that the predicate accepts, and verify_schema (verify.rs:175-198) still requires every catalog-manifest entry to be present and equal, accepts catalog entries absent from the manifest only while such a receipt exists, and checks seed rows as today. gdaemon schema apply, which the start also runs (src/gobby/storage/hub/postgres.py:407), reaches only validate_lineage and the pending-migration plan (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner.rs:108-124). The installed-identity check (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265, via src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:67-77) stays exact: a checkout pin that differs from the installed generation's identity still refuses, which is why schema inputs land only in a cut's step 6 (D22). The rollback path it makes true: after a cut applies an expand migration, restoring the pinned generation (GEN-ROLLBACK's restore) plus the deactivation commit starts and serves with no database restore. The deactivation commit reverts the cut's schema inputs together with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation and only the hub is ahead, which the window covers; a later cut re-lands the same migration file in its step 6 (the retry after Josh's reassessment, or the next cut that needs it), byte for byte and under its number, whose receipt then matches. Its Rust is dormant until promotion. Its Python preflight edit is in a checkpoint-only module (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py, reached through src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py only at restart, cutover, hub-backup and pack), so it forms one prepared commit on the append-only branch port/prepared/SCHEMA-WINDOW, reviewed with the chunk and recorded by SHA at its close, which CP-RUNNER-CUT lands in its step 6, before its activation commit. The chunk changes no schema-identity input: no migration, no rename or edit of an existing asset (426_retire_legacy_wiki.sql keeps its name and bytes), no baseline, catalog or seed manifest change, and RUNNER_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 1 (crates/gcore/src/schema/assets.rs:3, 510-526). So CP-RUNNER-CUT's activated build keeps its pinned generation's identity, its gdaemon-alone restore passes the partial-promotion check, and its rollback target never meets a newer hub: CP-RUNNER-CUT carries no schema step.
chunks.oracle: gcore schema tests on synthetic hubs: a non-destructive receipt above the head is accepted; a destructive one is refused and named; a mismatch at or below the head is refused as today; a broken directive and filename pairing fails the pairing test; the pairing test and the lint pass on today's migrations directory, whose files all sit at or below the floor, with 426_retire_legacy_wiki.sql unchanged; a synthetic directive-only file and a synthetic marker-only file above the floor each fail the pairing test; an unmarked file above the floor with a DROP, a SET NOT NULL, a REVOKE on an existing table or an EXECUTE format('DROP ...') inside a DO block fails the lint, and an unmarked file above the floor that creates a table, revokes PUBLIC's privileges on it and grants gobby_daemon_runtime access to it passes the lint. gdaemon schema verify cases: it passes on a hub one expand receipt ahead whose step added a table, a nullable column and an index, and it refuses one destructive receipt ahead, a manifest object that was altered or dropped, and extra catalog objects with no receipt above the head. Apply, plan, preflight and verify on a hub one expand receipt ahead leave schema_migrations and the catalog unchanged (rows and manifest compared before and after). chunks.title: Checkpoint review: the Rust runner
chunks.goal: Review pause before the Rust runner goes live. Ruling 14 names 'after we port the daemon runner' as the first checkpoint, and ruling 16 makes its cutover a one-way switchover with three outcomes. Packet: R0-R6 landed and validated on the full-daemon harness with the Rust runner: R0's lifecycle fixtures, R3's crash-point corpus, R4's fake-clock corpus and R6's shutdown-ordering corpus, plus the restart, shutdown and lease-handoff cases; the dormancy proof, in which the same harness on code defaults replays every existing corpus unchanged (D37); SEAM-FAMILY's lifecycle and job contracts that R2-R6 implement; SCHEMA-WINDOW's schema-gate tests and Python preflight test, with its prepared commit's SHA; each prepared commit and each pick that carries a schema input, listed as deferred to the next cut that lands schema inputs, because CP-RUNNER-CUT lands none (D40 item 3); GEN-ROLLBACK's isolated rehearsal and, unless Josh refused it at map approval (D38), its live drill; and the three outcomes, stating that the first or second retires the Python runner for the rest of the build (R-RETIRE), so nothing can fall back to it afterwards. On no-go, after the de-escalation, send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight gateway and pilot chunks (PROJ-1, SEAM-CALLERS, SEAM-WS, GW-1, GW-2, A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG, A1-SECRETS, B0-READ, B0-WRITE and B0-CLOSE): they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until the fixes Josh names close. When those fixes close, the session Josh opens for this review sends a second one that releases them, before it builds its new packet. R4's diff of R0's fixtures against its loop list, and R4's fake-clock case for each op on the list. R6's three rows go Native at this cut (D68), so the packet lists each admission case, the presence refusal of an agent bearer, the cookie check through Python's status route, the guard cases against Python's staging and the security review's record. R2's startup-progress row goes Native with R6's rows at this cut, so the packet also lists gobby start's poll against the native row. Before writing the packet, this review's unspawned session proves the hub rehearsal profile on a real stack, because its tests fake Docker (tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:43-69), no commit since #21868 (2026-09-05) records a real run, and a failure first met at CP-RUNNER-CUT's step 5 would sit under that cut's landing freeze: it builds a fresh stack and isolated home as that step says in docs/port/map-v2.md, restores P's newest verified hub-backup (GEN-ROLLBACK's drill's or, if Josh refused that drill, the seed backup start gate item 17 keeps) through GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE, reads one row back with docker exec and psql on the stack's PostgreSQL container, starts no daemon on it, and removes the stack and its volumes. The packet names the result and the restore's elapsed time, which sizes step 5 in the window plan; a failure is a no-go fix. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-RUNNER-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes from 0.9.0-gg as D40 item 3 defines them; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-RUNNER; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: the Rust runner goes live
chunks.goal: Category code: this task owns the activation commit, which gets the code-reviewer seat, with the deactivation commit, before the hold is set (step 3). Run the schema-identity comparison that ends step 3 as soon as that seat passes and before setting the hold, so that a difference stops this cut before anything is held, pinned, frozen or landed. Ruling 16: a one-way switchover with three outcomes. #25475, R7's runner landing, is this chunk's activation commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. The announcement also names the window's two deliberate restarts: a plain gobby restart and one gobby restart --full. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. In this step, before setting the hold, compare the activation build's schema identity (gdaemon schema version --json, the probe that src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:58 runs) with the identity of the installed generation that this step pins, and stop on any difference, because the gdaemon-alone restore refuses a changed identity (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254). (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. Projects P2 (#25038: #25045 and #25046) runs in SEAM-CALLERS after #24967, because #25045 is blocked by #24967 and #25046 by #24452, #24964 and #24967, and the project inventory, detail, checkouts and cross-project listing (#25052) are PROJ-2's, served when CP-WAVE1-CUT flips the family to Native. PROJ-1 also lands the one project metadata guard that every native reader of project.json policy outside gprojects uses (D63): crates/gcore/src/project_metadata.rs opens the sidecar .gobby/.project.json.lock as Projects plan 4.5a specifies, takes its exclusive flock within at most two seconds, checks .gobby/.project-update-recovery/ under the lock, and returns the committed object, absent metadata, or a distinct refusal for malformed or non-object metadata, an unreadable file, a lock deadline or pending evidence. It lives in gcore because B0-WRITE, B0-CLOSE, SRC and PLANS land before PROJ-2 and V5A's CLI verbs do not link gprojects. It is synchronous, so async callers run it off the executor (plan 4.5a). A caller reads in one call, or keeps the returned guard held across its merge and publication, as V5A's toggles and gprojects' writers do, and passes a held guard to nested helpers instead of locking twice, because a second flock on a new descriptor in one process blocks. Every caller takes it before any project row lock and never while holding one (.gobby/plans/gdaemon-projects-files-docs-family.md:1017-1018, 1031-1032). chunks.oracle: 1.2's family tests (crates/gprojects/tests/family.rs: dispatch_is_exact, mode_assembly_is_scoped, composition_preserves_startup) and REC-PILOT's corpus, replayed unchanged with the family registered on its Proxy default (D37). crates/gcore/tests/project_metadata.rs: a second process holding the flock past the deadline, a seeded pending entry, a malformed and a non-object file, an unreadable file and a missing file each return their distinct outcome and never a default (D63). A holder that merges and publishes under the guard excludes a second process, and a nested helper given the held guard takes no second flock (D63).

chunks.title: Seam: WS handler registry and in-process publish
chunks.goal: Frozen seam wave contract, part 3: families claim WS message types through a handler registry; FamilyContext gets an in-process publish handle, so the broker stops being private; unclaimed message types are forwarded to Python over the existing bridge. Owns the WS transports and subscribe and unsubscribe (already delegated) and ping. A claim takes effect only while its family's backend is Native, so a dormant family's types keep reaching Python (D37). The publish handle carries both operations Python's publisher sends: a filtered publish and a server-side subscribe for one connection (docs/contracts/native-ws-transport.md, Publish; src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:250-261), which TERM-2 and CHAT-2 use. The contract also carries what Python's connection handler does outside its message table (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:357-445). Each claimed handler receives the connection's id and its SEAM-CALLERS Admitted value (#25046), taken at the upgrade on a connection with a private leg as on one without (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:220-240), because the bridge's ready frame carries only admitted and confined (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/transport.rs:115-128). The registry dispatch holds the confinement gate, because a claimed frame no longer reaches Python's: on a confined connection a frame whose type is off Python's allow-list, or whose project or session selector at any depth differs from the signed claims, answers Browser message refused and reaches no handler (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:499-513; src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:90-124). A claim declares whether its handler runs on the read loop, as src/gobby/servers/websocket/message_classes.py:18-55 classifies Python's: an on-loop handler finishes before the connection's next frame is read, and a disconnect cancels the connection's off-loop handlers (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:436). A connect event runs once the welcome frame has reached the socket, and a disconnect event runs exactly once when the socket closes or a send fails, on a connection with a private leg as on one without. TERM-1's attachment finalization, CHAT-2's reconnect rebroadcast and VOICE's attached-session speech cleanup bind those events, so no family edits the frozen transport for them. This chunk also builds the leg-free connect path (D102), dormant behind one compiled default that CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit flips. Today NativeWs::accept refuses without Python's binding and opens one private leg per connection, and Python's end of that leg admits the client, sends the welcome and answers ping (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/transport.rs:237-255, 452-465; src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:216-236), so without this path every WebSocket client is refused from CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A, when no worker exists. With the default on, accept needs no binding and opens no leg, and a connection stays open when the worker exits; shutdown still closes it with 1001. Its bounds come from a constructor parameter holding what Python's bind sends: the configured ping interval and timeout, and WebSocketConfig's 5 MiB message limit (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_publish.py:130-136; src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:309-315; src/gobby/servers/websocket/models.py:40-42). That activation commit fills it in serve.rs from the DaemonConfig that A1-CONFIG moves to gcore::config, and websocket.enabled false keeps today's no-binding refusal. Admission runs after the front door's authenticate, on SEAM-CALLERS' verified-admission type, with the answers of each entry's Python owner (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:159-177): a direct refusal keeps its status and body (src/gobby/servers/websocket/auth.py:27-90), and a browser refusal keeps 101 then close 4401 (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:283-307). The first frame is the welcome, with Python's fields in Python's wire format (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:393-405): a new client_id, user_id as Python's adapter sets it (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:209; src/gobby/servers/websocket/auth.py:79-80), latency 0.0 (src/gobby/servers/websocket/asgi_adapter.py:19) and conversation_ids through a one-method port with an empty default, which CHAT-2's runtime implements. Dispatch keeps what crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/subscriptions.rs already answers (subscribe, unsubscribe and the parse refusals) and adds the confinement gate, the claimed handlers, ping, and Unknown message type for anything else (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:589-591). A handler failure answers Internal server error (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:422-424). ping answers {"type": "pong", "latency": 0.0} (src/gobby/servers/websocket/handlers/core.py:164-171). Until the flip ping stays forwarded, so nothing changes before CP-WAVE5-CUT. A binary frame takes the same dispatch, as Python's json.loads reads it. This chunk documents the form in docs/contracts/native-ws-transport.md, and S3-DELETE removes the legged form.
chunks.oracle: Existing: ws_envelope_golden, terminal_ws_golden and the delegated rows' tests. Recorded first in this chunk from Python, through P0-HARNESS's WS case kind with the entry and the connecting credential as case inputs: ping's answer; the welcome on each entry, with client_id and the generated user_id normalized; the admission matrix on both entries (no credential, a wrong scheme, an invalid token, an API key, a live and an expired cookie, a live browser-testing cookie and an agent token), with each direct status and body and each browser close; and the frames for an unknown type, a confined session's refused type and a mismatched selector. With the default off these replay unchanged, a fixture family's claimed type reaches its handler only on a Native backend and reaches Python on Proxy, and on a confined connection a claimed type off the allow-list or with a mismatched selector answers Browser message refused with no handler call. A test that turns the default on through a constructor parameter (D37) and binds no worker replays the same cases, and also shows that no leg opens, that the claimed type reaches its handler, that the connect event follows the welcome, that the disconnect event runs once on a close and once on a failed send, that a connection outlives a worker's exit, that shutdown closes it with 1001, and that websocket.enabled false refuses as it does today.

chunks.title: GW-1: native /mcp gateway with per-tool routing
chunks.goal: #24884 under runner-first (D26): native policy, discovery and dispatch at /mcp and the gobby meta-tools call_tool, get_tool_schema and list_tools (HTTP and stdio), with schema leases shared with Python through the DB. Every server:tool resolves to its own backend: Native, Compare or Proxy, where Proxy forwards to Python through the backend proxy with an internal caller class: to Python's own /mcp until GW-2 adds the loopback compatibility endpoint, and to that endpoint from GW-2 on, because the gateway owns the single policy pass (D26); an unknown tool falls to Proxy. gcore's ToolRegistry gains a composition rule: several family crates may contribute tools to one server, and only a duplicate tool name is rejected, which replaces ToolRegistry::new's DuplicateServer refusal (gcore mcp.rs:186-241) and lets the pilot's gobby-tasks tools go to Compare and then Native at the CP-TEMPLATE cutovers while the agents, plans and team tools on the same servers stay proxied. Compare reads run dual-leg and writes go to Python once. #24841 is the plan: map approval approves it as amended here against runner-first (the worker boundary replaces runner_backend.front_door_secret; amendments 2.1.8 and 2.1.9 fold into this brief), which settles its criterion 3. #24884's edge on #24151 narrows to GW-2's preflight worker op (s2-11:264). #24884's edge on #21566 is cut: MUX-1 reaches this chunk through GW-2 and lands after it (D26), so GW-1 resolves an external server's tools to Proxy like any other tool and builds only the parts of #24884's multiplexer criteria that need no Backend. It builds the native cancel route (#24884's 2.1.9; .gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md 2.2): POST /api/mcp/tools/cancel {call_id}, which admits the callers POST /api/mcp/tools/call admits and takes the caller's session from the front door's identity, where call_id is the x-gobby-call-id header gmcp sent on that call (MCP-CRATE). A caller-scoped registry holds the calls that reach Backend, so it stays empty until MUX-1 binds it. A registered call answers {cancelled:true}. Any other id leaves a tombstone in the caller's scope (kept 600 seconds, at most 4,096, oldest evicted first) and answers {cancelled:false}, so another session's cancel leaves a call running, and a late or duplicate cancel changes nothing. The call entry checks the caller's tombstones before it dispatches on any backend, and a hit answers the ordinary failure payload with error_code CANCELLED and dispatches nothing. A call already running on Native or Proxy is never interrupted, so until CP-WAVE5-CUT an in-flight external call runs to its own end. What needs Backend is MUX-1's: external dispatch behind the same policy pass (2.1.6), and forwarding an external cancel, the external tool-inventory cache, the passive GET /api/mcp/tools read and the external schema_hash (2.1.9), with their two tests. The gateway also keeps Python's per-call metrics (the MCP metrics of the multiplexer plan's Decision 3), which OBS's gobby-metrics tools read: a call it dispatches to a Native handler, and from CP-WAVE5-CUT to Backend, writes the tool_metrics aggregate and the tool_call event that MetricsManager.record_call writes (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/metrics.py:54-96; Python's two call sites are src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:650-672 and src/gobby/mcp_proxy/client_manager/invocation.py:121-136). A Proxy call and Compare's Python leg are recorded by Python's dispatch behind the compatibility endpoint, and Compare's native leg records nothing, so each call counts once. The gateway classifies tool results with a native port of src/gobby/hooks/tool_outcomes.py, whole, at crates/gcore/src/tool_outcomes.rs (normalize_tool_outcome, classify_raw_tool_result, tool_outcome_from_data and hook_event_tool_outcome; the Python module imports only the standard library), because its /mcp and REST answers read classify_raw_tool_result from CP-MCP-CUT, before RULE-N2 and HOOK-2 land; both reuse this port (D99). Its /mcp call_tool keeps GobbyDaemonTools.call_tool's behaviours (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:234-387): canonicalize_call_tool_wrapper's refusals as is_error results, the caller-session refusal, the client guard, the wait heartbeat with its timeout cap (crates/gmcp/src/call_tool.rs is the Rust reference for the cap), the failure flattening and the stripped success field. A result under enforcement whose error_code is INVALID_ARGUMENTS and that carries a schema appends that tool to the unlocked_tools session variable, on every backend (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:223-234; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/schema_guidance.py:44-65). ToolProxyService's tool filter has no production setter (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_proxy.py:75-93; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:123-130), so its branches (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:478-480; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_discovery.py:44-57, 103-105) are debt and are not ported. A Native handler that fails with an error answers the payload of Python's except path (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:743-809), with fallback_suggestions [] until MCP-FLIP binds the native resolver, and on a Compare leg that field is triaged as an accepted contract change until then (D17). A failure payload a handler returns carries no such field, and a Proxy failure carries Python's own. Output repair, the after phase, result offload and the outcome tracker (D99) stay in Python's own /mcp path while this chunk's Proxy forwards there; GW-2 builds them at the gateway when it moves Proxy to the compatibility endpoint, so this chunk leaves one hook point after dispatch on every backend. The caller-session refusal treats daemon-owned execution as speaking for its caller (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:471-490). The /mcp mount keeps Python's transport guards, which Python gets from the MCP SDK and a native mount must build, because replay sends no attack (src/gobby/servers/app_factory.py:100-136, 160; docs/guides/configuration.md:351-358, 395-417; D124). Bearer auth runs first. On a loopback bind the Host must match a loopback host or an mcp_allowed_hosts entry, its port wildcard form included, else 421, and an Origin, when sent, must match a loopback origin or a configured host's https origin, else 403; off loopback neither check runs. A POST needs a JSON Content-Type, else 400, and a body over the SDK's 4 MiB limit gets 413 (mcp.server.transport_security). While MCP exposure is on, the admitted hosts add this node's Tailscale name, with its port unless that is 443, read when the listener starts, never persisted, and left out with a warning when Tailscale cannot answer. These keys need a restart (src/gobby/config/registry.py:619, 626), so the family reads them once at start through FamilyContext's config epoch. The Tailscale read (src/gobby/ui_exposure.py:217) goes in gobby-core, which V1A's exposure reconcile and V1B's ui verbs reuse.
chunks.oracle: REC-PILOT's gateway cases and the existing gmcp wire contracts (crates/gmcp/contracts, including unicode_name_aliases.v16.json), replayed differentially with every tool on Proxy, then with fixture tools registered Native by a test family. The multiplexer plan's 2.2.4 gateway orderings on each backend: a cancel before the call's POST and a cancel while the gateway resolves the call's context each end the call CANCELLED with nothing dispatched; a cancel before an internal call starts skips it, while one already running completes; a late or duplicate cancel changes nothing; and another session's cancel returns {cancelled:false}. A Native call adds one tool_metrics count, and a Proxy or Compare call adds one through Python's dispatch, never two. The vectors of src/gobby/hooks/tool_outcomes.py in tests/contracts/rules/normalize_vectors.json, which P0-DECISIONS writes, replay equal through crates/gcore/src/tool_outcomes.rs.
