REC-PILOT's completion cases replay here only on Proxy, through Python's own /mcp, because this chunk builds no completion pipeline (see its goal). tests/servers/test_mcp_allowed_hosts.py and tests/servers/test_mcp_admitted_hosts.py replay natively on /mcp: an unlisted Host with a bearer gets 421, a listed one without a bearer gets 401, an empty list keeps loopback and refuses a tailnet Host, a port wildcard accepts any port, a configured host's Origin must be its https origin, and exposure admits only the node's name. A body over 4 MiB gets 413 and a POST without a JSON Content-Type gets 400.

chunks.title: GW-2: REST tool routes, per-tool Compare and the preflight worker op
chunks.goal: #24885: the REST tool routes (/api/mcp/tools, /api/mcp/tools/call and /schema, /api/mcp/{server_name}/tools and the per-tool POST) on GW-1's dispatcher; the Python compatibility backend per tool: a dormant, loopback-only, secret-bound Python endpoint that dispatches each Proxy tool against Python with no policy pass (docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md:82, 86-88; D26), to which GW-1's Proxy backend then forwards; per-tool Compare for Native tools; and the preflight rule pass through an allow-listed worker op into Python's rule engine, run by the gateway for every tool, Native, Compare or Proxy, whenever it serves /mcp, and kept until HOOK-3's joint flip (D27). Acceptance 2.2.5 runs here on the Stage 1 pair fixture (tests/e2e/test_hub_node_pair.py:253, hub-only placement), not on Stage 4 machinery. #25283 (gobby-results, in MCP-FLIP) waits on this chunk, not only on #24884. Compare's Python leg goes to the compatibility endpoint, as Proxy does. The gateway runs the preflight op once per call, before either leg, and the native leg runs no pass of its own. The preflight op also carries the after phase (D82): the gateway calls it once more after a dispatched call completes, with the completed result, and a shim in R0's worker package rebuilds the completion event from the fields the before call returned and runs apply_after_tool_workflow (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/result_handling.py:234-287), so the gateway's single policy pass is a before pass and an after pass on every backend (docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md:69-71). An after-phase failure records diagnostics and returns the handler's result unchanged, with no redispatch. The REST call routes run the pass only where Python's route enforces it, on a wrapper-marked request or an agent token (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/execution.py:50-57, 271, 434, 627, 753), so an operator-credential call with no wrapper marker runs no pass, which HOOK-3's in-process dispatch relies on (s2-11 7.7). The compatibility endpoint answers for every tool on Proxy, not only Python's internal registries, because MUX-1 lands after this chunk and every external server stays on Proxy until CP-WAVE5-CUT. Its list, schema and call go through the service's existing dispatch (_execute_tool, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:677-735; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_discovery.py:51, 154), which runs no rule pass (the service's call path runs it around that dispatch, :430, :619) and reaches an external server through Python's MCPClientManager with Python's own secret resolution, OAuth, browser policy, untrusted-value cleaning and per-call metrics. The gobby namespace's Python tools (GobbyDaemonTools, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:49, 758) answer on the same endpoint until their chunks flip (MUX-2, RULE-2, OBS and MCP-FLIP). It still runs no policy pass and exposes no external configuration route. This amends #24885's plan (.gobby/plans/rust-internal-mcp-servers.md 2.2 and its 2.2.1, which resolve only an internal registry), and this chunk updates docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md:82-88 to match (D26). It also builds the pipeline that completes a gateway-served call as Python's call path does (D99; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:609-634, 223-244): dispatch, output repair, the after phase with the tracker in the same op, then result offload, on GW-1's hook point. This chunk records that order beside the policy pass in docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md. Repair: the compatibility endpoint calls the existing maybe_repair_output (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/output_repair.py:742-768) on _execute_tool's result, so a Proxy call and Compare's Python leg answer repaired and the after phase reads what Python's reads; D101 settles who repairs after CP-WAVE5-CUT. The endpoint serializes a CallToolResult with model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True) and its answer marks it as one, because the REST routes' failure shape (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/execution.py:161-170), GW-1's failure flattening (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:358) and the offloader's serialization (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/result_offload.py:365-390) branch on that type; the shim revalidates a marked result before the after pass and the tracker read it. Offload: this chunk ports the write path natively (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/result_offload.py:60-361, 370-390 and the helpers they call; ToolResultStore.save and _chunk_content, src/gobby/storage/tool_results.py:56-110, 220-258), with the exempt patterns, the gobby-sessions get_handoff exemption, the thresholds, the too-large and store-failure envelopes and the BM25 intent matches on tool_result_chunks (crates/gcore/src/search.rs::sanitize_pg_search_query over the hub pool, as crates/gcode/src/search/fts/content.rs queries, with no new crate). It reads the live tool_result_offload.* keys per call through gcore's ConfigSource (crates/gcore/src/config/resolve.rs:98-109), with the defaults in crates/gcore/assets/config/runtime_config_contract.json. It runs on /mcp's call_tool and on both REST call routes, with or without a wrapper marker, because Python passes wrapper_originated true on all three (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:333; src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/execution.py:657, 765), on every backend, after the after phase, and on Compare only on the answer served. A body offload false on POST /api/mcp/tools/call (:593-598) and X-Gobby-CLI-Internal: 1 with no wrapper marker on the per-tool POST (:748-750, 769) skip it, and a caller that reaches GW-1's routing in process, such as PIPE-2's MCP steps, never offloads, as Python's in-process calls never do (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:633). The rows stay shared (D19): Python's gobby-results pages them until MCP-FLIP ports the paging, and Python's op cleans them until CP-WAVE5-CUT. Error text: this chunk ports src/gobby/hooks/tool_error_tracker.py:74-160 and 240-305 (sanitize_record_text, render_bounded_identity, _bounded_identity, _canonical_json, extract_error_snippet and their private helpers) to crates/gcore/src/tool_error_text.rs, which the REST failure shape and the offload envelopes use and RULE-1H, SES-3B and HOOK-2 reuse. The external server pool (MUX-1 and MUX-2) and the removal of Python's MCP backend (MCP-FLIP) go live at CP-WAVE5: the pool is single-owner state that moves only after its last Python callers (rule preflight, pipelines, hooks) are native, and the flip needs every internal server native. Packet: GW-1's and GW-2's validation: REC-PILOT's gateway and REST tool cases and the gmcp wire contracts replayed with every tool on Proxy, then with fixture tools Native through a test family, with one case per backend (Proxy, Native and Compare) asserting that exactly one policy pass runs, in the gateway; the dormancy proof; R-RETIRE's landing; CP-RUNNER-CUT's window record. On no-go, after the de-escalation, send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight gateway and pilot chunks (PROJ-1, SEAM-CALLERS, SEAM-WS, GW-1, GW-2, A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG, A1-SECRETS, B0-READ, B0-WRITE and B0-CLOSE): they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until the fixes Josh names close. When those fixes close, the session Josh opens for this review sends a second one that releases them, before it builds its new packet. The packet also carries GW-2's after-phase cases (D82): on every backend the after phase runs exactly once after each dispatched call, and an after-phase failure keeps the handler's result. The packet also carries GW-2's Proxy cases for an external fixture server and a gobby-namespace tool (D26) and GW-1's cancel orderings. The packet also carries GW-2's completion cases (D99): offload envelopes and the rows Python's gobby-results pages, a repaired openapi result on Proxy, the open_tool_errors and unlocked_tools deltas and the REST shape of a failed external result. It states the accepted difference that Python's /api/metrics stays flat for gateway-served REST calls until OBS at CP-WAVE1-CUT. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-MCP-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build serves REC-PILOT's gateway and REST tool cases through gmcp from every CLI's MCP config. The restored generation proxies /mcp again, and Python's proxy reads back the schema lease rows the gateway wrote. (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The gateway family's compiled default flips from Proxy to Native for /mcp and the REST tool routes. Every tool's compiled per-tool default stays Proxy, and Proxy now forwards to GW-2's loopback compatibility endpoint, which dispatches each Proxy tool against Python with no policy pass (D26). The gateway runs the single policy pass for every tool through GW-2's preflight worker op, as the contract requires (docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md:82, 86-88). gmcp's code is unchanged, because it executes nothing itself (crates/gmcp/README.md:1-9). The op's after phase runs once after each dispatched call (D82). Proxy covers external servers too: until CP-WAVE5-CUT the endpoint dispatches their tools to Python's MCPClientManager, and until their chunks flip it dispatches the gobby namespace's Python tools (GW-2, D26). GW-1's cancel route serves from this activation and interrupts nothing yet, because only a call that reaches MUX-1's Backend registers. (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours. Triggers: health or start proof failure; an error rate above baseline; an MCP call from any of the five CLIs failing through gmcp; a tool call that skips the policy pass or runs it twice; a schema lease mismatch between the gateway and Python; discovery output (list_tools, get_tool_schema) that differs from the recorded cases. One more trigger: a call, tool list or schema read on an external server that fails through the compatibility endpoint or differs from the recorded cases. One more trigger (D99): a large tool result returned whole, an offload envelope that gobby-results cannot page, or a proxied failure that opens no open_tool_errors record or a proxied success that resolves none. (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with the tag merged into 0.9.0-gg in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. After a stamped-set restore, the code-index gateway refuses the restored gcode until the deactivation build is promoted, because that gcode is below the checkout's gcode pin (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5). chunks.title: A1-RUNTIME: runtime handshake and managed principals (#21559 P4)
chunks.goal: Josh's A1, first part (#25341 D1; D25). #21559 P4 (#24439) in the existing runtime family crate (crates/gruntime): the managed challenge route (#24453), credential issuance (#24454), rotation with the grant.json rewrite (#24455), the native managed handshake (#24456), grant presentation (#24457) and GET /api/runtime/config. #24456 follows Python's current in-request retry (0.25/0.5/1.0 s delays; a lost race reuses the competing successor; runner_init/servers.py:427-488, 047fa598a7), not the leaf's credential_issuance_failed. #24453-#24455 are re-verified against the P4 Python drift since the plan stamp (#24816, #24675, #25264; +129/-28). D12 and ruling 16: materialize_managed_launch becomes a gruntime service, and rotate_due's native iteration is written and registered here on R4's scheduler, active only once the runtime family is (CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT). Capability-token verification (#24452) is built earlier, in SEAM-CALLERS. The family claims only the paths it implements: A1-RUNTIME claims /api/runtime, A1-CONFIG and A1-SECRETS extend the claim, and A1-SECRETS lands the family's default flip dormant for CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT to activate. This chunk also carries #25068 (closed as superseded by this chunk's task, D31), which moved here because #24457 blocks it and this chunk depends on SEAM-CALLERS. SEAM-CALLERS lands the leaf's agent-token class. This chunk adds its runtime-grant class to #25046's admission type: a grant that meets the route's RequiredCapability as Python's _GRANT_ROUTES declares it (src/gobby/servers/grant_auth.py:85-171: mode=daemon on the compute routes, a bare capability name on the status routes, a broker operation on the code-index routes), through #24452's token verification and #24457's managed grant presentation, with no second verifier. A missing, insufficient, revoked or wrong-mode grant is Rejected, and unavailable authority is a typed 503. Each family declares its own route's capability and binds the class at its own activation: AI-1B (#25106), VOICE and CIX-1 for their grant routes, and code-index 1.9's grant checks converge on it. The table's POST /api/admin/savings/record entry (:170) has no route and no ledger row, so nothing binds it. #25264's renewal is this chunk's too, though its leaf and plan name neither it nor the notice: an expired seat's POST to the handshake passes only on a validly signed expired token with an agent_run_id, a live run and a matching identity, and the grant it renews has no token_exp (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:316-322, 507-535; src/gobby/servers/routes/runtime_handshake.py:183-186; src/gobby/runtime_grants/handshake.py:154-178). When a renewal fails with credential_issuance_failed, the route still answers Python's 403 (src/gobby/servers/routes/runtime_handshake.py:130-139, 234-235) and, when the run has a parent, writes one agent_recovery row for that parent: event capability_expired, the token's exp as dedupe_key, Python's text and its deterministic id under ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (src/gobby/servers/routes/runtime_handshake.py:99-127; src/gobby/agents/resume_finalization.py:144-199). No run or no parent means no row, and a failed write is logged and never changes the answer. The notice has no wake and takes no lock, so it is a shared-row write under D19 and needs no worker op: gruntime declares a one-method notice port with an interim adapter that writes that row, until AG-3's agent_recovery writer replaces the adapter in CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation commit (D29).
engines: managed principals and the runtime handshake
chunks.oracle: REC-PILOT's runtime cases (recorded with the pilot corpus) and the grant and secret-seal golden vectors; differential replay asserts DB deltas and grant.json deltas on a temp HOME. #25068's runtime-grant class replays REC-PILOT's grant cases and compares each outcome with Python's middleware (src/gobby/servers/grant_auth.py:180-233), and its tests refuse a missing, insufficient, revoked or wrong-mode grant. Renewal and notice cases are recorded here from Python before the port (tests/servers/routes/test_runtime_handshake_renewal.py:151, 240, 288): a renewal issued, an expired token refused, one credential_issuance_failed 403 with one agent_recovery row byte-equal to Python's, id and metadata_json included, a repeat for the same exp adding none, a run with no parent adding none, and a failed write leaving the 403 unchanged.
chunks.size: M, 2 checkpoints (challenge, issuance and rotation; handshake, presentation, materialize_managed_launch and #25068's runtime-grant class). Python in scope: runtime_grants 1.3K, managed credentials and handshake ~2.5K, runner_init managed issue ~0.6K; Rust ~3K in gruntime. Renewal and the notice add about 0.2K.
chunks.registration: Extends crates/gruntime and its existing family entry; rotate_due registers on R4's job registry from this chunk; no serve.rs edits. #25068's class extends #25046's crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/admission.rs and adds no route, family line or default: it goes live with each family that binds it (D37). The notice port takes its interim adapter in the same family entry, and CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation commit re-binds it to AG-3's writer.
chunks.risks: Python's runner init reads managed credentials in-process: Rust rotation keeps grant.json's format and the reload signal Python listens for. Secrets use temp keys only. #25068's security review splits with its classes: this chunk's review approves the exact SHA of the runtime-grant class, and SEAM-CALLERS' review approved the agent-token class before CP-MCP-CUT could make it live. That review is D106's security-auditor seat on the exact candidate SHA, and this chunk is a gated chunk under D106.

chunks.title: A1-CONFIG: config model, reads and writes (#21559 P5a)
chunks.goal: Josh's A1, second part. #21559 P5 config routes (#24440): GET /api/config/schema (#24458), the active-state reads of values, UI settings and global tool approvals (#24463), GET /api/config/effective, YAML template read and export (#24462), per-key and complete-candidate validation (#24464, #24465), PATCH /api/config/values (#24466), YAML 1.2 reading in Rust (#24468), and PUT /api/config/template with POST /api/config/import (#24469). DaemonConfig's model moves to gcore::config under SEAM-FAMILY's config epoch, and every write publishes a new epoch that R2's worker reconciliation applies to Python. The brief starts from today's counts: 84 validator decorators, not the plan's 78 (new: validate_accept_band, validate_api_base, validate_decisions, validate_mcp_allowed_hosts, two app.py model validators, validate_roots), and a schema contract of 465 exact keys (463 public, 2 machine) plus 11 patterns, 474 properties. For #24468, crates/gruntime/src/yaml.rs reads the YAML documents that PUT /api/config/template and POST /api/config/import receive as YAML 1.2 core, and crates/gruntime/src/pyyaml.rs keeps an exported string plain only when PyYAML's 1.1 resolver and the 1.2 reader both read it as a string, so every Rust export reads back unchanged through yaml.safe_load. The plan's Python Yaml12Loader and Yaml12SafeDumper (gdaemon-runtime-family plan 5.11) are not built (D4), so Python's YAML 1.1 readings of imported documents, and its plain export of 0o17, 1e5, 1.5e5, 1E+5 and .5e3, which the 1.2 reader reads as numbers, are D18 known-bad rows. #24466's 5.9.10 (one project-scoped secrets set) is met in MUX-1, whose multiplexer-plan 1.4 absorbs the secrets set this chunk lands into SecretStore::set_in. Nothing publishes config_active_state once commit A stops Python's ConfigRuntime, and that row is what every native read serves (crates/gruntime/src/config.rs:61; crates/gruntime/src/grant.rs:68-84; crates/gruntime/src/handshake.rs:95-98; crates/gruntime/src/verify.rs:60-66; src/gobby/config/runtime_active_state.py:53-75). An existing hub would keep a frozen row, so every PATCH /api/config/values would commit and then answer reconcile_failed after 65 seconds, and a fresh hub would have no row, so GET /api/config/effective and GET /api/runtime/config would answer 503 and the managed handshake would refuse. So this chunk builds a native publisher on a hub, behind gdaemon's compiled backend default and dormant while that default starts the worker, and commit A activates it with no code of its own. It reads config_store and config_state, builds the same document (src/gobby/config/runtime_active_state.py:15-50), with secret bindings sealed under Python's associated data (crates/gruntime/src/secrets.rs:123), and upserts the same row: first at start before any door admits, as ConfigRuntime.start publishes before ready (src/gobby/config/runtime.py:176-219), then on each native write's commit, on gobby_config_changed and on a 30-second poll that retries a failed upsert (src/gobby/config/runtime.py:806-865). Before its first publish it does reconcile_registry's work, as src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:233 does before ConfigRuntime starts: it deletes stored rows of removed config, repairs each row's is_secret from the contract and refuses a residual key (src/gobby/storage/config_repository.py:175-202; src/gobby/config/registry.py:612). Each failure is a fatal start hook error with Python's message: a residual key, which a relaunch would not clear, takes R2's refused state, and a failed first publish ends the start nonzero. Activation is per key from runtime_config_contract.json: a live key moves to active at once, a managed key through the port of managed_embedding_projection (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:246; src/gobby/config/runtime.py:727-733), and a restart_required key stays at its boot value and is listed in pending_restart_keys until the next start. Native has no prepare step, because a family reads a key per call or through FamilyContext's config epoch, so failed_live_keys stays empty, and each successor of a stateful subscriber (src/gobby/runner_init/config_subscribers.py:153-205) rebuilds when the epoch moves. Each published revision moves the epoch and goes out as config_event on the broker (src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:67-78; src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:300), which web/src/hooks/useConfiguration.ts listens for.
chunks.oracle: REC-PILOT's config cases (recorded with the pilot corpus; the #25599 start-gate fix makes config_values replay clean) and the checked-in runtime config contract (gcore/assets/config); differential replay asserts DB deltas and config-file deltas on a temp HOME. An accepted contract change named in this chunk's python_edits is recorded the same way: an entry and citation in a fixture copy, which the activation commit that flips the family lands (D84). Publisher vectors recorded from Python before the publisher commit: for a fixture store the native document equals Python's, sealed values compared by opening them. With the worker default off on an isolated hub, a stored row of a removed key goes at the first boot, a row whose is_secret disagrees with the contract is repaired, a residual key answers 503 backend_refused with Python's message until a full restart, a first boot with no row publishes before admission, GET /api/config/effective answers 200 and the managed handshake succeeds; a PATCH of a live key commits with no failed key and publishes config_event; and a PATCH of a restart_required key lists it in pending_restart_keys with its active value unchanged until the next start.
chunks.size: L, 3 checkpoints (model, schema and reads; validation; writes, template and import/export). Python in scope: config 12.7K (model and validators ~9K ported), config routes ~2.5K; Rust ~6K. The native publisher and the registry reconcile add about 0.5K of Rust.
chunks.python_edits: The port adds no Python of its own. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

Readiness treats this escalated task as open, so no wave 1 chunk starts until Josh's go closes it, and the template fan-out also waits for CP-TEMPLATE-CUT to close.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover 1 of 4: the pilot families go to Compare
chunks.goal: Category code. The first of the pilot's four cutovers: the runtime family (A1) and the tasks family go from Proxy to Compare, which is D13's live Compare day. Callers still get Python's answer (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:186-254), so this step changes what is observed, not what is served. Before step 1, this session copies the census, the project record and the split map that CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW wrote to the directory named in its packet attestation into its worktree, and lands them as a docs-only commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. The two pilot families touch no other datastore. (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. In Compare, Python performs every write, so the rehearsal proves that the restored generation serves REC-PILOT's corpus in Proxy on the same schema and that the compare log is the only new state. (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The runtime and tasks families' compiled defaults flip from Proxy to Compare, and so do the per-tool defaults of their tools (gobby-tasks, gobby-tasks-ops, gobby-config, gobby-hub:get_machine_id and gobby-hub:list_cross_project_tasks). (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: one full active day, from the promotion until the next quiet hours begin and at least 16 hours, so step 2 starts this cut soon after quiet hours end. Triggers: a compare class that the review did not classify (gdaemon compare-report exits 1 on any diff, native error or mismatch, crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:30-39); added latency on task reads above the bound in the window plan; a close or land_commit failure; a hook stop-gate decision that differs from the recorded envelopes; a tool call that skips the policy pass or runs it twice; health or start proof failure. (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with the tag merged into 0.9.0-gg in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). Here outcome 1 means the day's compare-report is clean, or every class is triaged as D17 requires. (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Otherwise restore the full set only when gcode or ghook itself broke, because gcode below the checkout floor breaks the code-index gateway (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796). After a stamped-set restore, the code-index gateway refuses the restored gcode until the deactivation build is promoted, because that gcode is below the checkout's gcode pin (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5). The restore burns the activated versions, never the restored target's own. Promote the deactivation build only as step 5 proved it: when a trigger implicates a dormant landing rather than this stage's defaults, stay on the restored generation with the pin and the hold extended, add a revert of that landing to the deactivation commit first, and rerun step 5's deactivation proof on the changed commit. Then give the prepared deactivation commit fresh version bumps, first rebasing it onto 0.9.0 HEAD if an outcome-2 fix or another landing has moved HEAD past the commit it was built on, because land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task (step 3), and every fix commit changes the version lines that this commit bumps. Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with the deactivation commit that A's rehearsal proved (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, which proxies both families. The restore members are gdaemon alone.
