chunks.risks: Compare runs both legs of every GET, which adds load and latency to every task read: the window measures it. Compare sends each write to Python once and runs check_proxied on it (#25520), so a Rust write defect shows only as far as check_proxied sees it; CP-TEMPLATE-WRITES-CUT has its own window for writes.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover 2 of 4: A1 goes live and the tasks reads go Native
chunks.goal: Category code. The second pilot cutover, and the point where A1 goes live: the runtime family serves every route it claims natively (A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG and A1-SECRETS), and A1-RUNTIME's rotate_due job replaces Python's one-iteration op on R4's scheduler. The tasks reads go Native too. #24474 (`runtime` defaults to native) is this activation commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. hub-backup archives none of ~/.gobby/bootstrap.yaml, the daemon config file and ~/.gobby/grant.json (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:432-513), and native config writes and grant rotation change them, so this session copies all three into the backup directory with mode 0600 and records their sha256 in a window-plan attestation that supersedes step 3's (supersedes_id). (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build replays REC-PILOT's runtime, config, secrets and read cases and runs one grant rotation, writing config, secret and grant rows and rewriting grant.json. The restored generation, with Python serving the runtime family again, reads them back and keeps rotating grants from the rewritten grant.json. (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The runtime family's compiled default flips from Compare to Native, and A1-RUNTIME's native rotate_due job registers (D12). The tasks family's default flips to Native with its claimed routes limited to the read routes, so its write, close and landing routes still reach Python (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:119-126). The read tools' per-tool defaults flip to Native, while the write, close and landing tools stay in Compare. A1-RUNTIME's renewal and its capability-expiry notice serve natively with the handshake, the notice through gruntime's port on its interim adapter. (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours. Triggers: a managed handshake, challenge or credential issuance failure; a grant rotation that fails or leaves grant.json unreadable to Python; a config read or write that differs from the recorded cases outside the classes D17's triage fixed, registered as known-bad or accepted (CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW's packet lists them); a config reload that Python misses; a tasks read that differs from Python's in ordering or pagination; health or start proof failure. Further triggers: a seat's renewal refused where Python would issue it; a capability_expired row missing or doubled. (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with the tag merged into 0.9.0-gg in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with the deactivation commit that A's rehearsal proved (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-TEMPLATE-CUT's last promotion, which carries its Compare defaults. The restore members are gdaemon alone. The rehearsal proved that it reads a grant.json rewritten in the window; if it does not, restore bootstrap.yaml, the config file and grant.json by hand from the step 4 copies, with the daemon stopped, and check their sha256.
chunks.oracle: CP-TEMPLATE-CUT's window record; REC-PILOT's runtime, config, secrets and read cases and the grant and secret-seal golden vectors on the release build; the window's trigger log.
chunks.size: M, 1 session plus an 8-hour window. Python in scope: 0; Rust edits: two family defaults, the tasks read claims, the rotate_due registration, per-tool defaults and version bumps.
chunks.registration: The activation commit: the runtime family default, the tasks family default with read-only claims, the rotate_due job registration, the read tools' per-tool defaults and the version bumps. It also carries the entries and case citations of the A1 accepted contract changes and the regenerated parity ledger (D84).
chunks.risks: Config and grants are files that Python also reads in-process: Rust writes keep their formats and emit the reload signal Python listens for (A1-CONFIG). Real secrets pass through Rust here for the first time, so the window watches handshake and rotation failures first.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover 3 of 4: the tasks writes go Native
chunks.goal: Category code. The third pilot cutover: the tasks writes, claims, dependencies and lifecycle go Native (B0-WRITE). (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. hub-backup does not archive the task JSONL backup (~/.gobby/backups/<project-uuid>/tasks.jsonl), which native backup_tasks writes, so this session copies it into the backup directory with mode 0600 and records its sha256 in a window-plan attestation that supersedes step 3's (supersedes_id). (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build replays REC-PILOT's write, claim and lifecycle cases with DB deltas, plus the claim and stop-gate hook envelopes. The restored generation, with Python writing tasks again, reads back the Rust-written task, claim, dependency, label, comment and attestation rows and accepts their pg_notify events. If B0-WRITE's prepared commit carries a migration, this is the first cutover with an expand step, and its rehearsal is SCHEMA-WINDOW's live drill: the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub. (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The tasks family's claimed routes grow to its write, release-claim, dependency and lifecycle routes, and those tools' per-tool defaults flip from Compare to Native. The close route keeps reaching Python, and the close and landing tools stay in Compare. The prepared commit that lands before it is B0-WRITE's, with its schema inputs (D22). POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/claim keeps proxying until AG-3 binds the native AssignmentNotifier at CP-WAVE2-CUT (tasks-family Q11); MCP claim_task, which sends no assignment notice, flips here with the other tools. It also binds gtasks' ClosurePolicy port to B0-CLOSE's interim adapter, because a native reparent or delete that leaves a parent with no open child closes it through the policy (B0-WRITE), so each such ancestor close gets its decision from Python's evaluate_closure_policy through the closure-policy worker op (D41). The bound policy lifts tasks-family 4.1's exclusion of POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/close, so this commit's claimed routes still leave that route out until CP-TEMPLATE-CLOSE-CUT. B0-WRITE's stale claim sweep registers on R4's registry in place of Python's op. (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours. Triggers: a write whose DB delta differs from Python's recorded delta; a claim, release or hand-off that leaves a task in a state Python's readers reject; a missed pg_notify or WS event that leaves a Python cache stale; a cycle check that differs; a task JSONL backup that Python cannot read; health or start proof failure. An ancestor auto-close after a reparent or delete that differs from Python's, or that stays open because the closure-policy worker op failed or timed out, is also a trigger (D41). Job triggers: a job this activation swapped in that misses its cadence, errors on every fire, or deletes or changes a row its Python op would keep. (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with the tag merged into 0.9.0-gg in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Otherwise restore the full set only when gcode or ghook itself broke, because gcode below the checkout floor breaks the code-index gateway (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796). After a stamped-set restore, the code-index gateway refuses the restored gcode until the deactivation build is promoted, because that gcode is below the checkout's gcode pin (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5). The restore burns the activated versions, never the restored target's own. Promote the deactivation build only as step 5 proved it: when a trigger implicates a dormant landing rather than this stage's defaults, stay on the restored generation with the pin and the hold extended, add a revert of that landing to the deactivation commit first, and rerun step 5's deactivation proof on the changed commit. Then give the prepared deactivation commit fresh version bumps, first rebasing it onto 0.9.0 HEAD if an outcome-2 fix or another landing has moved HEAD past the commit it was built on, because land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task (step 3), and every fix commit changes the version lines that this commit bumps. Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with the deactivation commit that A's rehearsal proved (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT's last promotion. The restore members are the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook (gobby rollback restore <generation> --bin gcode,gdaemon,ghook), because this cut's schema inputs change the identity that all three embed.
