chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover 4 of 4: close and landing go Native
chunks.goal: Category code. The last pilot cutover: close_task's gates, commit linking, attestations, land_commit and the landing freeze go Native (B0-CLOSE). It holds #25521: the native default for key callers and the coherent release, with its installed hashes and announcement (4.3.4). (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. This session also copies the landing freeze file under the git common dir (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_landing.py:35-72) into the backup directory and records its sha256 in a window-plan attestation that supersedes step 3's (supersedes_id), because hub-backup does not archive it, native set_landing_freeze writes it and the restored generation must read it. (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build replays REC-PILOT's close, commit-linking, attestation and land_commit cases on temp git repos, writing attestation and commit-link rows and the freeze file. The restored generation, with Python closing and landing again, reads back those rows. The rehearsal sets the freeze with the activated build and proves that the restored generation's land_commit refuses a non-owner with landing_frozen and admits the freeze's owner, then proves the reverse: a freeze the restored generation set binds the activated build the same way. (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The tasks family's claimed routes grow to POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/close, and the close, attestation, commit-link, land_commit and set_landing_freeze tools flip from Compare to Native, with #25521's native default for key callers. This commit switches the landing code itself, so after the restart the session confirms that the native land_commit still refuses a non-owner while the freeze is set and admits this task's session (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:653-655). Each native close and landing gets its policy decision through the interim adapter that CP-TEMPLATE-WRITES-CUT's activation commit bound: Python's evaluate_closure_policy, reached through the closure-policy worker op (D41). (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours, including one real close and one real landing through the native code by this cutover's own session under the freeze: a docs-only subtask of this cutover, created, landed and closed. Triggers: a close gate that passes or fails where Python's would not (integration ancestry, linked commits, uncommitted task-attributed files, validation evidence, criteria review); a land_commit that lands a commit Python would refuse, or refuses one Python would land; a freeze that is not honored; a stop-gate decision that differs from the recorded envelopes; health or start proof failure. A close or landing refused because the closure-policy worker op failed or timed out is also a trigger (D41). (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with the tag merged into 0.9.0-gg in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with the deactivation commit that A's rehearsal proved (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-TEMPLATE-WRITES-CUT's last promotion. The restore members are gdaemon alone. Restore it before anything else lands, because every later landing would run through the landing code under suspicion.

chunks.title: Terminal family: WS, inventory, viewports and operator input
chunks.goal: Wave 1 (the richest oracle in the tree). #23206 M2, landed dormant and activated at CP-WAVE1-CUT: the native terminal WS connection and operation state machine (#24577), terminal inventory reads and HTTP handlers (#24575), the attachment viewports that terminal_set_viewport writes in the Rust lease registry for its sizing, with no viewport route (#24576, below), the bounded proxy relay and frame and lifecycle fanout (#24578), operator input under the route action hold (#24579), and family registration and activation (#24580); the capture_output, send_keys and terminate_terminal descriptors. The gterm host manager and composer ledger stay the single Python owner until TERM-HOST: Rust reaches host effects (spawn, write, resize, capture, terminate) through allow-listed worker ops, so the Python write and runtime clients planned in #24571 and #24574 are not built. #25201 (D21): the Rust write path keeps hub-mode's remote write branch. #24576 closes as superseded by #24797 (the team-lane runbooks it served are retired), and #24577's edge on it is dropped. #24579's test target becomes a Rust test, because #24571's Python client is not built. #24580 runs after R6 (its 2.13.3 restart test) and claims its WS message types through SEAM-WS's registry. Its activation keeps gdaemon handing Python the terminal route value that keeps Python's host manager running (crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:160-169), because Python skips its host manager when that route is native (src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:64-72); only TERM-HOST's activation moves that value (D19). To keep it there, this chunk separates the two values that terminal_route() carries today (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:59-75): the terminal family's route backend, whose compiled default this chunk's activation flips at CP-WAVE1-CUT, and a terminal ownership default that feeds RouteLatch, the supervisor mode and GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE (crates/gterminals/src/family.rs:52-67; crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:160-169), which stays Proxy until TERM-HOST's activation. RouteLatch's registration check keys off the routes the family claims. It also lands one dormant Python helper that both of Python's terminal route reads use (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:83; src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:65-69): it returns GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE when gdaemon set it, and the bootstrap value (default proxy) otherwise, and the start refusal stays only for an explicit bootstrap terminal_ws entry that disagrees with the latched value (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:80-91). It is inert at landing, because gdaemon latches proxy and the bootstrap has no terminal_ws entry (D37). From then on Python follows the route gdaemon latches, so CP-WAVE5-CUT flips only gdaemon's compiled terminal ownership default and a gdaemon-alone restore hands the host back to Python in one restart. If Josh refuses this Python edit, CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation flips both Python reads with gdaemon's default, and its recipe lands the deactivation commit under the freeze, then restores the pinned generation, then promotes the deactivation build under the token (D19). #24573, the Rust runtime route, moved to TERM-HOST, because plan section 2.9 ties it to 2.8's single settler (#24572), which TERM-HOST builds. Its WS operator input (#24579) and its relay (#24578) report each admitted operator write and each output frame to one turn-observer trait in crates/gterminals, whose default does nothing, because Python's observer sees neither once this family is Native (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_input.py:21; src/gobby/servers/websocket/proxy_relay.py:469). AG-3's native observer binds it at CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation (D73). From CP-WAVE1-CUT to CP-WAVE2-CUT a mediated interrupt of an AGY session, the only provider that observer serves (src/gobby/sessions/terminal_turn_observer.py:23), does not end its turn until later evidence arrives, and CP-WAVE1-REVIEW's packet records that. From this chunk's activation Rust's lease registry owns attachments, holders, generations, viewports and write admission, while Python's host manager, composer ledger and write coordinator stay live, so Python's registry holds no WS attachment until CP-WAVE5-CUT. The family builds that registry whenever the terminal route backend is Native, whatever the ownership default says, because with_write_route builds Registry::new and its coordinator only in Owner mode today (crates/gterminals/src/family.rs:103-124); the loopback write route itself stays Owner-only. Its Coordinator takes a Runtime over D103's op in place of NativeWrite and TmuxWrite (:115-120) until TERM-HOST. Only the operator write needs that op: Python's coordinator refuses an operator origin its own registry cannot vouch for (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:575-580, 649-665) and returns at once for every other origin, so send_keys and the other host effects call their one-line ops directly and never pass the native Coordinator, which leaves Python's latch and quarantine as the only ones. The spawn op is a one-line registration on spawn_web_terminal (src/gobby/terminals/web_spawn.py:73) with the worker's terminal manager and resolved runtime; it serves terminal_create and TERM-2's pane spawns (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_create.py:48-127; src/gobby/terminals/workspace_ops.py:811). The native registry keeps the holder's focus flag with Python's rules (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:149-150, 481-496), and D105's op keeps Python's wake reading it. Input grants do not go through Python: the grant is host state that Python holds no copy of (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:696-718), and the host authenticates each control connection (crates/gterminal/src/host/control.rs:171-181). So ws.rs is the applier plan 2.2 describes (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md:2374-2385), and because 2.8 (#24572) moved to TERM-HOST this chunk also builds the ControlClient::revoke_input that 2.2 takes from it, against crates/gterminal/tests/fixtures/wire_golden/control_revoke_input.json. #24892 came after the plan, so 2.2's line that leases.rs needs no edit no longer holds. terminal_take_control carries an optional host_attachment_id, and a value that is not a positive 64-bit integer answers invalid_host_attachment_id (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_control.py:62-82). The native registry, which has no such field yet, keeps it on the attachment as Python's does (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:148, 519-540), and the applier sends it in grant_input as crates/gterminal/tests/fixtures/wire_golden/control_grant_input.json does. A direct holder with no such id gets a revoke and no grant, and a failed grant also revokes (src/gobby/terminals/input_grants.py:81-112). A failed grant or revoke leaves the handoff record for Python's expiry pass (src/gobby/terminals/input_grants.py:150-165) until TERM-HOST's. There is one lifecycle sequencer, the family registry. gclient drops a terminal_event from another epoch until its next roster read, and a workspace_event from another epoch with no re-read at all (crates/gclient/src/app/live.rs:301-310; crates/gclient/src/app/workspace_ops.rs:54-60), and Python stamps its own epoch and sequence until CP-WAVE5-CUT (src/gobby/runner_broadcasting.py:97-106; src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:469, 582). So while the family is Native the native publish path (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/publish.rs:82-133) re-stamps each terminal_event and workspace_event frame Python publishes with the registry's epoch and next sequence, and sends it through the same ordered queue as the family's own lifecycle events (crates/gterminals/src/leases.rs:421-453), because gclient drops a sequence at or below its pin (crates/gclient/src/app/live.rs:471-475). A large workspace_event arrives as terminal_ws_fragment frames (src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:471-484), so the path reassembles it, stamps it and fragments it again with the new sequence as message_seq (crates/gterminals/src/ws_protocol.rs:202). That path is a project_policy.security_paths entry, so this chunk's landing needs D106's seat. #25201 has two parts. Until TERM-HOST, D103's op carries node terminals as it carries local ones, so Python's _dispatch keeps the branch, its refusals and its ledger record (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:759-767, 801-802). For TERM-HOST's activation this chunk builds the Rust branch, dormant because it serves only Owner mode: before the Coordinator resolves a backend's runtime (crates/gterminals/src/write.rs:382), a terminal whose machine_id is another machine goes to a node runtime over a port this crate declares and crates/gdaemon binds to the node registry's command sender (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/registry.rs:230), with Python's refusals, ledger record, terminal.write payload and stage mapping (src/gobby/hub/remote_terminal.py:23-38; docs/contracts/node-commands.md:219), so such a write never reaches a local runtime. Two Python gates also came after the terminal plan (#24273, #24908) and move here, because a claimed frame no longer reaches Python's message gate (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:499-513) and a worker op binds no caller, so Python's ownership check passes there (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:837-850; src/gobby/hub/caller_scope.py:54-70). The WS connection takes its caller and any browser claims from SEAM-CALLERS's Admitted value at the upgrade (#25046; crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:220-240), because the bridge's ready frame carries only admitted and confined (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/transport.rs:115-128), and that caller fills each Requester (crates/gterminals/src/leases.rs:79-84). A break-glass connection, which Python leaves unbound, takes the nil caller and no ownership check. The first gate is confinement. It sits in SEAM-WS's registry dispatch (D102), so this chunk, TERM-2 and every later claimer (SES-2, CHAT-2, VOICE and MUX-1) pass it: on a confined connection a claimed frame whose type is off Python's allow-list, or whose project or session selector at any depth differs from the signed claims, answers Browser message refused and reaches no handler (src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:90-124). A confined terminal_list lists the claim's project alone, with no client project_id and no global project (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws.py:402-407, 431-433). The second gate is machine ownership, with Python's rule that a bound caller with no user owns nothing. terminal_attach checks the row's machine once and refuses with Python's machine_not_owned, machine_not_found and machine_ownership_unavailable (:231-250), terminal_list answers an empty page (:421-429), and a bound caller's send_keys checks the terminal's machine before its write op call and answers as Python's refused write does (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:220-228; src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:792-834). D103's operator write takes no check, because its attachment vouches for it as Python's lease does (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:769-790), and capture_output and terminate_terminal have none in Python. #25338 also came after the plan. send_keys passes a target gate before its write: it refuses a bare shell, a process that is no agent CLI, a composer that is not idle, a credential prompt and an unreadable pane, failing closed, and drains a held composer for a clear key (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:169-275). The gate reads the composer ledger, the detection registry and a pane snapshot, which stay Python's until TERM-HOST. So the native send_keys makes Python's first checks itself (the idempotency key, the caller and target, the speed command; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:279-301), calls a one-line op on send_keys_target_refusal, bound to the worker's terminal manager and runtime registry (D4), answers its refusal or cleared result as _deliver does (:164-179), and only then makes its ownership check and write op call. A failed call or a lost reply answers send_keys_target_unconfirmed with no write, as the gate fails closed (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:271-274). send_wake (#25720) came after this map's ledger, so the cut's regenerated ledger adds its row, which this chunk's selector already names. It types one fixed line and takes the same gate and write with no clear key, after its caller and target checks and the target's message_sender_capabilities admission, which it asks through a one-line op on recipient_policy, bound to the worker's database (D4), until CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation commit re-binds it to AG-3's native admission, refusing a withheld target as Python does (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:53-113, 130-142, 324-343; src/gobby/agents/team_communications.py:77). The write op's reply reads Delivered, Suppressed or AutomaticWriteQuarantined by its _type, and IndeterminateWrite as an unknown outcome that is never retried, as D103 reads a lost reply (src/gobby/terminals/runtime.py:137-142, 168).

Worker-op calls are asserted in the corpus as side effects, so the later host switch can replay the same cases against the native host. A fixture observer sees each admitted write once with its outcome and sequence, and each output frame in order, and a refused write reports its refusal. E1 gates 7 and 8 of .gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md (:2748-2757) run over this chunk's commits. A git diff audit: no change under crates/gterminal/; no production change under crates/gclient/src/, with crates/gclient/tests/client_loop.rs the only gclient edit; no change under tests/fixtures/terminal_ws_golden/; no protocol change; no production backend-authoring field; every terminal inventory producer emits backend. A bounded source-agnostic audit of backend selection and inventory consumers: every producer, special value, error subtype, failure boundary and display consumer the plan names has a passing test, and no separately invoked hook leaves a process, pending or live row, lease or lifecycle publication without its paired settlement. D103: a native WS operator write asserts the op call as a recorded side effect, unlatched and with origin operator, and a fixture worker answering an unavailable runtime, a stage none refusal, a partial delivery and a lost reply gets refused runtime_unavailable, refused held, indeterminate_partial_delivered:<bytes> and indeterminate_backend (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_write.py:174-195). chunks.title: Workspaces: WS rows and WorkspaceOps
chunks.goal: #25263: the workspace WS rows and the WorkspaceOps service natively, and the gobby-workspaces descriptors, over TERM-1's terminal family. Workspace operations that touch panes go through TERM-1's host worker ops until TERM-HOST. Python keeps reserving panes after this chunk's activation, for a placed spawn until CP-WAVE2-CUT and for a relaunch until CP-WAVE5-CUT, and its in-flight set and in-doubt registry are single-owner live state (D19): it marks a pane before it inserts the row and holds the mark until settle (src/gobby/terminals/workspace_agent_panes.py:364, 511-531, 657-659; src/gobby/storage/workspaces.py:345; src/gobby/terminals/in_doubt.py:116). So native WorkspaceOps treats a pane as in flight when its own set or Python's holds it, through this chunk's two worker ops (D4). The sweep selects its candidates under its row locks, as Python does (src/gobby/storage/workspaces.py:889-955), calls workspace_spawns_in_flight once with its NULL-terminal candidates, and then deletes with the liveness re-check, so a read with no such candidate makes no hop, and a pane Python marked cannot be missed, because the mark precedes the insert. Each refuse_in_flight guard (close, close_tab, move_tab, remove_pane, move_pane, swap_panes and rebalance_tab; :957-986) calls both ops once with the panes and bound terminals it locked, and the busy or not_found answer for a pane with no terminal reads the first op (src/gobby/terminals/workspace_ops.py:915-931). Each call has a 2-second bound, because it runs under row locks that Python's reserve can wait on, though the op itself needs none of them. On a failed or timed-out call the sweep keeps every NULL-terminal candidate for that read while a dead bound pane still goes, and a guard answers busy, so a lost reply removes nothing. Its types pass SEAM-WS's confinement gate: on a confined connection workspace_op answers Browser message refused, and workspace_attach and workspace_snapshot pass with selectors that match the claims (src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:90-124).
chunks.oracle: gclient workspace wire contracts plus REC-PLATFORM's workspace cases, replayed differentially. A fixture worker answers for the native sweep: a NULL-terminal pane the op reports in flight survives the read, one it does not report is swept as Python sweeps an unmarked NULL pane (tests/storage/test_workspaces.py:356), a failed call or a call past its 2-second bound keeps every NULL-terminal candidate while a dead bound pane still goes, and a read with no NULL-terminal candidate makes no call. A guarded mutation answers busy for a pane the first op reports, for a terminal the second op reports and on a failed call. On a confined connection workspace_op is refused with no write, and workspace_attach and workspace_snapshot answer only with matching selectors.

chunks.risks: gclient is the main consumer and is also Rust: its contract tests run against both backends. Python's own sweep still cannot see a native reservation, because Python never calls Rust (D19). After this cut its only in-process sweeps are the cold start's read and split (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/admin_cold_start.py:153, 170), until AG-5 ports it. chunks.title: Templates: single loader, DB sync and definition registries
chunks.goal: Wave 2 opener (D15). A gobby-assets crate embeds src/gobby/install/shared at build time (build.rs include_bytes!, no new dependency); its source path moves to assets/shared at S3-DELETE. TPL becomes the single loader and DB-sync owner of bundled templates (rules, pipelines, variables, agent definitions, prompts), replacing the workflows sync_rules, sync_pipelines and sync_variables, sync_registry.py and the prompts loader; SKILLS consumes the same loader for bundled skills (#24999). R2's content phase calls the native sync and, once CP-WAVE1-CUT activates it, sends the worker's startup_content phase with sync_bundled false, so Python's bundled sync stops while the rest of that phase runs (D83). Also owns the agent-definition registry surfaces (/api/agents/definitions and the agent-definition tools) and the generic test style of AGENTS rule 16: every bundled YAML gets syntax validation plus an engine dry run, with synthetic definitions for behavior. The bundled-skills asset script #24999 planned (scripts/build_bundled_skills_asset.py, not in the tree) is not built: gobby-assets embeds the skills with every other template (D15). TPL also ports the bundled agent-definition validity checks (AgentDefinitionBody plus gobby agents check) to Rust. It declares the template tree as gobby-assets' embedded input ([package.metadata.gobby] embedded = ['src/gobby/install/shared'] in its Cargo.toml), which GEN-ROLLBACK's release fingerprint reads, so from this landing on every template edit changes gdaemon's release identity, bumps gdaemon under the version rule and is a prepared commit, which the next checkpoint cut lands in its step 6 and promotes with its activation (D39). gdaemon's embedded copy then equals the checkout at every promoted commit, so Python's gobby sync and the native sync write the same rows. Its native rule sync ports normalize_rule_yaml_entry and prepare_rule_definition_for_persist (src/gobby/workflows/rule_validation_yaml.py; src/gobby/workflows/delivery_disposition.py:100), so the differential's rows stay equal, and RULE-2's writers reuse them. It runs no validate_rule dry run (src/gobby/workflows/sync_rules.py:389), which needs the rule engine that starts after this chunk: this chunk's generic test runs Python's dry run over every bundled YAML at every merge of 0.9.0, gdaemon embeds that same tree, and RULE-1A's parse and RULE-1B's compile of every bundled body hold the same check on the Rust side. The soft-deleted definition purge of Python's session expiry (src/gobby/sessions/lifecycle.py:381: rule, agent, session-variable and pipeline definition rows deleted over 30 days ago, every session_lifecycle.expire_check_interval_minutes) is TPL's job, registered on R4's registry at CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation in place of Python's op, and S3-DELETE deletes the op (D14). At CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation R2's content phase also stops calling Python's dirty-content refusal (src/gobby/runner.py:292-294): the native sync publishes gdaemon's embedded tree, which a dirty checkout cannot change, so a dirty checkout no longer refuses a worker's boot. Python's CLI keeps its own check for as long as it serves. TPL's sync covers the bundled tree only, every target of src/gobby/sync_registry.py:22-39: this chunk's own for prompts, agents, pipelines, rules, variables, detection manifests and MCP templates, and SKILLS' bundled service on this loader for skills. Python's start publishes only in dev mode, after a dirty-tree refusal, because it publishes the working tree (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:47-59, 72-77), and its dev-mode test needs the pyproject.toml and the src/gobby/install/shared that S3-DELETE removes (src/gobby/utils/dev.py:45-83). The native sync publishes gdaemon's embedded copy, so it takes neither gate: it runs at every hub or standalone start, a repeat changes no row because it refreshes only on drift, and a node never publishes (D83). Flip deletes a bare legacy collection named like the alias before it creates that alias, and a resumed flip whose alias exists deletes nothing (src/gobby/ai/embedding_switch_runner.py:317-324); gc skips that name, which is now the alias (:379). They then reach that dispatcher through the live-wake ops on dispatch_live_wake and dispatch_live_wakes, which src/gobby/sessions/mailbox_delivery.py:18-94 calls today. So the composer gate runs inside the op (src/gobby/events/wake.py:757-849): the local composer ledger read under composer_action_lock (src/gobby/terminals/composer_lock.py:41), a node terminal's reported composer state, and lease focus holds. AG-3 builds the native wake decision (agents-family 5.2) here, in crates/gagents/src/messaging/wake.rs, and for a terminal recipient it stays dormant until CP-WAVE5-CUT, when it replaces the dispatcher. It takes its host effects through the one AttentionHost trait (crates/gagents/src/host.rs), because this chunk lands before AG-1's machine effects gain their pane read and terminal write: the per-terminal composer lock held across the probe and the write, the composer activity read (state, reason and open-turn fingerprint), the lease focus hold, the wake write to a local or node terminal, and a node terminal's reported composer, where only empty takes the wake and a missing entry reads unknown and withholds it while the message stays queued (src/gobby/events/wake.py:757-957). A web-chat recipient's wake goes through a web-chat wake seam that AG-3 declares and CHAT-2 binds at its activation (agents-family 5.2.2). From CHAT-2's activation Python's dispatcher reaches no web-chat session, because Python never calls Rust (D19). So the seam's binding also reads each live web-chat session's undelivered wake messages every 5 seconds, as Python's replay reads them (src/gobby/events/wake_recovery.py:131-155), and wakes the session through the native decision under the same fanout rule. The recheck stops at CP-WAVE5-CUT, when the native decision replaces Python's dispatcher. Wake replay (agents-family D1.3). Until CP-WAVE5-CUT each status writer has its own replayer.
