chunks.title: Agents 1: spawn, definitions and personas
chunks.goal: spawn_agent (provider CLI launch through the node launch path), can_spawn_agent, evaluate_spawn, apply_agent_definition, apply_persona, /api/agents/spawn and launch-defaults; definitions from TPL's registry; worktree isolation through AG-4; panes through TERM-1's host worker ops until TERM-HOST. Seat checkout location (AGENTS rule 15) and the depth limit stay declared in definitions, never named in code (rule 16). Once AG-1 activates (CP-WAVE2-CUT), CRON calls the native spawn and no longer calls its agent-dispatch worker op, which S3-DELETE deletes. #25255's wait on the #21570 MCP flip is replaced by GW-1's per-tool routing (D26). SDK and ACP launches use ACP-CLIENTS, and launch reuses gdaemon's existing nodes/agents sandbox and repair code (about 9.3K non-test lines). AG-1 extends gagents' machine effects with spawn, cancel, pane read, terminal write and the completion hand-off, deliver_completion (agents-family 6.1, D71). AG-4 defines the effects and gdaemon implements them (.gobby/plans/agents-family.md Decision 6). gdaemon's deliver_completion keeps an in-memory set of run ids, each with the message its caller composes (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/agent_cancellation.py:113, 162), and one task. The task calls one allow-listed worker op on src/gobby/agents/terminal_delivery.py::deliver_existing_terminal_run, the call cancel_agent_run makes after its commit (src/gobby/servers/routes/agents.py:807-824), and then rereads the run's completion_subscribers rows. No rows left acknowledges the run. A false return (run missing or not terminal) drops it with a warning. A failed call, a lost reply (an unknown outcome that the reread reconciles, never a blind retry), a retained row or a failed reread keeps the run for another call 5 seconds later. The task calls nothing before R3's agents recovery step has finished. AG-1's own spawn failures end this way: the deferred spawn health check fails a run whose process exited after spawn and hands it off (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_health.py:206). AG-1 also binds gdaemon's adapter for gsessions' gagents port (crates/gdaemon/src/sessions_ports.rs, sessions-family Decision 7) to the session port functions AG-4 exports (agents-family 3.6), so from CP-WAVE2-CUT the sessions family reads and moves agent_runs rows through them. Its parent delivery goes through AG-3's mailbox (agents-family 5.1 and 6.1). Its HTTP rows declare AG-4's admission class (agents-family Decision 11). Launch (agents-family Decision 7 and 4.1). The launch code takes the run-state store and the terminal host as parameters, through a run-state store trait extracted from crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/state.rs. Node mode keeps its run-state file and host control, and crates/gdaemon/src/hub_launch.rs passes a store over the hub's agent_runs rows and the hub terminal host, which until TERM-HOST is D110's worker op for a launch and TERM-1's host ops for the terminal's later effects. No launch code is copied. The spawn effect launches a hub-local run in process and sends agent.spawn for another machine, mapping machine_cap_reached, remote_loopback_endpoint and spawn_in_doubt. gagents never touches sessions or session_variables rows itself (agents-family Decision 16): a child session comes from SES-2's create_session child fields, and variables and deletes go through gsessions' public services. A native spawn or resume also emits the WS events Python emits for it, as B0-WRITE emits its family's: agent_started, with the terminal-created event when the run has a terminal (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_execution.py:203-205; src/gobby/agents/resume_executor_settlement.py:146-148; src/gobby/runner_broadcasting.py:181-194). AG-1 also ports the agent workspace module (src/gobby/agents/agent_workspaces.py), which no family plan names: the per-project anchor and daemon-owned repository, seat and epic grants at spawn (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_providers.py:17, resume_executor.py:16), the session and epic bindings that HOOK-2's session handlers and AG-5's team teardown call through gagents, and the nightly commit behind the gobby:agent-workspaces system row (:434), whose handler CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation binds natively in place of CRON's worker op. workspace_handoff_references stays with SES-2. Its spawn gate re-collects a provider once on a model miss through AI-1C's refresh_provider (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_provider_resolution.py:228-247). The prompt file sweep of Python's session expiry (src/gobby/sessions/lifecycle.py:353: files over an hour in $TMPDIR/gobby-prompts, which src/gobby/agents/spawners/prompt_manager.py:61 writes) registers on R4's registry at that activation in place of Python's op, and S3-DELETE deletes the op (D14). Its checkout grant reads the merge_base_commits seat capability (src/gobby/agents/agent_workspaces.py:736-756, src/gobby/workflows/agent_resolver.py:47). That name is a constant in gcore, which TPL adds, because this chunk and RULE-1H's rule port of src/gobby/workflows/base_merge_commits.py:51 both read it and neither depends on the other. Launch's existing policy reads, the sandbox write paths (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/caches.rs:192-203) and the metadata copy (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/repair.rs:135-143), and the ported spawn sandbox read (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_providers.py:192-233) go through PROJ-1's metadata guard: a refusal rejects launch preparation before any launch, with no weaker sandbox and no reuse of a failed snapshot, and the copy releases its source guard before it touches the destination (Projects plan 4.5a; D63). The deliver_completion effect also takes an optional composed result: the set keeps it with the message, and the task calls one more one-line op on src/gobby/agents/terminal_delivery.py::deliver_and_cleanup_terminal_run (:418-484) for such a run, because deliver_existing_terminal_run rebuilds only status, run_id and error (:566-598). The reread is the same (D71). spawn_agent's resume_session_id parameter is an ordinary spawn and ports here (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_resume.py; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_implementation.py:159-164, 403-419). The daemon-stop relaunch does not: AG-WAIT's native relaunch reuses this launch path (D78), and a spawned run writes the resume_metadata_json snapshot that path reads (src/gobby/agents/resume_metadata.py:121-199; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_runtime.py:125). spawn_agent's placement parameter ports here, over TERM-2's workspace operations and D110's worker op (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_factory.py:352, 396-406; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_placement.py:52-207; src/gobby/terminals/workspace_agent_panes.py:219-659). gobby-core gains redact_terminal_output, a port of src/gobby/utils/terminal_output.py:9-55 beside redact_database_url (crates/gcore/src/degradation.rs:100), with Python's patterns in Python's order and the home-path rewrite, because this chunk is the first of its consumers and NODEHUB and COMMS-2 reuse it (D124). Spawn failures and the spawn health check pass pane text, cwd and messages through it (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_support.py:272; src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_providers.py:80-81; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_health.py:65). spawn_agent's extra_write_paths and write_paths_reason keep Python's authority check, which no recording refuses (src/gobby/agents/external_write_grants.py:23-162; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_implementation.py:209-220, 650-651, 931): a nonblank reason, each root through validate_external_write_roots (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/external_roots.rs:9) on gagents' MachineEffects seam, because gdaemon holds it, with the resolved roots, de-duplicated in request order, kept as the grant's canonical_roots, a recorded asserting session on the launch machine, a managed child only narrowing the roots its run recorded and one with none creating none, a remote target taking only a root session's assertion, and the grant stored with its audit fields in resume_metadata, where AG-WAIT's relaunch revalidates it (src/gobby/agents/resume_executor.py:138). gdaemon's launch path differs from Python's local launch in four ways, and this chunk closes them there, for hub-local and node launches alike, because from CP-WAVE2-CUT every hub-local seat launches through it and a comparison with gdaemon's own output cannot show what it never had (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/runtime.rs:129; crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/mod.rs:125, 137-152). First, the spawn env's own cache, Cargo home and Cargo target grants drop once the run's replace them, as src/gobby/agents/srt_runtime.py:640-645 and src/gobby/agents/sandbox_policy.py:974-986 do. gdaemon keeps them today (crates/gdaemon/tests/fixtures/node_srt/corpus.json:90, 106), which lets a sandboxed seat write the Cargo home and target that unsandboxed builds execute from. tests/agents/test_node_srt_corpus.py's chain skipped that step when it recorded the corpus (:422-431), so it takes the step and the corpus is re-recorded under D4's allowance for recording. Second, a workspace holding the vendored libghostty-vt gets LIBGHOSTTY_VT_ZIG_SYSTEM_DIR over the stable mirror of ~/.cache/zig/p with Python's pin check, because Zig's own fetch unpacks into zig-pkg, where the sandbox denies .gitmodules, so a seat cannot otherwise build gterm with vt-engine or run guard set G's groups that do (src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:336-362, 687-707; src/gobby/agents/sandbox_policy.py:922-923, 940-972; src/gobby/agents/sandbox_run_environment.py:88-89; src/gobby/agents/zig_packages.py). Tarball entries unpack through the tar crate with no member or link leaving the destination and no device or special file, as Python's data filter refuses (D125), and the mirror stays outside every run's write grant, because the daemon rebuilds it before each run and must not follow links a run planted (src/gobby/agents/sandbox_run_environment.py:42-45). Third, every launch gets the cargo launcher, so a reviewer building another checkout gets that checkout's own target under the existing grant (#24313; src/gobby/agents/sandbox_cargo.py; src/gobby/agents/srt_runtime.py:753-762), embedding src/gobby/agents/sandbox_cargo_runner.mjs, whose path S3-DELETE changes. Fourth, an SRT launch on Linux, or on macOS when it may open run sockets, gets the short run temp root, and the macOS one also gets a Unix-socket grant on it, the sccache keys that need that socket, and the reserved _agent_srt_socket_root variable that admits that root to the temp-write rule, recorded or withdrawn at every launch and relaunch through SES-2's narrow export, because D110's op does not write it (src/gobby/agents/srt_runtime.py:506-521, 604, 612, 621, 724-730; src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_providers.py:169-181; src/gobby/agents/sandbox_policy.py:855-870; src/gobby/agents/cargo_environment.py:13-32; src/gobby/workflows/condition_helpers_paths.py:105-112).
chunks.oracle: REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' spawn cases with the fake CLI launcher; launch commands compared with gdaemon nodes/agents provider_command output. The completion hand-off cases in REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS cover three outcomes. A failed spawn's run reaches Python's registry once, a retained subscriber row is retried, and a missing run is dropped (D71). Each of its HTTP rows replays its recorded admission matrix, with the refused agent token and the missing credential (agents-family 11.1.1). Node launch keeps its argv, environment, sandbox wrapping and run-state records through the store trait, and the spawn effect sends agent.spawn for another machine with every hub-flow code (agents-family 4.1.1 and 4.1.3). The workspace cases come from tests/agents/test_agent_workspaces.py's behavior on temp repositories: a dirty tree commits, an oversized file or symlink is skipped, a failed project does not stop the next, and a project's gc runs at most weekly. A seeded pending recovery entry refuses spawn before launch, and no candidate bytes reach the target checkout (D63). A transition with a composed result reaches Python's registry once with that result's fields, and a plain one goes through the delivery op (D71). A spawned run's resume_metadata_json replays src/gobby/agents/resume_metadata.py's snapshot for the same inputs, and a placed spawn replays Python's placement outcomes (D78). A spawn with resume_session_id replays Python's resume target and seat outcomes. A hub-local launch through D110's op replays REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' spawn cases with the fake launcher: the terminal row carries agent_run_id, title and machine_id; a cancel, a refused host and a retry on a row that is not pending answer as Python does; and a lost reply leaves the run in doubt with no second spawn. A placed launch whose op refuses before the attempt owns the row fails AG-1's own pending row and compensates its placement; a timed-out launch answers spawn_timeout while the worker settles the row; and a Codex launch's prompt arrives after the op returns. tests/utils/test_terminal_output.py's cases replay against the port, and a spawn failure's stored pane tail holds no secret-shaped text or home path (tests/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/test_failure_cleanup.py). tests/agents/test_external_write_grants.py's authority cases replay natively: a protected overlap (:114), a child widening its recorded roots (:129), a child with no grant (:158), a missing or inconsistent identity (:167), a changed grant on resume (:184) and a grant from another machine (:213, 223) each refuse. Canonical de-duplication and the audit fields replay from that file (:96). The launch path's own cases replay natively too: tests/agents/test_srt_runtime.py:653's write policy, where no unsandboxed Cargo path and not the shared sandbox cache root is writable (:887-892), tests/agents/test_sandbox_zig_packages.py, tests/agents/test_sandbox_cargo.py, tests/agents/test_cargo_environment.py and tests/agents/test_srt_socket_root_variable.py. The node launch comparison above admits only these differences.
chunks.size: L, 3 checkpoints (9 rows, large engine). Python in scope: spawn and definitions ~12K. The agent workspace module and the prompt sweep add about 0.9K of Python.
chunks.python_edits: One one-line allow-listed worker-op registration (D4, D71): the completion hand-off on src/gobby/agents/terminal_delivery.py::deliver_existing_terminal_run, bound to the worker's database, run manager, completion_registry and run_db. It is no longer called once AG-WAIT activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), and S3-DELETE deletes it. CRON's agent-dispatch worker op stays registered in Python until S3-DELETE, because retained generations still call it. One more one-line registration (D4, D71): the composed-result hand-off on src/gobby/agents/terminal_delivery.py::deliver_and_cleanup_terminal_run (:418-484), bound to the worker's database, completion_registry and run_db. It is no longer called once AG-WAIT activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), and S3-DELETE deletes it. One allow-listed op with a small shim in R0's worker package, agent_runtime_spawn (D110), over _runtime_spawn: it lands dormant, is no longer called once TERM-HOST activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), and S3-DELETE deletes it. tests/agents/test_node_srt_corpus.py's recording chain takes the launch's grant filter and its corpus is re-recorded, in the commit that changes gdaemon's grants, under D4's allowance for recording; no production Python changes for it.
chunks.registration: Standard family: one registry line (the agents family) in the agents crate that AG-4 creates (crates/gagents, .gobby/plans/agents-family.md Decision 3). gdaemon's deliver_completion task starts only while the agents family is active, from CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation (D37). It runs while its set holds a run, so it is not a timer job. Its prompt file sweep registers through R4's registry, and the agent-workspaces handler through CRON's system-job bindings.
chunks.risks: A spawn case must never launch a real provider CLI: the fake launcher is part of the harness contract. From CP-WAVE2-CUT to CP-WAVE5-CUT this chunk's placement and Python's re-placement of a relaunched seat (D78) share no insert lock or in-flight set, because both are process memory (src/gobby/terminals/workspace_agent_panes.py:242; src/gobby/storage/workspaces.py:345). Row locks keep each layout write consistent, and a wait past 30 seconds refuses as timed_out (workspace_agent_panes.py:53, 402-420; workspaces.py:899). A read-time sweep on one side can remove the other side's unbound pane (workspaces.py:889-930), whose bind then fails as not_found (workspace_agent_panes.py:527-528), so that one spawn or relaunch ends as a placement failure and compensates. TERM-2's worker ops close one side of that sweep: a native read keeps Python's unbound pane (D4). The side that remains is Python's sweep of this chunk's unbound pane, only through src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/admin_cold_start.py:153, 170 until AG-5, and that one spawn compensates as above.

chunks.title: Agents 2: runs lifecycle and watchdog
chunks.goal: Running agents and runs reads, cancel and cleanup, kill and stop, end_agent_run (structured handoff fields), unregister, cancel_stale_helpers, checkpoint_agent_worktree, capture, live output and result; the lifecycle monitor and stuck detector (autonomous/stuck_detector.py) as R4 jobs; failure categories. It absorbs agents 8.1's hub-side pane-monitor pass, so the node pane monitor (#24383) stays in S4-NODE and agents 4.1's file-contention edge on #24383 is dropped. #25269's remote runs reach this chunk through three allow-listed worker ops until CP-WAVE5-CUT, when NODEHUB moves the reported pane store after its last Python in-process reader (D19). The run reconciler (src/gobby/hub/remote_reconcile.py::RemoteRunReconciler) runs inside the health pass this chunk ports (src/gobby/agents/agent_health.py:158-165, 459-462), so this chunk registers Python's reconcile step as a one-iteration op on R4's registry at the health pass's cadence, and NODEHUB's native reconciler swaps it at CP-WAVE5-CUT. Remote idle is this chunk's idle check, which covers remote runs as Python's does (src/gobby/agents/idle_check_handler.py:125-154, 195-231): their reported idle facts come from Python's reported pane store through two read ops, RemotePaneStore.machine_ids and RemotePaneStore.get (src/gobby/hub/remote_pane.py:117-126), until NODEHUB's store serves them at CP-WAVE5-CUT. A node terminal's tail, composer state and stopped mark are read and written where a local terminal's are, on Python's host side until TERM-HOST, because Python resolves a node terminal to its remote runtime over the same store (src/gobby/hub/remote_runtime.py:32-136), so agents-family 2.0's loopback pane route (/_gobby/remote-pane) is not built (D4). Without these ops remote runs would go unsettled and their idle unwatched from CP-WAVE2-CUT, because Python's lifecycle loop does not start in worker mode (R4). Completion (D71). Every native terminal transition here calls AG-1's deliver_completion once, after its commit and its parent delivery, even when the parent delivery fails (agents-family 6.1.5). That covers cancel, kill, stop, end, unregister, cancel_stale_helpers, cleanup, and the watchdog's and pane-monitor pass's terminations. It also covers every termination another native family makes through this chunk's termination service: HOOK-2's session end and its binding of RULE-1B's step-workflow completion, PIPE-2's agent steps, CHAT-2's continue_in_chat kill and NODEHUB's node-run routes and reconciler. This chunk also builds the native in-memory completion waiters that PIPE-2's wait steps use from CP-WAVE4-CUT (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_executor_steps.py:144-176). deliver_completion and PIPE-2's execution completions notify them in process. A waiter also resolves from its durable agent_runs or pipeline execution row, read when it registers and every 5 seconds while it waits, because Python settles remote runs (the reconcile op) and exited panes (src/gobby/agents/terminal_cleanup.py:105) until CP-WAVE5-CUT. AG-WAIT takes the waiters over. Composer (D19, D74). The local composer ledger and the per-terminal composer lock stay Python's until TERM-HOST. This chunk's pass reaches the ledger through three one-line worker ops on src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py: read_composer (:525-535), which the watchdog's gate (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/composer_gate.py:16-29) and the attention pass's hold check (src/gobby/terminals/composer_attention.py:78-83, ported natively) read, and composer_unconsumed_submit_at and record_composer_local_command (:578-588), with which the attention pass settles a local command (src/gobby/agents/interactive_attention_monitor.py:274, 289). For a node terminal, the gate reads the composer from the RemotePaneStore.get op's entry, as remote_composer_state reads it, and only an empty composer takes the write (src/gobby/hub/remote_runtime.py:32-58). The idle reprompt and the capacity reprompt hold the lock across their probe, drain and write (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/recovery.py:363-399; interactive_capacity.py:89-111), and Python's wake holds the same lock until CP-WAVE5-CUT (src/gobby/terminals/composer_lock.py:10-12, 71; src/gobby/events/wake.py:875). A lock that Python holds cannot span separate worker ops, so both reprompts go through D74's one op, which runs those steps under the lock in Python and returns their outcomes. The pass rereads the capacity transcript just before the op, and on a capacity refusal it makes the blocked transition through the attention op after the op returns. After a delivered reprompt it updates its own idle and capacity state. Every other pane-step write takes no lock in Python (src/gobby/agents/terminal_prompt_monitor.py:114, 197) and stays TERM-1's plain write op. These ops sit behind gagents' machine effects (.gobby/plans/agents-family.md Decision 6), and TERM-HOST re-binds those effects to its native ledger and action hold at CP-WAVE5-CUT. Attention (D72). This chunk's attention writers reach Python's attention store through three one-line worker ops on AttentionStateManager.transition_async and AttentionMetadataStore.set and clear, until AG-3's attention family activates at CP-WAVE5-CUT. The writers are src/gobby/agents/attention_tracker.py, interactive_attention_monitor.py, watchdog/interactive_capacity.py and the idle check's remote sync. Its readers read the shared attention_states rows. get_agent_live_output keeps its Proxy backend until CP-WAVE5-CUT, when it flips with NODEHUB's reported pane store (D26), as the Orchestrator ruled on 2026-10-28 (.gobby/plans/agents-family.md:309-311). Turn lifecycle (D73). The pass's wait and provider-failure transitions (src/gobby/agents/attention_tracker.py:209-252; interactive_attention_monitor.py:366-409; watchdog/interactive_capacity.py:124-142) call AG-3's native turn reducer in process, with no worker op. Capacity recovery's provider-failure block is the one reducer write Python publishes today, so until CP-WAVE5-CUT it reaches browsers on the 5-second roster refresh (web/src/hooks/useSessionAttention.ts:26, 224-226), as a hook-path provider failure does. Jobs (agents-family Decision 8). Besides 8.1's eight pane steps (trust, loop, approval and queued-continuation prompts, periodic Enter, attention classification, initialization timeout and provider stalls), this chunk's R4 jobs run the interactive attention pass of src/gobby/agents/interactive_attention_monitor.py; the database steps of Python's lifecycle loop (pending-termination reconciliation, stale-pending reaping, daemon-stop orphan reaping, terminal-run session expiry, completed-task and autonomous-stuck sweeps, dispatch-mutex refresh, the acknowledged stale-run sweeps and reconciliation-pending reclassification); and the local idle decision (src/gobby/agents/idle_check_handler.py::IdleCheckHandler.check_idle_agents: reprompt, fail, recovery and coordination holds) with its transcript watchdog recovery (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/) and the local health and memory watchdogs. Python's InteractiveAttentionMonitor starts in the app lifespan (src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py:271-301), outside the runner, so R5 stops starting it at CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation; otherwise both passes would send capacity reprompts (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/interactive_capacity.py:157-199). Its HTTP rows declare AG-4's admission class (agents-family Decision 11). Parked sessions (D71). The idle decision and the autonomous-stuck sweep leave a parked session alone, as Python's do through CompletionEventRegistry.is_awaiting (src/gobby/agents/idle_check_handler.py:380; src/gobby/agents/lifecycle_monitor.py:212-214, 704-708). A session is parked if it has a durable completion_subscribers row whose agent run is active, read as src/gobby/storage/pipeline_subscribers.py::has_active_agent_wait reads it, or whose pipeline execution is not terminal, because native spawns and native pipeline executions subscribe durably only. It is also parked if Python's registry says so through a one-line worker op on is_awaiting (src/gobby/events/completion_registry.py:108-118), because Python's in-memory subscribers, such as task expansion's lineage (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_expansion_registry.py:167, 189), have no durable row. From CP-WAVE5-CUT AG-WAIT's service answers it, and the op is no longer called. Capture barrier (agents-family 6.1). Python's terminators still run beside this chunk's until CP-WAVE5-CUT (the reconcile op and terminal exit cleanup), and the _capture_lock in src/gobby/agents/capture.py:113 is process-local, so the durable predicates are the only fence between them: record_termination_intent updates only a pending or running run, replace_capture_slot compare-and-sets on capture_id and capture_revision with the marker check (src/gobby/storage/agents/_termination.py:32, 64), and the terminal transition compare-and-sets on status. A stop happens only after the capture persists, as capture_then_kill_async does (src/gobby/agents/capture.py:426). Session data (agents-family Decision 16). gagents never reads, locks or writes sessions or session_variables rows itself. Run reads, termination and cleanup use gsessions' public services (.gobby/plans/sessions-family.md 1.1, 2.2 and 2.4) and its transaction-scoped session_rows(tx, selector, lock). A statement Python wrote as one join (src/gobby/storage/agents/_queries.py, _selectors.py, _termination.py, _lifecycle.py, _cleanup.py) selects its own candidate rows, reads their sessions through session_rows in the same transaction, and applies the session predicate, ordering and limit in Rust. A read-only path (run reads, cleanup selection) opens with SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY. Termination stays at read committed: it locks its agents rows, then takes session_rows with lock set, in Python's lock order, and evaluates the session predicate only after both locks are held. Pane steps (agents-family 8.1). The pass runs over a run source and an action sink. The hub source is the agent_runs rows of running runs whose terminal is on the hub's machine, so it skips other machines' runs. The hub sink writes through the hub terminal host (TERM-1's write op until TERM-HOST), transitions attention through the attention ops until CP-WAVE5-CUT and terminates through this chunk's service with the reasons of src/gobby/agents/agent_health.py::check_initialization_timeout and check_provider_stalls. The idle decision is its own job, never a step in the pass. S4-NODE's node pane monitor (#24383) reuses the pass with its run-state file as the source and its report and terminate posts as the sink. Its jobs take the lifecycle monitor's iteration apart by owner (src/gobby/agents/lifecycle_monitor.py:377; R4's loop list): credential rotation is A1-RUNTIME's, closed-team teardown AG-5's and the remote reconcile NODEHUB's. This chunk's jobs run the rest, including the reconciliation-pending reclassification, which reaches the monitor through a runner callback (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:430-470, called from src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_callbacks.py:21-27), and the interactive attention monitor, whose Python service R5 stops starting at CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation (D98). Sandbox cleanup is this chunk's on the hub, because nothing else ports src/gobby/agents/sandbox_reaper.py or src/gobby/agents/srt_process_cleanup.py before Stage 4, and hub runs launch under SRT, so orphans and run roots would leak. It ports both behind gagents' machine effects, which gdaemon implements in crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/reaper.rs and runner_reap.rs, the paths #24384 names, and S4-NODE reuses them. A known difference until CP-WAVE5-CUT: AG-1's native placement and Python's re-placement of a relaunched seat share no insert lock or in-flight set, so a workspace read can sweep the other side's unbound pane, and that one spawn or relaunch ends as a placement failure (D78). chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: Stage 2 wave 2 goes live
chunks.goal: Category code. Activates Stage 2 wave 2. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. chunks.title: RULE-1B: the rule evaluation engine
chunks.goal: Rule evaluation over RULE-1H's conditions and helpers: templates, the rule pass and its effects, step and agent tool enforcement, the hardcoded lifecycle, the observers and the pass driver (s2-11 2.13-2.19), and rust-rule-evaluation's DR1-DR8 (s2-11 Decision 12). A library with no routes, proven offline; it serves hooks and tool calls only at HOOK-3. It also implements gtasks' ClosurePolicy port natively (#24151's gworkflows adapter under tasks-family C1; tasks-family 3.7), evaluating the task_close and task_land events over the installed task-closure rules, proven offline like the rest of the library; HOOK-3 binds it in place of B0-CLOSE's interim worker-op adapter (D41). Its scope: templates rendered with minijinja and minijinja-contrib's pycompat callback (D76), with shlex_quote, regex_search and regex_replace, and DR7 cache entries that compile every condition, pattern and template of their rows once, a stored row whose pattern the regex crate rejects being skipped and counted like a body Python rejects, logged once per row and revision (D33), so every bundled rule body and every condition and template of a bundled agent step workflow compiles (s2-11 Decision 11); the rule pass, which takes the event, session facts, variables, project id and a deadline and returns every response field, the eager variable delta, the staged on_receipt payload in the _gobby_staged_effects shape, the ordered effect log, audit records in record_rule_evaluation's line schema and the DR8 outcome, or DR5's DefinitionsUnavailable or DeadlineExceeded, over all 15 RuleEffect types (F2's seven kept) with aggregate blocking and the effect seams McpDispatch, SkillLoader and CommandRunner; the external effects run_command, proxy_hook with rtk, MCP injections, seat messages and transitions and skill-load guidance, failing open as Python does; step-workflow and agent tool enforcement with the step lifecycle under AgentStepInstanceMutation at priority 875 (DR6); the hardcoded lifecycle of src/gobby/workflows/engine/core.py::RuleEngine.evaluate and F4's rewrite recheck; the observers (plan mode, context usage, MCP, commits and turn interrupt, plus src/gobby/workflows/observer_terminal_hosting.py and its reserved native_terminal_hosted variable, which #25486's purge adds before the cut; .gobby/plans/task-25486.md 3.2); and the driver, the engine's public entry point, which serializes each session's passes in FIFO order, loads variables at one revision, runs observers and the pass, and commits the delta key-scoped under SessionVariableMutation at priority 950 (DR6, #23808). It includes the engine modules s2-11 does not list (src/gobby/workflows/engine/_offload.py, definition_binding.py, enforcement_guidance.py and offloaded_output.py). Site rows (s2-11 Site Disposition): 7, 10, 21, 22 and 26, each with its node-event outcome tested. The pass persists nothing (s2-11 2.14), so the driver writes what Python's evaluate writes directly, a failed write being logged and changing no decision as in Python: workflow_audit_log rows through a native store in this crate (src/gobby/storage/workflow_audit.py's writes, called from src/gobby/workflows/block_audit.py and from enforcement_audit.py, enforcement_completion.py, core.py and run_command_effects.py under src/gobby/workflows/engine/), which V5A's gobby rules audit reads, and rule_eval rows in metrics_events for blocked rules (src/gobby/workflows/engine/evaluation.py:686-699 and 816-836), which OBS's rule stats read (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/metrics_events.py:172-202). The crate's compile_stored_rules example compiles every enabled stored row over a read-only connection and prints each pattern the regex crate rejects, and CP-WAVE4-REVIEW runs it against the live hub (D33). engine::outcome keeps per-event-type counters behind outcome_snapshot(), counting each pass once (s2-11 2.14.5); HOOK-3 publishes them. The driver ports tool_context.py with DR6's pending tool context, hook_project_path.py, reserved_variables.py and variable_defaults.py (src/gobby/workflows/), and a cancelled pass commits nothing and returns Python's cancelled response. gdaemon builds one driver instance, which the ingress pipeline and the gateway share, so every Rust pass of a session joins one FIFO (s2-11 2.19). For the same reason these modules, which s2-11 5.2, 3.4 and 5.8 place in the hooks crate but the engine imports, live in this crate and HOOK-2 and HOOK-3 reuse them: src/gobby/hooks/effect_deadline.py, background_tasks.py, mcp_result.py, the staged-payload half of receipt_effects.py (STAGED_EFFECTS_FIELD, merge_staged_payloads, peek_worker_staging, record_worker_staging, stage_append_set_variables, staged_append_set_values and staged_session_variable) and format_discovery_result (src/gobby/hooks/dispatchers/mcp.py:150). chunks.title: HOOK-ENV: hook envelope and event normalization

chunks.title: Checkpoint review: Stage 2 wave 3 and the engine lanes, with the mid-port calibration
chunks.goal: Review pause after Stage 2 wave 3 (memory, code index, the comms core, chat, voice and the MCP crate) and the rule-engine and hook-envelope lanes, all landed dormant. This review also runs the second calibration: D17's gate, the resizing of waves 4-5 and Stage 3, and the census refresh for wave 5. Packet: The calibration measurement: a bounded replay soak across every family that is native or about to be (three passes, then differential and dual-run write replay of every recorded corpus), plus a detached 24h run only if Josh asks. The re-measured D11 rate, mismatch rate and cost per chunk; D17's gate result, which decides the go; the resized waves 4-5 and Stage 3; the refreshed census of Python in-process callers of single-owner state for wave 5; the re-recorded drifting provider fixtures. The regenerated project record and census, written under ~/.gobby/port/CP-WAVE3-REVIEW/, outside the checkout and outside any session scratchpad or /tmp, and named in the packet attestation; CP-WAVE3-CUT lands them as its first, docs-only commit. Resized sizes and splits are applied with update_task and create_task on the chunk tasks. Each split writes its parts into a scratch copy of docs/port/map-v2.json under that directory: new chunk ids whose depends_on, ledger_selectors and tree_nodes divide the split chunk's, with every chunk that depended on the split chunk depending on all of its parts. The parts get one blocks edge per depends_on entry, the dependents' edges move from the split task to the parts, and the split task closes as superseded by them only after its edges have moved. The ledger check, the disposition check and mapcheck run against that scratch map. The activation list for CP-WAVE3-CUT: the memory, code index, comms core, chat, voice and rules family defaults Native; the providers family default (#25111) with native web chat; CIX-2's native nightly repair; the memory jobs (#25557) replacing Python's ops on R4 and its interrupted dream-run recovery step in R3's order, with MEM-3's native nightly dream; #24712's grants default, after which native grants carry no projection operations; the gmcp bump; PROJ-2's attachment relocation and the namespace cutover, with CHAT-1's native attachment sweep. The irreversible step this cutover carries, for Josh's go: PROJ-2's once-only attachment relocation (#25050), whose only undo is a backup restore that loses every write made after the backup. PROJ-2's relocation and namespace cutover carry no schema input of their own (a prepared commit if the relocation needs one), and RULE-1A's rewrite is a prepared commit of this cut unless an earlier cut landed it. The prepared commits that CP-WAVE3-CUT lands include PROJ-2's consumer commit for the namespace cutover (web, skill intro references and docs), after which the cut runs gobby ui build; GET and PUT /api/files/user-md keep serving beside /api/hub/user until POST-CLEAN (D48). The voice default also moves the ai family's GET /api/llm/status to Native, because serve.rs composes VOICE's probe into the ai family only while the voice family is Native (D50), shown by REC-CATALOG's status cases replayed with that probe. The packet also carries CHAT-2's lifecycle worker-op cases (D81): the managed events for a managed session and none of them for an AGY session; SESSION_END, INTERRUPT and the ask-user and tool-approval NOTIFICATION for every session, each matching the recorded Python pass; BEFORE_AGENT's staged effects applied once on the delivered prompt; and a failed BEFORE_TOOL call that blocks. CP-WAVE3-CUT's opening smoke runs .gobby/plans/code-index-family.md E1's live gates 7 and 8; that cut's window names them. The replay soak runs with the namespace cutover's default off, so the old attachment paths match their recordings and no waiver applies; a live Compare record never cites a waiver (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:424), and CP-WAVE3-CUT's rehearsal is the first replay with that default on. CP-WAVE3-CUT's activation commit adds the four attachment waiver entries with their case citations and the regenerated ledger (D48). The sessions items for CP-WAVE3-CUT: GET /api/sessions claimed with CHAT-2's web-chat port bound, with its exact-page and error-propagation cases (.gobby/plans/sessions-family.md debt B3 and B10), and MCP set_handoff native, with its web-chat branch and the terminal results that Python's post-tool hook claims until CP-WAVE4-CUT. CHAT-2's expire pass across a plain restart, a native row left waiting and a Python row expired, with R5's start list no longer holding the lifespan's expire (D70). CP-WAVE3-CUT's activation commit also lands the entries and citations of the sessions debt B3 and B10 cases, and of any other sessions debt case on a surface it flips (D84). VOICE's close record lists each engine contract change under D107, #25072's criterion 3 and the probe's unavailable reason among them, and this review accepts or refuses them under D17. The packet says whether the machine that takes this cut has ffmpeg, because native speech-to-text reports unavailable from this cut on without it, and whether a Crane server answers at voice.tts_crane_url, because chatterbox reads as crane from this cut on and native text-to-speech fails without one. It says for A's adoption that gdaemon's build needs cmake, a C++ compiler and libclang from this cut on (D107). For Josh's go, it says that an attached CLI session's replies are not spoken from this cut until CP-WAVE4-CUT (D109). Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-WAVE3-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes from 0.9.0-gg as D40 item 3 defines them; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-WAVE3; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: Stage 2 wave 3 and the rules family go live
chunks.goal: Category code. Activates Stage 2 wave 3 and the rules family. Before step 1, this session copies the record, the census and the split map that CP-WAVE3-REVIEW wrote to the directory named in its packet attestation into its worktree, and lands them as a docs-only commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. This cut's prepared commits include PROJ-2's consumer commit for the namespace cutover, so the seat reviews it and step 5 rehearses it (D48). (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. Memory and code index write Qdrant and FalkorDB. hub-backup snapshots both but restores only PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348), so the rehearsal also proves a hand restore of the Qdrant snapshot and the FalkorDB RDB on scratch containers. The backup's files_home copy is also the only undo for PROJ-2's attachment relocation. (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build replays the memory, code-index, comms, chat, voice and rules corpora, writing memory, embedding, index, channel, chat and rule rows and Qdrant points in the scratch containers, which this rehearsal first restores by hand from step 4's snapshot and RDB. The restored generation reads them back, Python's in-process memory and tool-search writers keep honoring AI-2's serving lease, and open chat sessions reattach. It also runs PROJ-2's attachment relocation on the restored copy; the relocation cannot be undone in place, so for it the rehearsal proves the files_home and PostgreSQL restore instead. The activated build replays the four old attachment-path cases that the activation commit cites as Waived, and the deactivation build, which reverts their entries and citations with the default, replays them against their recordings (D48). (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. chunks.oracle: P0-DECISIONS' decision corpus plus REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' handler side effects (DB deltas). The terminals group's worker-op calls are asserted as recorded side effects, so the same cases replay later against the native terminal host; the edit-trigger case (one notify per hub-local edit, with root and relative path); and one node-origin case for each of Site rows 16 and 19, recorded from Python's branches. A session start that bumps only its own machine's STOP epoch (5.5.2), and 5.10.2's restart cases, in which a dead dispatch and an unconfirmed compact each settle as Python's do. 5.6.2's missing compact row, 5.7.2's fail-open session end, 5.9.2's reservation and 5.9.3's Grok pending context. Delivery of rows that set_handoff staged, from Python's tool or the native one, replays REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' compact and clear delivery cases, with each terminal call as a recorded side effect. A provider-failure resume and a failed handoff attempt each persist one notification and wake once with Python's metadata and bypass_debounce, an undelivered resume other than session_active blocks the provider failure, and a failed attempt that cannot be woken is queued. A session end reaps the agent's sandbox roots. D75's op cases assert its calls as recorded side effects: a set_handoff completion calls the after-tool entry once and an ordinary tool event makes no hop, a Stop with a staged marker calls the stop entry, each compact, clear and Codex site calls its entry with the session the site names, a failed call fails no hook response, and a failed clear continuation queues its pull prompt. A test of the shim in R0's worker package feeds each entry a recorded site's arguments and asserts that Python's function receives the same HookEvent fields or session row. The native delivery services replay the compact and clear delivery cases over a fixture host whose scripted composer lock stays held across every read and write of a ladder, as tests/terminals/test_composer_arbitration.py:437-465 asserts of Python's. A provisional resume asserts the finalize op's call, and a failed call returns the ingress's retryable refusal (D78). The fixture host's draft cases replay: a delivery wipes a draft and then types, an exact pending command gets bare Enter, and a draft that will not clear fails composer_not_clean with nothing typed.
chunks.size: L, 3 checkpoints. Python in scope: hook handlers ~16K of hooks 40.8K; Rust ~10K. The handoff delivery services outside hooks add ~2.6K Python and ~1.5K Rust. D75's op shim adds about 0.1K of Python in R0's worker package.
