They are no longer called once TERM-HOST activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), and S3-DELETE deletes them. It also registers D75's one handoff delivery op, whose shim sits in R0's worker package and which is no longer called once TERM-HOST activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), and one one-line registration (D4, D78) on finalize_resume_handoff_async (src/gobby/agents/resume_finalization.py:58-79), which is no longer called once AG-WAIT activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT). S3-DELETE deletes both.
chunks.registration: Hooks crate. Its handoff triggers read the compiled terminal ownership default that TERM-1 separated: on Proxy they call D75's op and on Native they call the delivery services, so no runtime switch is read (D37).
chunks.risks: Handlers write through many families: every write goes through the owning family's crate API. Terminal effects pass through worker ops until CP-WAVE5-CUT, one hop per handoff trigger or composer call, as TERM-1's host effects do; the composer-wait close runs on every tool event (src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_base.py:255-272), so that op is one hop per tool event, under CP-WAVE4-CUT's hook latency bound. Python's handoff recovery entry point would treat a native dispatch's marker as dead and deliver it again (src/gobby/hooks/terminal_handoff_delivery.py:465-476), so the slot changes owner in the activation that starts the native delivery services (CP-WAVE5-CUT). From CP-WAVE4-CUT to CP-WAVE5-CUT a native handler and Python's delivery share one handoff. The handler commits its own writes before it calls D75's op and the claim stays atomic on the shared row, but a native port of a site's check that disagrees with Python's leaves the delivery to the Stop entry or to the restart, so the op cases compare each check with the recorded site.

chunks.title: HOOK-3: hook ingress and the joint hooks and MCP rule-pass flip
chunks.goal: #24151's flip (s2-11: #24151 flips last): POST /api/hooks/execute, the node hook replay and receipts endpoints (D11) and outbound webhooks move to Rust together with the native tool-call rule pass on the gateway (D27). One CLI session's hook passes and tool-call passes share one engine and one FIFO (s2-11's hooks_mcp_split guard, leaf 7.15.5, whose two sides here are the hook-ingress default and the tool-call rule-pass engine default, not the /mcp route, which the gateway serves natively from CP-MCP-CUT, D26). Hook ingress and the rule pass land with Proxy defaults, and CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation commit flips them to Native together. From then on the gateway no longer calls GW-2's preflight worker op, which S3-DELETE deletes. HOOK-3 also re-binds gtasks' ClosurePolicy port from B0-CLOSE's interim worker-op adapter to RULE-1B's native policy, and CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation commit flips that with the rule passes, so close, landing and the vacated-parent walk no longer call the closure-policy worker op. That re-binding is #24151's close-route activation under tasks-family C1 (D41). Its composition also binds the native message processor's turn interrupts (crates/gsessions/src/turn_interrupt.rs; src/gobby/sessions/processor_transcripts.py:349-368) to AG-3's native turn reducer (D73). Each of RULE-1B's audit records increments rule_evaluations_total and observes rule_evaluation_duration_seconds, and only allow records become durable lines (src/gobby/telemetry/rule_allow_audit.py:206-228). The composition publishes those two metrics and DR8's outcome_snapshot() counters through SEAM-FAMILY's Rust telemetry routing, which OBS's reads serve: that is the family's per-route observability (rust-rule-evaluation D2.5), because the hooks-compare.jsonl that s2-11 7.13 names is not built (D13, D37). The composition also binds RULE-1B's admission release to the ingress admission (src/gobby/hooks/adapter_execution.py::release_session_admission_for_external_wait). In s2-11 terms it carries 3.2-3.5, 5.11, 5.12, P6's node replay, receipt and webhook routes (6.2's detection manifests are NODEHUB's, D11) and P7's composition, admission binding, drain handover, audit lines and flip (7.1, 7.7, 7.12, 7.13, 7.15); its family claims only its own rows and leaves /api/nodes/checkouts, /api/nodes/report and /api/nodes/runs to NODEHUB, and the machine check runs after the floor check and before any claim (3.2.1, 3.2.3). HOOK-3 drives hook ingress and the gateway's tool-call rule-pass engine from one compiled default, and a test asserts that no build exposes them apart; 7.15.5's start refusal keyed on route values is not built, because no front_door.routes value is used live (D37). The gateway stops calling both phases of GW-2's op, the preflight and the after phase (D82). Hub inbox jobs (3.5): Python's drain and pruning loop (src/gobby/hooks/inbox_maintenance.py:89-162) and its quarantine retention loop (src/gobby/hooks/quarantine_retention.py:97-166), scheduled at src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_periodic.py:333-342, run as R4's one-iteration ops from CP-RUNNER-CUT, and this chunk's native jobs replace both ops on R4's registry at CP-WAVE4-CUT. The drain loop and Python's startup barrier both POST each spooled envelope to the front door's /api/hooks/execute over loopback HTTP (src/gobby/hooks/inbox.py:260-299, 488), so after the flip either would be a Python client of the native route, which D4 rules out. 7.13's compare mode and hooks-compare.jsonl are not built, because no hook compare runs on the live hub (D13, D37). The native drain dispatches each spooled envelope in process through the route table, never over HTTP (s2-11 Decision 5), settles it by response, quarantines a 403 without replay, keeps inbox claims exclusive and restorable, and prunes inbox, temp and quarantine files at Python's ages and bounds (3.5.1-3.5.3). Its startup pass (3.5.4) returns the fields of drain_hook_inbox_barrier's result (src/gobby/hooks/inbox.py:316-326, 698) and takes the drain half of R3's hook-barrier step at the same activation, so the Rust side stops calling Python's drain entry point and hands those fields to Python's classification entry point (s2-11 D2.1). The same pass runs on demand with a deadline for the lifecycle monitor's reclassification of fenced runs, which runs the barrier again with a 5-second timeout (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:427-451), and that call binds to it at the same activation. Receipt retention (3.4): Python also runs two receipt steps that s2-11 does not list. The receipt prune loop (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_periodic.py:343-350; src/gobby/runner_maintenance/messaging.py:48; src/gobby/storage/hook_receipts.py:376-420, a 24-hour window and a 100,000-row bound) and the hook-effect retirement step that session expiry leaves as a Python op for #24151 (src/gobby/storage/hook_receipts.py:357-373) run as R4's one-iteration ops, and this chunk's native jobs over 3.4's receipt seam replace both at CP-WAVE4-CUT. Composition and dispatch (7.1, 5.11, 7.7): the family's composition binds hook broadcasts to the native WS broker (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/broker.rs:350) and the engine's command runner to a local process runner for run_command effects, and every seam group no family adapter binds yet returns SeamUnavailable. Its in-process dispatch sends a request through the front door's authentication and route table with a loopback peer and the local operator credential, and the inbox drain uses it too. Every tool call the pipeline makes, its metadata mcp_calls, rule mcp_call effects and handler calls, goes as POST /api/mcp/tools/call through that dispatch, so it reaches whichever backend serves the tool and, under the operator credential, runs no policy pass, as Python's in-process calls run with enforce_workflow false (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_proxy.py:277-292; src/gobby/hooks/dispatchers/mcp.py:420; src/gobby/hooks/factory.py:471; src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/execution.py:50-57); the pipeline's own calls never re-enter the pass, and an unreachable backend returns SeamUnavailable. Blocking webhooks apply their decisions and retry under RetryConfig as Python's do. Its composition appends each pass's allow records, which RULE-1B returns among its audit records, to rule-allow-audit.jsonl through a bounded writer with Python's file name, queue capacity, shutdown drain and rotation, because hub-backup archives that file (s2-11 7.13, gate D2.6; src/gobby/telemetry/rule_allow_audit.py:24-188; src/gobby/config/logging.py:19, 67-122; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:790-793). Route execution (5.12) keeps s2-11's Site Disposition rows 1 and 25 (from .gobby/plans/hook-envelope-file-facts.md Decision 12): every delivery runs with its delivery origin set, hub-local or the node's machine id, as delivery_scope does (src/gobby/hooks/adapter_execution.py:16; src/gobby/hooks/checkout_reads.py:81-99), and an AGY startup preflight for a node envelope is refused before any disk walk; an unavailable checkout read blocks a critical hook and degrades any other (5.12.3). Hub-origin checkout reads use the engine's local implementation (s2-11 2.2); node-origin reads stay unbound until S4-HOOKS binds the node adapter (s2-11 7.11), which matches Python today, whose reads fail while nodes have no checkout.read handler (#24521), and no production node sessions exist before Stage 4 (#25284). Admission (7.12): its routes consume SEAM-CALLERS' verified admission (#25046, #25068) and hold no verifier of their own, and unavailable authority returns 503. Agent tokens with matching, mismatched, revoked and expired identity keep Python's outcomes on execute and the webhook list and are refused on node hook replay, receipts and the webhook test; API keys, the local operator and ordinary cookies keep Python's permissions; managed cookies are refused on every POST before any effect; and the node rows receive the key's machine. HOOK-3 also implements CHAT-2's web chat lifecycle port on HOOK-1's manager and HOOK-2's handlers over the shared driver, so one web chat session's lifecycle, hook and tool-call passes join one FIFO (s2-11 7.1, D1.1 and D1.2), and CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation commit re-binds the port from CHAT-2's interim worker-op adapter with the rule passes (D81). From then on no web chat event runs a Python rule pass, for AGY sessions or any other, which is what s2-11 7.14's Python guard protected, so that guard is not built. Hold-open (5.12): the route keeps Python's order (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/hooks.py:550-590): a PostToolUse settles a terminal question even when an after-tool rule blocks, a rule or adapter denial is final, and otherwise a hook type of src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/hook_responses.py:13-22 carrying X-Gobby-Session-Id may hold its response open (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/hook_hold_open.py:29-209), with the envelope lease renewing through the wait. For a web chat session, a tool that session, project or global approval rules allow is approved through CHAT-2's approval helpers, a session already holding three pending interactions is denied with too_many_pending, and otherwise the hook waits on a tool or ask-user interaction in CHAT-2's native pending-interaction manager, with Python's 300-second timeout and pending_approval broadcast; approve_always adds the key to the session's approved tools. For a Claude terminal session, an AskUserQuestion PermissionRequest waits for Telegram's answer and its PostToolUse settles the question, through two one-line worker ops on Python's TelegramQuestionController.ask and terminal_answer, bound to the worker's communications manager and pending-interaction manager (src/gobby/communications/telegram_questions.py:46-137; D4), because Python's adapter connections, callback routing (src/gobby/communications/manager.py:828) and that controller's in-memory prompts stay Python's until COMMS-2. ask is a bounded call: its own 110-second window sits inside ghook's 115-second wait, the Rust caller times the call at those 115 seconds, and a failed or timed-out call returns the hook's own response, as ask's None does. That manager writes the question's wait through Python's turn reducer until then, a shared-row write that serializes with the native reducer on the row lock (D19). CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation re-binds both calls to COMMS-2's native controller. 5.12 also carries run_adapter_hook's per-session admission with its two-timeout abandonment and the 5-second watchdog that R4's service list gives this chunk (src/gobby/hooks/adapter_execution.py:155-280), adapter timeouts that answer adapter_timeout and finalize their envelope later, the AGY startup-claim preflight with its rollback and invalidation (src/gobby/hooks/startup_claim_preflight.py), the retry bodies (preflight_timeout, ingress_backpressure and adapter_timeout) and the graceful-error rules (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/hook_responses.py). Its composition also registers these jobs on R4's registry at CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation, each in place of Python's op, and S3-DELETE deletes the ops (D14): hook receipt retention (src/gobby/runner_maintenance/messaging.py:48, src/gobby/storage/hook_receipts.py:376), the two hook steps of Python's session expiry, hook-effect retirement and the startup-mark prune (src/gobby/sessions/lifecycle.py:333-344; src/gobby/storage/hook_receipts.py:357, src/gobby/storage/session_startup_marks.py:53), and workflow audit retention (src/gobby/runner_maintenance_audit.py:20, session_lifecycle.workflow_audit_retention_days), because the rule pass this chunk flips writes that table. Hold-open autoapproval reads project approval rules through PROJ-1's metadata guard, and a refusal returns the existing deny envelope with reason project_metadata_unavailable, never an autoapproval through session or global rules (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/hook_hold_open.py:160; Projects plan 4.5a; D63). ghook's own hooks_disabled read stays outside the guard (D63). Its composition also binds SES-3B's message processor to the hook handlers that feed it, the event sink, VOICE's speech streaming (s2-11 7.1) and the transcript mirror, whose host reaches SES-3B's worker ops on Python's CommunicationsManager and COMMS-1's message read until CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit re-binds it to COMMS-2, and starts the processor as its own task only while the hooks family's compiled default is Native, which CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation commit flips (D37). The processor is an I/O pump, so it stays off R4's registry (ROADMAP.md:558-567; #22411). From the same activation R5 no longer starts Python's SessionMessageProcessor (src/gobby/runner_init/services.py:515-556), so exactly one processor tails each session. It also holds HOOK-2's handoff delivery services, which it starts only while the compiled terminal ownership default is Native, which CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit flips (D37, D75). Until then HOOK-2's handlers reach Python's delivery through D75's op. Python's rule evaluation runtime thread, which R4's service list gives this chunk (src/gobby/workflows/evaluation_runtime.py:81, built at src/gobby/hooks/factory.py:684), has nothing left to run from CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation, when the rule passes move, and S3-DELETE deletes it (D14). Each step runs under SEAM-CALLERS' daemon-owned execution with no request principal and its pipeline execution id, as src/gobby/workflows/pipeline/handlers.py:20-22, 66-72 does (#25416), and a step's tool that is still Python's reaches GW-2's compatibility endpoint with that scope (D121). chunks.title: Checkpoint review: Stage 2 wave 4 (hot path, pipelines, teams, node endpoints)
chunks.goal: Review pause after Stage 2 wave 4: the hot path (HOOK-1, HOOK-2 and HOOK-3's joint flip of hook ingress and the tool-call rule pass, D27), pipelines (PIPE-1, PIPE-2), teams (AG-5) and the node endpoints (NODEHUB), all landed dormant. Packet: The full decision corpus through ghook and the native ingress for all five CLIs; the mixed hook and tool-call FIFO case per CLI; the pipeline and team corpora; the node-endpoint cases against the live node's contract version; the dormancy proof; CP-WAVE3-CUT's window record. The activation list for CP-WAVE4-CUT: hook ingress and the rule pass Native together, after which GW-2's preflight worker op is not called; pipelines Native, so CRON stops calling Python's pipeline-dispatch op; teams Native; the node endpoints Native against the live node's existing gdaemon, except the report and terminate routes, which move with the reported pane store at CP-WAVE5-CUT (D19). The closure-policy parity proof: RULE-1B's native ClosurePolicy against REC-PILOT's closure vectors (#25501), and the activation item that re-binds the port from B0-CLOSE's interim worker-op adapter, after which close, landing and the vacated-parent walk no longer call that op (D41). It lists every enabled stored rule row with a pattern the regex crate rejects, from RULE-1B's compile_stored_rules example run over a read-only connection to the live hub: CP-WAVE4-CUT proceeds only with that list empty or each entry ruled on by Josh (D33). HOOK-3 also brings web chat lifecycle cases through the re-bound port, AGY SESSION_END, INTERRUPT and the ask-user and tool-approval NOTIFICATION included, in one FIFO with the session's hook passes (D81); the gateway's after-phase cases (D82); the drain, pruning, retention and startup-pass cases against Python's (s2-11 3.4, 3.5, D2.1); native audit lines that parse with Python's schema (s2-11 7.13); the admission cases on the hook and webhook rows, reviewed for security as SEAM-CALLERS' admission is (s2-11 7.12); the split tool-pair case across the activation restart (s2-11 7.15.6); and HOOK-2's terminal worker-op side effects, recorded for TERM-HOST's replay (s2-11 7.5), with its handoff dispatch recovery cases (s2-11 5.10). The activation list also re-binds web chat's lifecycle port (D81), stops the after phase of GW-2's op (D82), swaps Python ops on R4 for HOOK-3's native jobs (the hook inbox drain, quarantine retention, the receipt prune and hook-effect retirement), and gives R3's order HOOK-3's startup pass in place of Python's drain entry point (s2-11 3.4, 3.5, D2.1); R3's handoffs slot stays Python's until CP-WAVE5-CUT (D75). It also brings HOOK-3's hold-open cases: a denial stays final, the PostToolUse settle, auto-approval, too_many_pending, approve_always, a browser response resolving a native wait, and the two Telegram worker ops called once per question (s2-11 5.12). The sessions items for CP-WAVE4-CUT: SES-3B's message processor started by HOOK-3's composition in place of the one R5 started, with its cases, including the transcript mirror's worker-op calls; and HOOK-2's calls of D75's handoff delivery op for what set_handoff stages, with Python's delivery still the one live delivery behind it and the native services' compact and clear cases proven dormant over a fixture host (D75). PIPE-2's restart recovery against R3's crash-point corpus: one wake per subscriber on a whole restart, and no effect on a running execution on a backend respawn. A provisional resume at the native ingress goes through HOOK-2's finalize op (D78), and HOOK-2's tool handlers notify CIX-2's native edit trigger in place of Python's. The bundled expand-task pipeline runs end to end on PIPE-2 against PLANS' native run with a fake LLM, its wait step resolving from the run's row (D71). The activation list also has PIPE-1's import of landed files in R2's content phase in place of Python's, with import_landed false on the worker's startup_content phase, and reload_cache and POST /api/admin/workflows/reload Native with the pipelines family, with PIPE-1's import differential as evidence (D83). Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-WAVE4-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes from 0.9.0-gg as D40 item 3 defines them; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-WAVE4; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: the hot path and Stage 2 wave 4 go live
chunks.goal: Category code. Activates the hot path and the rest of Stage 2 wave 4. Its window opens with the five-CLI smoke that step 7 lists. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. Hook ingress writes sessions, rule state and webhook deliveries, all in PostgreSQL. (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build replays the full decision corpus through ghook for all five CLIs, the pipeline and team corpora and the node-endpoint cases, writing session, variable, pipeline-run, node checkout and agent-run rows. The restored generation, with Python's hook pipeline and rule engine serving again, reads them back and resumes the pipeline runs. The compact and clear delivery cases replay through D75's op, with Python's delivery behind it (D75). The bundled expand-task pipeline replays end to end on PIPE-2 against PLANS' native run with a fake LLM, so its wait step resolves from the run's row (D71). The activated build's first start also runs PIPE-1's import of landed files, over a copy of the live ~/.gobby/workflows in the isolated home and over the registered checkouts, which it only reads: each file reaches its row, and the log of skipped files must be empty or each entry ruled on by Josh. A rule, an agent, a pipeline and a variable file added under the isolated home's workflows root reach their rows at the next restart, and a malformed one is logged and skipped while the start succeeds. The restored generation's Python then imports the same files again (D83). (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. Hook ingress (POST /api/hooks/execute, node hook replay and receipts, outbound webhooks) and the tool-call rule pass flip to Native together (D27), so the gateway stops calling GW-2's preflight worker op. The pipelines, teams and node-endpoint family defaults flip to Native, and CRON stops calling Python's pipeline-dispatch op. The same commit re-binds gtasks' ClosurePolicy port to RULE-1B's native policy through HOOK-3, so close, landing and the vacated-parent walk stop calling B0-CLOSE's closure-policy worker op (D41). NODEHUB's report and terminate routes stay on Python behind its reported-pane default until CP-WAVE5-CUT (D19). HOOK-2's turn helpers and the native message processor's interrupts call AG-3's native turn reducer, so Python's reducer keeps two live callers until CP-WAVE5-CUT, the pending-interaction manager's Telegram question (src/gobby/servers/pending_interactions.py:136, 289) and the node report route's attention tracker (src/gobby/agents/attention_tracker.py:214, 245, through src/gobby/hub/remote_pane.py:192-244), whose writes stay safe on the row lock (D19, D73). The same commit binds AgentDefinitions' team methods (RULE-1H) to AG-5's crate API, so pod launch refusals and seat-team checks read native team rows from the first native pass. The same commit re-binds CHAT-2's web chat lifecycle port to HOOK-3's native pipeline, so web chat's lifecycle events stop calling CHAT-2's lifecycle worker op (D81), and the gateway stops calling the after phase of GW-2's op with its preflight (D82). HOOK-3's native jobs replace Python's one-iteration ops on R4's registry: the hook inbox drain, quarantine retention, the receipt prune and hook-effect retirement. Its startup pass replaces Python's drain entry point in R3's hook-barrier step, so the Rust side hands the pass's fields to Python's classification entry point, and the lifecycle monitor's reclassification calls the same pass. R3's handoffs slot stays on Python's entry point until CP-WAVE5-CUT, because Python's delivery stays live until then (s2-11 3.4, 3.5, D2.1; D75). Hold-open moves with the route: web chat waits on CHAT-2's native pending-interaction manager, and Telegram questions run through HOOK-3's two worker ops until CP-WAVE5-CUT (s2-11 5.12). HOOK-3's receipt retention, hook-effect retirement, startup-mark prune and workflow audit retention, PIPE-1's compact workflow-instance prune, PIPE-2's approval expiry and pipeline maintenance, and AG-5's closed-team teardown also register on R4's registry in place of Python's ops. HOOK-3's composition starts SES-3B's message processor with the hook ingress, as its own task and off R4's registry, and R5 no longer starts Python's SessionMessageProcessor, so exactly one processor tails each session (D37). Its transcript mirror reaches Python's communications manager through SES-3B's worker ops until CP-WAVE5-CUT. HOOK-2's handlers call D75's op from this commit, so Python's functions keep delivering under Python's composer lock, and the composition leaves HOOK-2's delivery services unstarted until CP-WAVE5-CUT (D75). HOOK-2's tool handlers notify CIX-2's native edit trigger from this commit, which leaves Python's edit trigger nothing to do. A session Python relaunched finishes its provisional resume at the native ingress through HOOK-2's finalize op (D78). PIPE-2's native restart recovery takes R3's pipeline_recovery slot as a hub-only, once-per-process step, and Rust stops calling Python's entry point (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:350-450, 749). HOOK-2's two direct wakes reach Python's dispatcher through the live-wake op from here until CP-WAVE5-CUT. R2's content phase also runs PIPE-1's import of landed files after TPL's sync and sends the worker's startup_content phase with import_landed false, and POST /api/admin/workflows/reload and reload_cache flip with the pipelines family default (D83). (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 12 hours. It opens with the five-CLI smoke: hook ingress for Claude Code, Codex, Droid, Grok and AGY, a spawn, a terminal attach, the close flow, and the live node using the native node endpoints, while its reports still reach Python's report route until CP-WAVE5-CUT. Triggers: any smoke step failing; a hook decision that differs from the decision corpus or from the known-bad registry's correct value; a hook and tool-call pair out of FIFO order; hook latency above the bound in the window plan; a pipeline run lost, run twice or stuck; a team admission that differs; the live node's reports or commands failing; health or start proof failure. A close, landing or ancestor auto-close that the native policy allows or blocks where Python's evaluator would not is also a trigger (D41). Further triggers: a pipeline wait step that misses or doubles an agent run's or a pipeline execution's completion, and a durable subscriber of a native pipeline execution woken twice or not at all (D71). Further trigger: a stored rule row the native cache skips because the regex crate rejects its pattern, because a skipped block rule fails open (D33). The smoke also opens one managed and one AGY web chat session and runs a tool call and a stop in each, whose lifecycle passes now run natively (D81); a web chat lifecycle decision that differs from the recorded Python pass is also a trigger. Further triggers: a spooled envelope delivered twice or left undelivered, a quarantine file or receipt kept past Python's age, a staged handoff delivered twice or never after a restart, and a missing rule-allow-audit.jsonl line. Hold-open triggers: an attached Telegram question that no longer reaches Telegram or whose answer does not reach the terminal, and a web chat tool approval that a browser response does not resolve (s2-11 5.12). Job triggers: a job this activation swapped in that misses its cadence, errors on every fire, or deletes or changes a row its Python op would keep. A session message, usage update or token event lost, doubled or out of order after the processor starts, an assistant text block mirrored to an attached Telegram conversation out of order, twice or not at all, and a staged handoff delivered twice or left undelivered, are also triggers. It includes a deliberate plain gobby restart with a native pipeline execution running, which must keep running. Further triggers: a native execution interrupted or resumed by a backend respawn; an interrupted execution's subscriber woken twice or not at all. A pipeline wait step that misses or doubles an expansion run's completion is a trigger too (D71). One more trigger: a valid file landed under .gobby/workflows or ~/.gobby/workflows that a restart leaves off its row, or a malformed or refused one that stops a start (D83). (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with the tag merged into 0.9.0-gg in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Otherwise restore the full set only when gcode or ghook itself broke, because gcode below the checkout floor breaks the code-index gateway (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796). After a stamped-set restore, the code-index gateway refuses the restored gcode until the deactivation build is promoted, because that gcode is below the checkout's gcode pin (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:795-796; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5). The restore burns the activated versions, never the restored target's own. Promote the deactivation build only as step 5 proved it: when a trigger implicates a dormant landing rather than this stage's defaults, stay on the restored generation with the pin and the hold extended, add a revert of that landing to the deactivation commit first, and rerun step 5's deactivation proof on the changed commit. Then give the prepared deactivation commit fresh version bumps, first rebasing it onto 0.9.0 HEAD if an outcome-2 fix or another landing has moved HEAD past the commit it was built on, because land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task (step 3), and every fix commit changes the version lines that this commit bumps. Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with the deactivation commit that A's rehearsal proved (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-WAVE3-CUT's last promotion. The restore members are gdaemon alone. Restoring it puts hook ingress and the rule pass back in Python together, as D27 requires. The restore also returns the message processor to Python: R5 starts Python's SessionMessageProcessor again, which re-registers the live sessions and restores each tail from the shared sidecar. Handoff delivery returns to Python's post-tool hook with it.

It also re-binds gtasks' ClosurePolicy port to RULE-1B's native policy (D41). It also binds RULE-1H's team methods to AG-5's crate API. It also registers HOOK-3's native hook jobs on R4's registry in place of Python's ops, puts HOOK-3's startup pass in R3's order in place of Python's drain entry point, and re-binds CHAT-2's web chat lifecycle port to HOOK-3 (D81). chunks.title: Terminal host: Rust becomes the single owner
chunks.goal: Wave 5 (callers before callees). After the last Python in-process callers of the host are native (agent spawn, pipelines, cron, rules, hook ingress, teams, wake delivery, handoff delivery, chat, release_composer), Rust takes the gterm host manager: host lifecycle and ownership (host_lifecycle.py, terminal_ownership.py), the native composer ledger (#24571, plan #25276), the reconcile settler and host exit proof (#24572), settlement branches and pane binding (#24574); terminal processes survive an ordinary restart (R6). Once it activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), no terminal worker op (TERM-1, SES-2, AG-3, CHAT-2) is called, and S3-DELETE deletes them. Its activation switch is the compiled terminal ownership default that TERM-1 separated from the terminal routes' backend: it flips to Native, which moves RouteLatch to Owner and GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE to native, and Python follows the latched value through TERM-1's helper (D19). Owns the native terminal default-flip gate row and replaces guard set G's host checks with a Rust test gate. It also builds #24573, moved here from TERM-1. Plan section 2.9 (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md) keeps 2.8's settler (#24572) as the only settler, with the runtime reporting the prepared spawns it holds through Effects::holds, and the route it plans serves Python's spawn, read and termination callers in Native through a Python runtime client that is not built (#24574, D4). So 2.9's operations (spawn prepare, commit and fail, settled once through that settler; observer reservations; snapshot, full snapshot, history, liveness, session presence, spawn refusal and attach locator reads; terminate and resize on the row's current host epoch) become the native host's in-process terminal runtime for its native callers, proven by 2.9.1-2.9.3's tests, and 2.9.4's HTTP path (POST /api/internal/terminals/runtime) is not built, because no caller outside the daemon remains. From this chunk's activation, node terminals' tails, composer states and stopped marks come from NODEHUB's reported pane store, which moves at the same activation (D19), so nothing calls Python's remote runtime (src/gobby/hub/remote_runtime.py) afterwards. From its activation, its composer ledger and action hold (crates/gterminals/src/write_api.rs) serve AG-2's watchdog composer calls and reprompts in process, so AG-2's three composer ops and D74's reprompt op are no longer called. It also binds the host effects of AG-3's native wake decision on AttentionHost: the composer lock to that action hold, the activity read to its ledger, the lease focus hold to its lease registry, a local wake write to crates/gterminals/src/write/wake_dispatch.rs::dispatch_wake, and a node terminal's composer to NODEHUB's store. So the native decision replaces Python's dispatcher, and AG-3's live-wake ops are no longer called. Its terminal exit cleanup ends an agent run as src/gobby/agents/terminal_cleanup.py:105 does: it delivers to the parent and calls AG-1's deliver_completion, which AG-WAIT's native service serves from the same activation (D71). The transitions from its exit cleanup and its composer attention go to AG-3's native attention family, which activates at the same time (D72). It also binds AG-3's AttentionHost (crates/gdaemon/src/attention_host.rs) to the native host at the same activation: capture to #24573's runtime snapshot, and local write to gterminals' Coordinator::write with Origin::Attention and action key attention-respond:<attention_id> (S2.7 3.4), so respond's local delivery serves natively with the attention family (D72). The native host's output reader reports each run's output to TERM-1's turn-observer seam, as Python's PTY output callback does (src/gobby/runner_broadcasting.py:148-152; D73). HOOK-2's composer-ledger worker ops and D75's handoff delivery op are terminal worker ops too, so from this activation they are not called either: the hook handlers' terminals seam group binds to the native host (s2-11 7.5). Python's terminal loops stop with Python's host manager when this chunk's route value flips at CP-WAVE5-CUT, and the native host's own tasks replace them: the host event reader (src/gobby/terminals/host_event_reader.py:100), the host health loop (src/gobby/terminals/host_manager.py:881), lease publication (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:311), and the host and frame clients (src/gobby/terminals/host_client.py:323, src/gobby/terminals/frame_client.py:535). It also builds the session liveness job on R4's registry, which no family plan names (src/gobby/sessions/liveness_monitor.py:138-227, 383-481: every 30 seconds on this machine's rows, a session whose terminal exited or whose foreground owner is gone expires conditionally through SES-2's status services, then its hook effects retire through HOOK-3's receipt store, its terminal row is released or marked exited, its summaries dispatch through SES-3B and its processor registration ends). Its tmux branch goes with #25486, so the job reads only native terminals and foreground ownership. Python's in-process suppression (mark_recently_handled, called from the session_end hook, src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_session_end.py:77-79) becomes a check on the row: the job skips a session whose updated_at is younger than Python's _RECENTLY_HANDLED_TTL, because HOOK-2's native session end writes that row. Python's lifespan service serves until CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation registers the job (D98), and S3-DELETE deletes the Python monitor (D14). That exit cleanup also runs AG-2's sandbox reap, in the srt_reap and sandbox_reap phases Python's has (src/gobby/agents/terminal_cleanup.py:157-171), so no Python reap remains after CP-WAVE5-CUT. Its action hold (crates/gterminals/src/hold.rs) also binds the composer lock effect of HOOK-2's handoff delivery services, held across each ladder's reads and writes, and at this activation HOOK-3's composition starts those services in place of Python's delivery, with their dispatch recovery in R3's handoffs slot and their shutdown pass in the ordered stop (D75). A hold lapses 10 seconds after its last step (crates/gterminals/src/hold.rs:15), and a ladder waits longer than that between steps (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_compaction.py:382-405), so this chunk adds a renewal to ActionGate that the ladder adapter calls at each read and each poll of a wait; a holder that dies still lapses in 10 seconds. A reprompt or wake adapter that meets a ladder's hold waits at acquire_action for up to the route's 30 seconds (crates/gterminals/src/write_api.rs:491-553), and a wake batch that finds another of its targets held refuses at once (:703-731). Either then reports not delivered, as a blocked wake does (src/gobby/events/wake.py:883-892): the durable message stays queued, and the watchdog's next pass repeats a reprompt (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/recovery.py:396-397). Operator input is not under Python's lock (src/gobby/terminals/composer_lock.py), and natively it queues behind a hold (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md 2.4 and 2.12), so input typed during a ladder waits for its release, and new input gets the explicit error frame once the oldest queued item has waited 30 seconds (crates/gterminals/src/hold.rs:134-151), a known difference that CP-WAVE5-REVIEW's packet carries. TERM-2's two in-flight ops and D103's, D105's and D110's ops are terminal worker ops too. From this activation every pane reservation is native, native writes reach the host through this chunk's Coordinator, the focus hold reads its registry and a hub-local launch spawns on this chunk's host, so none of them is called, and S3-DELETE deletes them. TERM-1's node write branch (#25201) goes live with Owner mode, so a write to a terminal on another machine stays off this host. It also ports send_keys_target_refusal (#25338) over its composer ledger, #24573's snapshot and the provider detection manifests (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:169-275; crates/gdaemon/src/pane_detection/mod.rs:121), so send_keys and send_wake stop calling TERM-1's gate op at this activation. The Rust test gate is crates/gterminals/tests/host_guard.sh, because one test binary cannot see the hosts another leaks. It lists gterm host processes by their --socket-dir as src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:72-102 does, runs the command it is given, by default cargo nextest run -p gobby-terminals, with TMPDIR set to a fresh short run root (a Unix socket path is limited to 104 bytes, src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:43-45), and then applies the rule of src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:207-238 and tests/terminals/conftest.py:61-75: a host still under the run root is a leak, which it ends, reports with its pid and socket directory and fails on, and a host under the gobby home that was in the first listing and has ended also fails. It replaces only the host checks of guard set G's groups 2, 3 and 7; src/gobby/guard_set_g.py stays until S3-DELETE, whose Terminal Acceptance job runs the crate's suite through this script. Inside a managed run host_guard.sh's run root sits under the run's own TMPDIR, the only place SRT grants Unix sockets, and a host listing that the sandbox hides goes through protocol step 6's route (docs/guides/gterminal-development-guide.md:232-238, 450-458). Four Python fixes also came after the terminal plan, and the native host carries them. Native paste (#23445, #25149): a single write sends text as one paste operation at any length, a submit follows as its own Enter after TMUX_TEXT_ENTER_DELAY_SECONDS, one second, which crates/gterminals/src/native_write.rs:24 already has, and text over 1 MiB raises the typed payload error (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:594-612, 643-668; tests/terminals/test_native_runtime.py:469-479). A batch's text over NATIVE_PASTE_THRESHOLD_CHARS, 2000, goes as one paste operation with a trailing Return as its own key operation PASTE_SUBMIT_DELAY_MS later, and at or under it keeps its single text write (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:68-72, 125-138). crates/gterminals/src/native_write.rs:95-129, 311-318 still sends that text as a text write, which loses a long kickoff's head in Claude Code. Epoch redial (#25175): a spawn commit whose transport failed before the request was written redials the epoch it was prepared on, a failed redial leaves the commit unsent, an epoch mismatch fails typed, and the executor resends once (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:154-158, 405-421; src/gobby/terminals/host_client.py:89-94, 423-445, 778-811; src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:335-350). Composer ledger: record_queued_submit consumes a flagged submit whenever no block is live (#24842), and record_local_command settles a flagged submit when a local slash command's transcript row is written at or after its receipt time, which unconsumed_submit_at reports (#25382) (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:332-364, 366-371, 372-389). record_composer_wipe joins the ledger for HOOK-2's wipe (#25595; src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:557). The native ledger loads and writes Python's <gobby_home>/runtime/composer_ledger.json at state version 1 (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:77, 624-660), so an open terminal's ledger survives this activation and a restored generation reads it back. It also binds its health_state (src/gobby/terminals/host_manager.py:176) to OBS's gterm_host port at that activation, and a host that fails to start marks gterm_host on SEAM-FAMILY's degraded set and records the error on R2's startup-progress row, as Python does (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:288-300). chunks.title: Agent waits and the completion registry
chunks.goal: The event-driven wait_for_* primitives and Python's in-memory completion registry (events/completion_registry.py), single-owner state that moves only once its last Python caller and producer is gone (D19, D71). It takes over the native waiters that AG-2 builds. s2-11's deferred D2 and agents-family's wake and mailbox obligations (:740) land here and in AG-3 (D29). Completion (D71). From its activation (CP-WAVE5-CUT) the native completion service is the only completion owner. It holds AG-2's in-memory waiters, native wait_for_agent and task expansion's in-memory subscribers, whose PLANS seam re-binds to it at that activation, with the caller's lineage read through gsessions, so PLANS' two completion ops are no longer called, and PIPE-2's wait step on an expansion is woken in process, keeping its durable read for a run that ended before it registered (D71). It delivers durable completion_subscribers through AG-3's wake decision, with one owner at a time so that no subscriber row is woken by both, and PIPE-2's delivery for its executions' subscriber rows moves into it. It also takes the startup redelivery of this machine's terminal runs in R3's agents slot, in place of src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py::_cleanup_terminal_agent_completion_subscribers. AG-1's deliver_completion re-binds to it, so AG-1's delivery op and composed-result op are no longer called (D4), and S3-DELETE deletes them. Coordination waits (agents-family 5.3). Registration and cancel reproduce the transactions of src/gobby/storage/coordination_waits.py::CoordinationWaitManager, including the owner lock taken through gsessions' session_rows. The delivery worker ports src/gobby/events/coordination_waits.py::CoordinationWaitService over gcore's new Pool::listen (crates/gcore/src/postgres_pool/listen.rs), which is one connection outside the pool listening on gobby_coordination_wait. The worker takes the recovery snapshot after every listen and retries an undelivered wake after 5 seconds. It is a job on R4's registry that registers only once the family is active (D37). From the same activation R5 no longer starts Python's CoordinationWaitService, so exactly one delivery worker runs. As the family's last activation, AG-WAIT also brings docs/contracts/agents-native.md and docs/guides/agents.md to native operation (agents-family 11.3). wait_for_output keeps Python's polling, pattern and timeout semantics over the pane read effect, with its matched, timed-out and ended-run outcomes (agents-family 2.2.3). This chunk's service answers AG-2's parked check from CP-WAVE5-CUT (D71). Coordination registration and refresh stay at read committed and lock the owner through session_rows before they read its status, so a wait never registers against a stale owner status (agents-family Decision 16 and 5.3.5). Restart recovery (s2-11 D2, #21564): this chunk ports the recovery steps that consume the hook barrier and takes their places in R3's order at CP-WAVE5-CUT: the barrier's classification and fencing (src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py:47-164), fed by HOOK-3's startup pass; agent-run reconciliation (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:45-424, 473-525; src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:158-201, 299-334), which skips fenced runs and which the monitor's reclassification calls for them (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:430-470); and session reconciliation with its excluded ids and recovery-safe flag (src/gobby/events/wake.py:192-212; src/gobby/events/wake_active_recovery.py), whose horizon and exclusions AG-3's native wake decision applies to later wakes (src/gobby/events/wake.py:210-211, 591). Their terminal reads use TERM-HOST's native host, which activates with them. From CP-WAVE4-CUT to this activation those steps stay R3's Python entry points, and the Rust side passes them the native pass's fields. D2.2's deletion of src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py is S3-DELETE's (D14). It also ports the feedback reviewer launch that OBS's review service waits behind (src/gobby/feedback/agent.py:184-364: the configured definition's checks, a native spawn with no checkout through AG-1, the wait on this chunk's completion service and the read of the submitted report). Until then Python's reviewer keeps spawning through its own AgentRunner into Python's terminal host, which moves at this same activation, and native terminal transitions hand its run to Python's completion registry. crates/gdaemon's composition adapts the launch to OBS's reviewer trait, and CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation binds POST /api/feedback/review and the gobby:feedback-review row to OBS's review service, with this chunk's orphaned-run mark in R3's slot, so CRON's feedback worker op and R3's entry point are no longer called, and S3-DELETE deletes them (D14).
