This chunk owns the native relaunch: src/gobby/agents/resume_executor.py::resume_agent_run (:116-726) with src/gobby/agents/resume_executor_settlement.py, resume_finalization.py and resume_placement.py, and the relaunch half of src/gobby/storage/agent_resume.py (refuse_parked_daemon_resume, finalize_daemon_resume, register_daemon_resume_waiter, rollback_prepared_daemon_resume and increment_daemon_resume_failure_count). It launches through AG-1's launch path and spawn effect, re-places a placed run through AG-1's placement or refuses it, never launching it unplaced (resume_placement.py:149-236), moves the old run's completion waits to its successor on this chunk's completion service, emits agent_started with the resumed_from_run_id key and the terminal-created event through AG-1's emit (src/gobby/agents/resume_executor_settlement.py:146-148; src/gobby/storage/daemon_resume_keys.py:23) and sends the relaunched notice through AG-3's recovery notice write. The native relaunch and Python's never run together: R4's op and R3's entry points stop in the activation that starts it, and the rollback recipe returns both (D78). Until that activation Python's relaunch of a placed run keeps its unbound pane in Python's in-flight set (src/gobby/terminals/workspace_agent_panes.py:364; src/gobby/storage/workspaces.py:345), which TERM-2's native WorkspaceOps cannot see when a workspace read sweeps dead panes (workspaces.py:889-930). Python's bind then fails as not_found, the launch is released and the run parks (workspace_agent_panes.py:527-528; src/gobby/agents/resume_placement.py:209-236; src/gobby/agents/resume_executor.py:614-621), and the parked retry counts that against its bound of three failures (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:337, 372-400). TERM-2's worker ops narrow this: its native sweep keeps any NULL-terminal pane in that in-flight set, and a failed op call keeps the pane too, so a native read no longer reaches that bind failure, and the bound stays for Python's other bind failures.

chunks.title: External MCP multiplexer: child pool and bridge
chunks.goal: #25259: the external MCP child pool (stdio, streamable-HTTP and legacy SSE servers over its own rmcp client transports) becomes a Rust-owned single-owner service, with status, refresh, the bridge routes and the tool_call WS message; GW-1/GW-2's proxied external servers switch to native. It runs after the last Python in-process callers of external tools (rule preflight, pipeline MCP steps, hook-driven calls) are native. It does not wait on #25207 (D35). Its first deliverable records the external-MCP corpus and maps #21566's D5 registry rows (19, because tool-timeouts stays while gmcp reads it, D65) to MUX-2; the multiplexer plan was rewritten by 2068aaf9a0 after #25259's commit list. MUX-1 also delivers the multiplexer plan's 1.4 (.gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md, Decision 11): SecretStore::secret_in and set_in in crates/gruntime/src/secrets.rs, absorbing the secrets set that A1-CONFIG's PATCH /api/config/values landed, so its secret updates go through set_in and #24466's 5.9.10 is met by 1.4's consumer test (crates/gruntime/tests/values_patch.rs::secret_updates_use_scoped_secrets_set). It also delivers #24467's 5.10.6 native half: the native POST /api/config/secrets accepts an optional string project_id, absent or null meaning global and a malformed one answered with the route's existing 422 body, and passes it to set_in, with a test that Python's SecretStore.get reads the scoped value back. That test replaces the criterion's crates/gruntime/tests/secret_save.rs::project_scoped_save_matches_python, which assumed Python's pass-through. Python's route is not changed (D4), so the field stays a native extension, inert until V5B's gclient mcp-proxy add-server prompt sends it (multiplexer plan 5.2), and the A1 corpora replay unchanged against the absorbed set. MUX-1 builds the multiplexer plan's hub side (.gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md P1) in crates/gdaemon/src/mcp_client/ (Decision 1). 1.1: Pool, with Decision 6's policy (a changed spec fingerprint replaces the connection; up to three connect retries at 1, 2 and 4 seconds; three failed connects open a 30-second circuit with one half-open probe; a 300-second idle close; one reconnect before a send and no replay after one; no health pings) and Decision 8's call registry (cancel tombstones kept 600 seconds, at most 4,096), the wire types and error codes, which S4-NODE's node handler reuses, and the gdaemon-mcp-fixture test server. Idle close is the pool's own connection timer, not a job. 1.2: the launch environment (${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expansion, offline npx, the chrome_executable_path and loopback_browser hooks, with the loopback config written to <gobby_home>/mcp/browser-loopback.json) and orphan-proof supervision through gdaemon mcp-child -- <argv> (Decision 7), with server stderr in <gobby_home>/logs/mcp-servers.log; a compile-only Windows clippy job in .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml proves the JobObject path, whose runtime proof stays post-1.0 with Windows (83a9445f). 1.3: the client transports (Decision 2): a stdio child through rmcp's TokioChildProcess, streamable HTTP with the spec's headers and the 30-second timeout and 300-second read timeout that Python's client sets (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/transports/http.py::build_mcp_http_client), and legacy SSE as an rmcp Transport, because rmcp ships no legacy SSE client; a 401 from either HTTP transport, at connect or on a request, answers unauthorized with the server's WWW-Authenticate value and drops the connection, and no configured header or environment value reaches a log line, a status entry, an error or Debug output (1.3.4). 1.5: Backend, which registers each call id, applies Decision 9's deadlines and the loopback-browser policy, resolves $secret: references through 1.4's secret_in and fails closed with missing_secrets, calls Pool::request, and cleans results and errors under untrusted_key, the policies Decision 3 gives Rust, without disclosing a resolved value; GW-1's gateway calls it in process, so no route fronts it. Backend::status keeps each server's last outcome from replies, with no health pings (Decision 6): connected after a successful reply; needs_configuration with the missing names after missing_secrets, or with the auth command as its last error after authorization_required (plan 2.1.8); failed with its code after any other failure. GET /api/mcp/status, MUX-2's registry and OBS's GET /api/admin/status report it. 1.6: OAuth on rmcp's auth feature (Decision 4), through an OAuthStore over secret_in and set_in that keeps Python's secret name (mcp_oauth_ plus the sha256 of project_id, id and url joined by newlines, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/oauth.py:166-167), its OAuthState JSON shape and its advisory lock key (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/oauth_keepalive.py::oauth_lock_key), so stored tokens survive the flip with no re-login, and that ports Python's rotated-token reload, shared backoff, consent clearing, refusal to re-register a client and credential-free failure summaries. 1.7: the login subcommand gdaemon mcp-auth <name> [--project-id] [--timeout] [--shape], which V5B's gclient mcp-proxy auth and oauth-shape execute (plan 5.2) once CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit B makes gobby the client; until then Python's gobby mcp-proxy auth keeps its own login on the same secret name, shape and lock key. The native OAuth keepalive (a refresh 600 seconds before expiry on a 60-second tick, under the same lock) is the family's job on R4's registry: it registers only from CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation (D37) and replaces Python's keepalive iteration (refresh_due_oauth_servers, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/oauth_keepalive.py:205-228), which S3-DELETE deletes (D14). From that activation GW-1's native cancel route (#24884's 2.1.9) forwards an external call's cancel to Backend::cancel; the registry keeps the caller's session, so another session's cancel leaves the call running, and a cancelled call answers the ordinary failure payload with error_code CANCELLED (plan 2.2). docs/contracts/mcp-multiplexer.md documents the Pool and Backend APIs, the wire types, error codes and policy, the scoped secret store, and the cancel route and its header. The plan's loopback route (/api/internal/mcp/*, 1.5), Python forwarder (2.1) and Python cancellation (2.2) are not built: Python never calls Rust (D19), and no Python client of a Rust endpoint is written (D4). MUX-1 also does the gateway side of the plan's 2.1, whose Python forwarder is not built. From CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation the gateway dispatches external servers through Backend behind its one policy pass (#24884's 2.1.6), and this chunk turns Backend's replies into the payloads Python's ToolProxyService returns today under #24884's 2.1.5 error contract: timeout as the existing timeout result; circuit_open, connect_failed, transport_closed, server_error, oauth_unavailable and untrusted_key with Python's MCPError messages; missing_secrets with Python's needs-configuration message and the names; authorization_required with its auth command; policy_refused with its message (plan 2.1.2, 2.1.3). A call with no timeout, and every list_tools, read_resource and warm call, takes Decision 9's finite 600,000 ms in place of today's unbounded wait. Each list_tools reply passes through 1.5's browser filter and metadata cleaning and is written where Python's cache_discovered_tools writes (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/client_manager/tool_inventory.py:272-305; src/gobby/storage/mcp_tools.py:49). That is the external tool-inventory cache of #24884's 2.1.9, from which the passive GET /api/mcp/tools read and the external schema_hash serve with the filter reapplied (plan :326-330, :782-784) and with no Python on either path. At that activation OBS's native GET /api/admin/status stops taking its mcp_servers block from Python: this chunk supplies the block's external entries from Backend::status, under Python's field names (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_health.py:449-480), and its internal entries from GW-1's ToolRegistry. Its native POST /api/mcp/refresh re-embeds the new and changed tools it caches, as Python's does (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/registry.py:414-454), so this chunk builds the one native tool vector writer, which MCP-FLIP's routes and tool_embeddings seam then call: the port of Python's embed_tool with its tool text, point payload, stale-point delete and collection ensure and repair (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/semantic_search.py:71-100, 183-230, 406-491), generating through AI-1A's embedding generation (#25095), asserting AI-2's serving lease and writing to each managed projection target the switch journal names through #25542's module, and taking gcore's project fence for the tool's project around each point write (crates/gcore/src/project_fence.rs, PROJ-2), as Python's embed_tool takes its project write context (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/semantic_search.py:417) (D8, D47). A tool point's identity stays Python's after #25488: its id is uuid5 of {server_id}/{tool_name} in the DNS namespace, its payload carries source_id, an existing point's source_id is preserved, and the stale delete filters on server_id and tool_name except that point (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/semantic_search.py:36-41, 455-491; 35d1d1d271).

Teams reverses #24173's Teams drop. iMessage is after 1.0, and gobby_chat is dropped. The connections are single-owner state and move to Rust once every Python sender is native; after CP-WAVE5-CUT, COMMS-1's worker op is no longer called, and S3-DELETE deletes it. The chunk also ports inbound webhooks, attachments on PROJ-2's files_home documents (#21576, D21), identity link, unlink and list, conversation attach, detach and list, send_attachment and send_operator_attachment. It also ports Telegram's question controller (src/gobby/communications/telegram_questions.py), with the callback routing and keyboard edits it uses (src/gobby/communications/manager.py:828; src/gobby/communications/telegram_decisions.py), on CHAT-2's native pending-interaction manager, and CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation re-binds HOOK-3's hold-open to it, so HOOK-3's two Telegram worker ops are no longer called, and S3-DELETE deletes them. Python's comms loops stay in the worker until CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation, and this chunk builds their native counterparts inside its connections: the polling manager (src/gobby/communications/polling.py:106), channel activation retry (src/gobby/communications/lifecycle.py:175), answer retry (src/gobby/communications/responder.py:499) and Discord's gateway and heartbeat (src/gobby/communications/adapters/discord.py:205, :344). The attachment step of Python's comms retention (src/gobby/communications/attachments.py:79) registers on R4's registry at that activation in place of Python's op, and S3-DELETE deletes the op (D14). Session status communications (src/gobby/runner_broadcasting.py:419-453; src/gobby/communications/manager.py:805-820) move with the connections: from CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation the operator-target reconcile and the Telegram target fallback register as a native listener on SES-2's committed status transitions, in place of SES-2's status op (D67). The transcript mirror moves with them: from CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation the message processor's mirror host binds to this chunk's native attachments and outbound (src/gobby/communications/manager.py:257-266, 344-368; src/gobby/communications/transcript_order.py; src/gobby/communications/outbound.py:32), keeping Python's per-block rows, holds, bounded retries and attachment floor, in place of SES-3B's worker ops. It also ports Telegram voice notes on VOICE's crate (#21588, Josh 2026-10-25): inbound transcription (src/gobby/communications/voice.py; src/gobby/communications/inbound.py:250) and outbound speech replies (src/gobby/communications/tts_voice.py; src/gobby/communications/chat_backend.py:145, 180, 290). Telegram's action controller moves here too (src/gobby/communications/telegram_actions.py:34-454). Python builds it with its own MailboxService over Python's wake dispatcher whenever a communications manager exists (src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:286-303), so its inbound session messages and agent menu call Python's dispatcher in process until CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation moves the connections. Natively it sends through AG-3's family API (D29), keeping Python's message type telegram_message, operator-pending message id, preserve_content and wake=true (src/gobby/communications/telegram_actions.py:172-187). It passes replace_composer only for the enrolled operator's attached direct conversation (src/gobby/communications/session_delivery.py:13-33), and after a successful send it completes an operator-pending message and clears that flag (src/gobby/communications/telegram_actions.py:188-192; src/gobby/storage/communications.py:511). This chunk adds replace_composer to AG-3's send, because only this controller passes it: it is refused unless the sender is the system session, the target a session and wake true, and it alone sets the operator_comms metadata that callers cannot set (src/gobby/sessions/mailbox.py:206-211, 284-290), which AG-3's native wake decision reads (src/gobby/events/comms_wake.py:11-21). A responder's decision answer is not sent again, and a mailbox-delivered one only wakes its committed row, best effort (src/gobby/communications/telegram_actions.py:53-62), through a committed-row wake that this chunk also adds to AG-3's family API, as src/gobby/sessions/mailbox.py:352-363 does. send_operator_attachment under daemon-owned execution takes the same grant and refuses a file outside the report directory (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/communications.py:250). The responder's chat turns land here too: ChatSessionCommsBackend (src/gobby/communications/chat_backend.py:119-396, wired at src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:357-371), CommunicationsChatStreamTransport (src/gobby/communications/chat_transport.py:46-245) and the responder's turn queue and commands (src/gobby/communications/responder.py:19, 99-174) become native over CHAT-2's public runtime API. Its settings come from the channel's responder config (agent, chat_mode, project_id, model, provider), a missing agent answers Python's configure message, and typing refresh, passive context limits, outbound session evidence and voice replies keep Python's values (src/gobby/communications/chat_backend.py:136-352, 419-440). Until CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation a comms turn stays on Python's chat runtime in the worker, with the adapter connections it answers. Inbound trust checks port with the adapters, because replay of recorded traffic never sends a forged request (D124). Each adapter's webhook verification keeps Python's refusals: no raw body, an unresolved $secret or a verifier timeout refuses (src/gobby/communications/webhook_verification.py:10-21; src/gobby/communications/inbound.py:335-394). Slack checks its HMAC-SHA256 signature and refuses a timestamp more than five minutes off (src/gobby/communications/adapters/slack.py:383-415), SMS Twilio's HMAC-SHA1 (src/gobby/communications/adapters/sms.py:230-270), Telegram its secret token (src/gobby/communications/adapters/telegram.py:885-892) and Discord its Ed25519 signature (src/gobby/communications/adapters/discord.py:631), in constant time, and email refuses (src/gobby/communications/adapters/email.py:594). Teams verifies the Bot Framework JWT as PyJWT's decode does: RS256 only, a key from the published JWKS fetched with a five-second timeout, audience and issuer present and matching, exp, nbf and iat each checked with no leeway when the token carries them and none of the three required, and an https serviceUrl equal to the activity's (src/gobby/communications/adapters/teams.py:25, 303-345). RS256 and Ed25519 use ring, which Cargo.lock already holds, and the HMACs use the locked hmac, sha1 and sha2 (D125). Inbound access keeps Telegram's allow_from, group policy, inbound mode and operator routing (src/gobby/communications/telegram_access.py; src/gobby/communications/group_policy.py:27-109; src/gobby/communications/inbound_mode.py; src/gobby/communications/operator_routing.py), and Telegram text and captions from a non-private conversation or a forward lose invisible characters through the gobby-core strip that PLANS adds, and a message that held nothing else is discarded (src/gobby/communications/adapters/telegram_inbound.py:345-352). Channels keep the token bucket and backoff (src/gobby/communications/rate_limiter.py; src/gobby/config/communications.py:11). Logs and stored errors keep redact_and_bound and the bot-token scrub on AG-1's redact_terminal_output (src/gobby/communications/redaction.py; src/gobby/communications/adapters/telegram.py:146-178, 304; src/gobby/communications/lifecycle.py:127). The Telegram proxy accepts only http, socks5 and socks5h (src/gobby/communications/telegram_proxy.py:6-46), through reqwest's socks feature, attachments keep the safe filename and the route's 413 (src/gobby/communications/attachments.py:124-126; src/gobby/servers/routes/communications.py:150-153), and email takes lettre and async-imap (D125). This chunk's consumer commit renames the listeners at web/src/components/activity/IntegrationsTab.tsx:82 and web/src/hooks/useIntegrations.ts:227 from comms_event to communications_event, the type Python and this chunk publish (src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:602-609), because nothing sends comms_event and the tab's live refresh has never run. A known difference for Josh's go: operator input typed during a ladder queues behind its hold, and new input gets the explicit error frame once the oldest queued item has waited 30 seconds, where Python's lock let it through. It also has AG-WAIT's native relaunch in place of R4's parked retry op and HOOK-2's finalize op, with its relaunch cases (D78), and AG-WAIT's service in place of PLANS' two completion ops and AG-1's composed-result delivery op (D71). The attention corpus replay reads AG-3's fixture copy of attention.get-roster.no-response-cache and attention.get-roster.publish-after-commit, and the websocket refusal cases read MUX-2's fixture copy, and CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit lands those entries and citations (D84). An adapter P0-LOWTRAFFIC could not verify for lack of an account shows as not run: no account (D100). The activation list also flips SEAM-WS's leg-free default, and the packet carries its recorded WS cases replayed with that default on, no worker bound and no private leg opened (D102). Its full-daemon proof shows GET /api/health's native body under gclient's startup, gmcp and gobby status with the worker serving, and the typed 503 with it stopped, with no request reaching the worker. The prepared commits that CP-WAVE5-CUT lands also include COMMS-2's consumer commit. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-WAVE5-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes from 0.9.0-gg as D40 item 3 defines them; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-WAVE5; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: the single-owner switches and the MCP flip go live
chunks.goal: Category code. Activates the single-owner switches and MCP-FLIP. Afterwards the activated build sends Python no request beyond the worker's startup phases (D83) and its stop, and calls no worker op, although gdaemon still starts the Python worker until CP-PREDELETE-CUT. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. The external MCP pool and the comms adapters keep their state in PostgreSQL and files_home, which the backup covers. The embedding switch that this cut activates writes Qdrant collections and aliases and, through the memories seam, FalkorDB entity vectors; hub-backup snapshots both but restores only PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348), so the rehearsal runs its switch on scratch containers restored by hand from this backup's Qdrant snapshot and FalkorDB RDB, as CP-WAVE3-CUT's rehearsal does (ruling 17, D52). (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137). Run hub-backup restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database; it covers PostgreSQL and files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:272-348). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:220; src/gobby/storage/secrets.py:399-414), and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings (src/gobby/config/persistence.py:164-171) at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose file's fixed-name volumes (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:104-107), empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation, with its Python while Python exists, starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build replays the host-restart corpus (stop the daemon, keep the panes, reattach) and the wait, external MCP pool and comms corpora, writing terminal ownership, composer, wait and channel rows. The external MCP and adapter proofs run against REC-MEMORY-COMMS' fixture MCP servers and fixture adapters registered into the scrubbed copy, never the live ones. The pinned gdaemon then boots against the activation commit's tree: it latches the old terminal route, TERM-1's helper makes Python follow it, Python's host manager starts and reattaches the panes, the external MCP children restart under Python's pool and the fixture adapters reconnect. The rehearsal opens one test pane under the pinned generation before its promotion and records in the window plan whether open panes survive that forward owner change and that hand-back. If Josh refused TERM-1's helper at map approval, the rehearsal runs D19's rollback order instead (step 9) and proves that the restored gdaemon's Python child starts. It also runs one embedding switch from start to active on the scrubbed copy, against scratch Qdrant and FalkorDB containers restored by hand from step 4's backup and an embedding stub, and the restored generation reads back the switch journal and the switched collections. It also replays REC-WORKFLOWS' report and report-settlement cases against the native report route, store and reconciler, and the pinned gdaemon's Python report route accepts the next report after the hand-back. It also replays REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' attention cases against the native attention family, including the turn reducer's published transitions (D73). After the hand-back, the pinned generation's Python attention store serves the next transition under a new epoch. The coordination and completion delivery cases replay against the native service. The wake and reprompt cases replay over the native host, with one action hold across each probe and write (D74). HOOK-2's compact and clear delivery cases replay over the native host too, with one action hold across each ladder's reads and writes (D75), and AG-WAIT's relaunch cases replay with a parked run and its successor (D78). SEAM-WS's recorded WS cases also replay on the restored copy with its leg-free default on and no private leg opened (D102). (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:27-44; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153). The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The terminal host moves to Rust: the compiled terminal ownership default that TERM-1 separated flips to Native, which moves RouteLatch to Owner and GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE to native; the terminal routes have been Native since CP-WAVE1-CUT. In CP-WAVE1-CUT's fallback, where TERM-1 could not separate them, this one flip is TerminalFamily's default backend (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:43-55; crates/gcore/src/route_family.rs:28-31) and moves both together. Python follows the latched value through TERM-1's helper, so the commit carries no Python line (D19). The terminal, release_composer, pane-wake and pane-input worker ops are no longer called. Waits, the external MCP pool and registry, and the comms adapter connections flip to Native, and COMMS-1's adapter-send op is no longer called. MCP-FLIP's front-door flip serves /mcp with no Python backend; the backend entry stays in code until S3-DELETE. The ai-embedding-switch family default flips to Native, which is #25118's activation and release, now that MCP-FLIP composes both collection rebuild seams (D52). The activation restart starts only when GET /api/embeddings/switch/status reports no running task: a live run first finishes at active or is aborted (AI plan 7.6). NODEHUB's compiled reported-pane default flips to Native with the terminal host (D19): POST /api/nodes/report and POST /api/nodes/runs/terminate serve natively, its reported pane store and node report inbox replace Python's, its run reconciler swaps the reconcile op AG-2 registered on R4's registry, and AG-2's idle reads and TERM-HOST's node terminal reads use its store, so AG-2's three node-report worker ops are no longer called. AG-WAIT's native completion service takes AG-1's deliver_completion, so AG-1's delivery op and AG-2's is_awaiting op are no longer called, and durable completion_subscribers delivery and startup redelivery become native (D71). Its coordination-wait delivery worker registers on R4's registry, and R5 no longer starts Python's CoordinationWaitService. AG-3's attention family default flips to Native (D72): the four /api/attention/ routes, transitions, the ordering cursor, the metadata store and publication. chunks.title: Checkpoint review: retiring Python from the live daemon
chunks.goal: Review pause before Python stops running. Its cutover makes the live generation Python-free: gdaemon stops starting the Python worker, the gclient verbs replace the Python CLI, and gclient takes the gobby name. Packet: The seven verb chunks' goldens (V1A, V1B, V2, V3, V4, V5A, V5B) through the renamed binary; S3-FREEZE's frozen corpora and its ledger closure (every row native, delegated or dropped, none proxied); the full-daemon proof on the release build with no Python worker, over every frozen corpus plus a bounded soak loop; V1A's Rust promotion and rollback verbs rehearsed in a temp home; CP-WAVE5-CUT's window record. The irreversible consequence for Josh's go: once S3-DELETE lands after this cutover's window, no generation from before this cutover can be restored. The activation is two commits in one window: commit A (gdaemon's backend default, the gclient bump that ships V1A's verbs, and S3-NAME's gobby-name installer constant turned on, which installs gclient under both names; the recipe's restore removes the installed gobby name), promoted with the Python CLI, then commit B (the console script leaves pyproject.toml, the instruction files switch to gobby, release.yml and its PyPI publish go, and release-gclient.yml ships the client as gobby with release.yml's CI gate and Homebrew tap dispatch, while CI runs on gclient-v* tags instead of v* tags, D55) once gobby --version resolves to the new gclient. From this cutover on, no HTTP route has a Proxy backend, so the deactivation path of D36 phase 3 is gone (D36 phase 4). The deep rollback to Python after S3-DELETE, and its cost: revert S3-DELETE's commit and both of this cutover's commits on 0.9.0 with fresh version bumps; if CP-FINAL-CUT's drops have landed, also revert its activation commit, and POST-CLEAN's if it landed, and replace each drop migration file with a no-op migration of the same number, which keeps later numbers and the embedded schema identity valid and drops nothing on the restored backup (the one named exception to D22's rule that applied migrations are never edited, because the restore discards the hub that applied them); if CP-FINAL-CUT's drops have landed, first restore CP-FINAL-CUT's backup with the daemon stopped; then rebuild and promote the reverted tree with uv run python -m gobby.cli cutover --path <main checkout>. It costs a revert of about 1.6 million deleted lines (582,631 src and 1,056,889 test), a full rebuild, a multi-hour outage and every write since that backup. Outside this repository, GobbyAI/homebrew-tap's gobby formula must install the client archive, with its version_scheme raised, before the first gclient-v* tag after commit B (D55), through the pull request CP-NODE-REVIEW's session opens (D127). Under D60's default the tap's gobby formula also carries gdaemon, gcode, ghook, gterm and gmcp, as resources from their own releases, and its four helper formulae retire. None of those members has a release at its pinned version today, and Josh's publication at .gobby/plans/node-install-enrollment.md E1 gate 3 is the first that does, so until then a Homebrew gobby stays unable to run a daemon, as it is today. This review's replay of REC-CLI's goldens through the renamed binary reads V5B's fixture copy of projects.files-migrate.final-layout for gobby files migrate, and CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A lands the real entry and its citation (D48). The full-daemon proof includes R6's no-worker restart form (D68) and V1A's and V1B's gdaemon subcommands (D69). The prepared commits that CP-PREDELETE-CUT lands ahead of commit A include S3-NAME's template commit, with its search result: uv run gobby left only in the consolidation rule's allow list (D39). Every other CLI golden that a family plan gives an entry, such as V3's five clone entries and V5A's cron.cli-* entries, also replays through the renamed binary over its chunk's fixture copy, and commit A lands the real entries and citations (D84). A known short-lived difference: between commit A's promotion and commit B, uv run gobby restart exits 1 on R6's null backend_pid while the restart proceeds (src/gobby/cli/daemon_lifecycle.py:596-599), and the cut's window does not count it as a trigger. Commit A's gdaemon ignores GOBBY_BACKEND_COMMAND, the cut's recipe restores with the Python CLI, and a Python console script ahead of the new gobby on PATH is renamed right after commit A's promotion and deleted at the cut's close. They also include V1A's prepared commit, with the bundled gclient-commands.md and admin/daemon.md references, listed ahead of S3-NAME's template commit, which takes the next PATCH version of admin/daemon.md when the cut's branch is prepared (A17-TEMPLATES). Its full-daemon proof also boots with the worker default off on a fresh hub that holds only V1B's install identity and on a restored copy, showing R2's no-worker start form with its machine row and system session, A1-CONFIG's publisher (the first boot before admission, a live and a restart_required write), GET /api/health's 200 with no worker, R6's fall-through 404 and a WS upgrade on an unclaimed path, the break_glass file, and every documented log file receiving its records. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-PREDELETE-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes from 0.9.0-gg as D40 item 3 defines them; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-PREDELETE; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: the live daemon runs without Python
chunks.goal: Category code. After this cutover the live generation is Python-free. Its window holds the acceptance smoke that step 7 lists. Its activation is two commits in the same window (commit A, then commit B), because the Python console script must outlive commit A's promotion. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:365-380; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with gobby hub-backup: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:123-126, 455-485). hub-backup stops the live daemon and starts it again (cli.py:228-240, 262-267), and its stop runs the protected-run admission that GEN-ROLLBACK adds, as cutover's does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:210-235). From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. This is the last backup taken while the Python worker still exists in the checkout, and it is taken with the Python CLI's gobby hub-backup, because V1A's Rust verbs are installed only by commit A's promotion. (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because hub-backup restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names (src/gobby/cli/postgres_backup.py:358-390), and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries (src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml:7, 41, 67-72). Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:28-69, 123-302; tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:72-137).
