The drop migration set itself is an irreversible step for Josh's go: a rollback is a backup restore that loses every write made after CP-FINAL-CUT's backup, through its window. The deep rollback to Python and its cost, as in CP-PREDELETE-REVIEW's packet: revert S3-DELETE's commit and CP-PREDELETE-CUT's two commits with fresh version bumps; if CP-FINAL-CUT's drops have landed, also revert its activation commit, and POST-CLEAN's if it landed, and replace each drop migration file with a no-op migration of the same number, which keeps later numbers and the embedded schema identity valid and drops nothing on the restored backup (the one named exception to D22's rule that applied migrations are never edited, because the restore discards the hub that applied them); restore CP-FINAL-CUT's backup first if its drops have landed; then rebuild and promote with uv run python -m gobby.cli cutover --path <main checkout>; about 1.6 million deleted lines, a full rebuild, a multi-hour outage and every write since that backup. CP-FINAL-CUT's activation also turns on PROJ-2's 4.6 recovery journal and commit witness (D47). CP-FINAL-CUT's activation commit also adds #25058's two cross-store-recovery waiver entries with the journal flip (D47), and its step 3 seat reviews a literal search of crates/ for project.json, which may find only identity reads, ghook's hooks_disabled read, gprojects' own paths, tests and reads through PROJ-1's metadata guard (D63). For Josh's go, as an accepted contract change: that commit also removes code_index.maintenance_log_file with its settings field, its frozen cases and any stored row through a destructive migration, an irreversible step this go covers, after which the cut runs gobby ui build through V1B's native verb (D65). The prepared commits that CP-FINAL-CUT lands include S3-DELETE's template commit, which takes the commands that only Python could run out of the template tree and rewrites the paths and links that the move and the deletion leave stale, with its search and link results (D39). Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-FINAL-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes from origin/0.9.0-gg (D40 item 3), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-25), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes from 0.9.0-gg as D40 item 3 defines them; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-FINAL; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml, under assets/shared since S3-DELETE moved the templates). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: dead tables and columns are dropped
chunks.goal: Category code. Drops the tables and columns that are dead now that Python is gone (ruling 17), under this cutover's backup. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (AG-WAIT's native wait_for_coordination); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the local CLI bearer token that the native admin route requires, and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, as V1A's restart and cutover verbs require. Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with V1A's gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with B0-CLOSE's native set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because land_commit refuses that SHA without it and its path scope covers every linked commit, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes 0.9.0-gg instead and has no run to check, because neither required workflow runs on that branch. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with V1A's gclient hub-backup verb, which archives the same artifacts as the Python verb it replaced: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken. It stops the live daemon and starts it again, and its stop runs the same protected-run admission as cutover's. From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. This cutover's rollback depends on it, because binaries cannot undo the drops. (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup with V1A's restore, which covers PostgreSQL and files_home, into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because that restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names, and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on A on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries. Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home, as V1A's hub-backup checks. Run the restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database. The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it and cannot be unwrapped otherwise, and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose stack's fixed-name volumes, empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step). If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The activated build applies the drop migrations to the restored backup and replays every frozen corpus. The pinned generation cannot run on the migrated schema, because the drop receipts above its head are destructive, which every gate still refuses (D22; crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:156-160). So the rehearsal proves the other path: restore the backup into a fresh isolated hub, start the pinned generation on it, and read back rows written before the backup. It also checks that the pinned generation reads no checkout path that S3-DELETE moved; templates are embedded at build time by gobby-assets. The rehearsal also starts the pinned generation against a worktree at 0.9.0 HEAD, which has no Python tree, and shows it serving and syncing zero template row changes, because step 4's backup restart runs that pairing live first. The activated build replays #25058's cited cases as Waived with the journal on, and the deactivation build, which reverts them with the journal default, replays those cases against their recordings (D47). (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). Then land the prepared commits, any regeneration commit and the activation commit with one land_commit on the activation commit's SHA, all exactly as step 3 reviewed them and step 5 rehearsed them, under the freeze as the hold's owner, because land_commit refuses a landing whose migrations or schema assets arrive without the schema identity pin (D22); a change to any of them after the rehearsal reruns the seat and the rehearsal first. Schema inputs and post-TPL templates land only here, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's schema pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (V1A's hub-backup verb keeps that proof). The activation commit flips only this stage's code defaults, a family default including the per-tool defaults of that family's MCP tools unless this cut's own text keeps a tool behind, and bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook (whose pins are runtime floors) and the unpublished gmcp, gclient and gterm included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (V1A's version pins); it is the shipping commit for every stamped binary but gdaemon, which landings bump (D39). After the landing, check that 0.9.0 HEAD equals the landed activation SHA; if another commit slipped in, record its SHAs on the task, confirm each is dormant under D37 and add them to the window evidence before promoting. A cutover activates only a commit whose CI is green (D34), so wait for each run the push started of the workflow named CI and of .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml, which the freeze keeps any later push from cancelling (D85); a path filter, or an adoption on A, can leave none to wait for. A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. A push or a run that a GitHub outage delays only delays this step, so the session retries the push on each later wake and keeps the hold and the pin alive meanwhile. Then promote 0.9.0 HEAD with V1A's gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token>, from an unspawned, operator-opened session. The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The activation commit is a schema step with drops (D22): migrations for the pruner's tables (#24711; migration 470 is already taken by 470_validation_run_records.sql, so it takes the next free number at landing) and for the census-listed dead Python-only tables and columns, with the pin generated from a real build and the catalog manifest regenerated. The gobby_chat channel rows are deleted too if no generation reads them (D28). This promotion is also S3-DELETE's first: gdaemon without the backend supervisor's Python spawn, and the template tree embedded from assets/shared, go live together with the drops. PROJ-2's compiled default for 4.6's recovery journal and commit witness turns on, so PUT and PATCH /api/projects/{project_id} and every native writer on 4.6's publication service journal their project.json updates from here on, with no Python reader or writer of project.json left (D47). (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (AG-WAIT's native wait). (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. chunks.title: Checkpoint cutover: Stage 4 goes live and the live node is updated
chunks.goal: Category code. Activates Stage 4: node enrollment, signed releases, node install and update, the node code index, node hooks, remote attach and the hub view. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (AG-WAIT's native wait_for_coordination); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the local CLI bearer token that the native admin route requires, and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, as V1A's restart and cutover verbs require. Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); decisions.question: Landing mechanism for chunk tasks on 0.9.0.
decisions.recommended_default: 0.9.0 is the integration branch, and the main checkout moves to it (ruling 15). Chunk tasks land with ordinary land_commit onto 0.9.0, because land_commit and its git hook target the main checkout's current branch (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:146-152; src/gobby/cli/installers/git_hooks.py:103), and P's main checkout sits on 0.9.0. The start gate also moves project_policy's integration branch from 0.5.0 to 0.9.0 (.gobby/workflows/rules/project-operating-policy.yaml:33, with a rule-17 bump), which only seat procedures and the injected policy text read. Each chunk works in its own task worktree off 0.9.0, for example 0.9.0-rust. Option A (a subtree landing target) and option B (close at cutover) are not built, and nothing merges into 0.9.0 from another branch: P's Python fixes, POST-CLEAN and Stage 4 all land on 0.9.0, A's fixes arrive only as reviewed cherry-picks, and only A merges, taking checkpoint tags into 0.9.0-gg (D40). The landing session pushes 0.9.0 to origin after each land, so the port branch always has an off-machine copy. A cutover session is unspawned and pushes for itself after each landing it makes; a spawned session's push goes through the port dispatcher (D116).
decisions.rationale: Josh: 'we're not merging back into 0.5.0. 0.9.0 will become the new working branch we'll merge into, and you'll be working in a worktree like 0.9.0-rust'. Ordinary landing keeps land_commit's landing lock, ancestry and clean-tree checks, all five close gates per chunk and blocked_by readiness, with no new landing code. The cost is lost isolation: the live daemon runs from the 0.9.0 checkout, so every landed commit reaches it at the next restart, which the live-checkout constraints and dormancy (D37) address. Order between chunks comes from one blocks edge per depends_on entry among the chunk tasks, which readiness honors, and from gport start, which refuses a chunk until every depends_on task has closed as done and, except for a review, its commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD.

decisions.question: Comms order (#25597 puts comms right after R0 and its seams; the 2026-10-25 edges make comms wait) and the close of #22340.
decisions.recommended_default: COMMS-1 in wave 3 after R5, AG-3 and its recorded corpus, with sends through a worker op, live at CP-WAVE3-CUT; COMMS-2 (adapter connections, inbound webhooks, attachments, identities) in wave 5 after the last Python in-process sender, live at CP-WAVE5-CUT. #25597's early order is not adopted. decisions.rationale: #25597 put comms early so that a broken comms port could roll back to the prior binary. GEN-ROLLBACK's retained generations now give every checkpoint that rollback (D38), so the early order buys nothing. Comms has no oracle until P0-LOWTRAFFIC records one, and adapter connections are single-owner state that cannot run in two implementations.

decisions.recommended_default: Only: tests/ and scripts/ for recording, and scripts/port/ for the port's checks (start gate); the R0-R6 worker package and runner edits; one-line allow-listed worker-op registrations for single-owner services, added by the Rust caller's chunk; GEN-ROLLBACK's promotion, rollback, landing-freeze-owner, hub-backup admission and protected-runs answer modules (D38); R-RETIRE's runner refusal; TERM-1's dormant terminal route helper (D19); GW-2's dormant loopback compatibility endpoint (D26); S3-NAME's dormant gobby-name installer constant, which CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A turns on, and its prepared packaging edits, made in commit B; SCHEMA-WINDOW's preflight edit (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py, reached through src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py only at restart, cutover, hub-backup and pack), a prepared commit that CP-RUNNER-CUT lands (D22); S3-DELETE; and bug fixes and friction fixes, which land on 0.9.0 (rulings 6 and 15). The Rust side stops calling a worker op at the activation that replaces it, and S3-DELETE deletes the op, because pinned and retained generations still call it. Every Python edit other than a bug fix, R-RETIRE's refusal (inert for the gdaemon-launched worker, which always carries the marker) and GEN-ROLLBACK's generation-retaining promotion (live at landing, so the generation each cutover pins is already retained) is dormant: behaviorally inert at landing, because new CLI processes and lazily imported modules run it at once. No per-family deletion of surfaces or domain modules, no Python client of a Rust endpoint, no modernization (af4be945). Also allowed, each under its own decision: D41's closure-policy op and shim; D47's fence half (src/gobby/projects/write_fence.py, src/gobby/storage/hub/postgres.py, src/gobby/runner_init/services.py), a prepared commit; D67's communications status op and shim; D68's restart start-proof entry in R6's worker package; D70's read of R5's start list in src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py's pending-interaction expire; D74's composer_locked_write op and shim; D75's handoff delivery op and shim; D81's web chat lifecycle op and shim; D82's after-tool phase in GW-2's preflight op and shim; D98's edit of src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py's three loop starts; D99's calls to the existing track_proxy_outcome and maybe_repair_output in GW-2's op shim and compatibility endpoint; D103's terminal_operator_write op and shim; D105's terminal_focus_changed op and shim; D110's agent_runtime_spawn op and shim; D121's daemon-owned execution and pipeline execution id fields on GW-2's compatibility endpoint. Each is dormant at landing or lands as a prepared commit, as its decision says, and S3-DELETE deletes it. D64's project.json fix sits in the bug-fix clause.
decisions.rationale: Keeps Python whole and equal to its recorded behavior, so differential replay stays valid and every retained generation still finds the Python code it calls. Worker ops are the cheapest correct path for single-owner services while their Python callers remain (ruling 9).
decisions.status: Default. It exceeds ruling 6 (port mechanics in Python), so Josh approves it with the map.

decisions.question: #21559 materialize_managed_launch and the rotate_due loop: the runtime plan keeps them in Python, but Stage 3 deletes Python.

decisions.question: What is the pilot's compare soak?
decisions.recommended_default: Two stages. First, CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW runs the bounded in-session replay soak: three passes of P0-HARNESS's soak loop over the committed REC-PILOT corpus, weighted by the gport shapes census, then differential and dual-run write replay of the whole corpus in the full-daemon harness, judged by D17. Then CP-TEMPLATE-CUT runs the live Compare day: the tasks and runtime families run in Compare on the live daemon for one full active day, so callers always get Python's answer (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:186-254) while gdaemon compare-report scores real traffic. A 72h soak runs only if Josh asks, as a detached process between chunks with no claim held. The real-data corpus (a pg_dump of the hub DB without secrets tables, restored into the test hub, never committed) stays off unless Josh approves it. CP-WAVE3-REVIEW's soak is bounded the same way, with an optional detached 24h run. Later families always get differential replay, and each wave's cutover window is its live observation.
decisions.rationale: Josh's pilot asks for 'a full compare soak'. Ruling 14's checkpoint cutovers make a live Compare window possible with no new machinery: Compare already gives callers Python's answer and logs every diff, so the live day adds real interleavings and agent load that a replay cannot see, at no risk to callers. A 72h soak inside a chunk session would hold a claim for days on waits bounded at 3,600 s (#25635), and #25460 v2 had already made it optional. The snapshot copies private data, so Josh opts in.

decisions.question: When is ported Python deleted, given the 1,172-module lazy-import cycle?
decisions.recommended_default: All at once in S3-DELETE, after S3-FREEZE and after CP-PREDELETE-CUT has made the live generation Python-free; no per-family deletion of surfaces or domain modules. Flagged: this reverses approved per-family deletion leaves (memory #25562 and #25563, code-index #24709, #24710 and #24713, cron #25035, s2-11 P7, #25499, and #24356's wrapper deletion; the memory plan with per-family deletion was approved on 2026-11-02). Each becomes 'stop serving and freeze' at its family's activation, and the deletion lands in S3-DELETE.
decisions.rationale: Josh: 'Yes, it can be deleted in one go, or we can strangler fig it.' One go is the cheaper of the two here: every pinned and retained generation before CP-PREDELETE-CUT still runs Python from the checkout, so a per-family deletion would break generation rollback (D38). Differential replay against Python is the drift oracle until S3-FREEZE. Still-Python callers reach MCP descriptors and managers in-process. Partial deletion inside the 1,172-module lazy-import cycle breaks untested lazy-import paths at runtime. Unreachable Python routes are harmless while the family's backend is Native.
decisions.resolved_by: ruling 14 permits it; one go is the map's default

decisions.question: Homes for port tooling, bundled templates and pin authority.
decisions.recommended_default: crates/gport (dev-only, never promoted) replaces the Python ledger generator and the scripts/port/ checks, and holds start, check-slice, census and shapes. gport start refuses a chunk until every depends_on task is closed with closed_reason done and, for every kind except checkpoint, its linked commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD. A gobby-assets crate embeds the template tree at build time (build.rs include_bytes!, no new dependency) and moves it to assets/shared at S3-DELETE, with TPL as the single loader and sync owner. Pin and promotion authority, with GEN-ROLLBACK's generation store, window hold and rollback verb (D38), moves to Rust in V1A. #24999's asset script is not built, and S3-FREEZE copies the SRT inputs into gobby-assets for S4-INSTALL's #24866.

decisions.question: Who owns the 327 operator CLI rows?

decisions.question: Calibration gate thresholds for CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW and CP-WAVE3-REVIEW.
decisions.recommended_default: Proceed when the D11 rate (partial+stub)/(done+partial+stub) is at most 5% of owned rows, the final replay pass has zero unexplained compare mismatches with every mismatch class triaged (fixed, known-bad, or an accepted contract change), and differential replay is 100% equal or classified. Cost data (session hours, tokens, checkpoints, Rust test lines and Python lines per checkpoint, recording cost per case, and cost against relief) resizes later chunks. The gate's result goes into the review packet. A failure is a no-go: a follow-up commit and a re-run of the replay soak, and a second failure means re-planning with Josh. D11 here and in the checkpoint packets names .gobby/plans/task-25341.md's fan-out gate (:131-135), not this map's D11; gport check-slice --report prints the rate from each chunk's status file (P0-RECORD).
decisions.rationale: Josh's pilot asks for a full compare soak and a measured partial/stub rate before fan-out, and thresholds turn the measurement into a gate. #25460 v2 had made the D11 gate and the 72h soak paperwork optional after B0. This map keeps the D11 gate before fan-out because its angle is oracle-first, runs the bounded replay soak of D13 in place of a 72h soak, and keeps the paperwork to gport's D11 report plus one compare-report summary.

decisions.question: Known-bad policy for Python-recorded oracles.
decisions.recommended_default: Rust implements the correct value, never python_observed. Shell-guard items in the friction queue are fixed first (start gate); the rest are registry rows. A fix that lands on 0.9.0 later retires its row in the same commit and re-records the affected cases. A row covers a difference below any one ledger surface; a difference on one exact surface takes a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry instead (D84).
decisions.rationale: Josh item 4; parity means contracts, not accidents (settled item 5).

decisions.question: Coexistence rules while Python and Rust implementations share 0.9.0.
decisions.recommended_default: Shared DB tables may have two implementations: the corpus proves equal DB deltas, Rust tolerates every Python-written row, both use the same lock keys and notify channels, and Rust emits the events Python caches listen for. Single-owner live state has one owner at a time and moves after its last Python in-process caller (callers before callees). Rust calls Python only through existing endpoints or allow-listed worker ops; Python never calls Rust. A stricter invariant needs a DB constraint Python already satisfies. Because the main checkout runs 0.9.0 (ruling 15), coexistence is live from CP-RUNNER-CUT on (runner job, recovery and lease rows), and from CP-MCP-CUT for the gateway's schema lease rows, not only in tests. A value that gdaemon hands to Python, such as the worker marker or the terminal route GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE (crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:160-169), is a child-contract value set only by gdaemon's compiled defaults, and Python follows the value gdaemon latches: TERM-1's dormant helper makes both of Python's terminal route reads use the latched value (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:83; src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:65-69), so an activation flips only gdaemon's default and a gdaemon-alone restore hands the old value back in one restart. If Josh refuses that Python edit, the activation flips Python's two reads with gdaemon's default, and the rollback lands the deactivation commit under the freeze as the hold's owner, then restores the pinned generation, then promotes the deactivation build under the token, because Python refuses to start when the two disagree (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:80-91); any other value gdaemon hands Python needs the same order. For project files the shared lock is the owner-only sidecar flock that Python's project initialization takes (src/gobby/utils/durable_file.py:26-38), and for derived writes scoped to a project it is gcore's project fence, which Python's ProjectWriteFence takes through its Python half (D47). S3-DELETE deletes TERM-1's helper with the rest of src/gobby.
decisions.rationale: Answers the cross-family and shared-table questions without any Python client of a Rust endpoint and without dual-mode machinery, and keeps every retained generation's Python able to start against the checkout it finds.

decisions.question: Rows dropped at ledger closure.
decisions.recommended_default: Drop the FastAPI docs, redoc and openapi rows (8; the Rust API is documented in docs/contracts), test-types and test-quality CLI (5; no Python tests remain), /api/admin/test/* (4; a harness feature), and /_gobby/ws/bridge (1; dies with Python). Keep the recorded drops #25449 (4), #19319 (1) and tasks compact and clean (#25499, 5). Josh approves each class. D66 adds one more class: gobby sessions renumber and backfill-context-windows (2).
decisions.rationale: None of these is a product surface once Python retires.

decisions.question: #25269, #25201 and #21576 would reverse approved Stage 4 placements.
decisions.recommended_default: Move their Python-surface parts to Stage 2 owners: #25269's hub side to NODEHUB, #25201 to TERM-1 (keep hub-mode's remote write branch), #21576 to COMMS-2 on PROJ-2's files_home documents. Node-side parts stay in Stage 4. #25269's hub side activates at CP-WAVE5-CUT, and its remote idle decision runs in AG-2 (D11).

decisions.question: Migration policy on the live 0.9.0 checkout.
decisions.recommended_default: Migrations are expand-only until CP-FINAL-CUT: a migration adds tables, columns or indexes that Python ignores, together with the GRANT and REVOKE statements on the objects it creates. Schema inputs (migrations with their assets.rs entries, baseline.sql, the pin and the catalog manifest) land only inside a checkpoint cut, in its step 6: after the verified backup (4) and the rehearsal (5), immediately before the activation commit, under the same freeze; the rehearsal builds from the cutover branch, where those commits sit under the activation commit. They cannot land before the backup, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265, via src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:67-77), and between cuts the same check would refuse every session's restart. Each schema-carrying chunk (B0-WRITE, SKILLS, CRON, PLANS and PROJ-2, and SES-2 only if Found Work gives it a schema input, because the sessions plan adds none) lands its dormant code at its own landing and closes; its schema inputs and the tests that need the new schema form one prepared commit, reviewed with the chunk, on the append-only branch port/prepared/<chunk id>, recorded by SHA at its close, and the first cut whose activation needs that schema, Compare included, lands it. Dependent chunks apply it only in their isolated harness. The carrying chunk's own tests that need its schema travel in its prepared commit, and a dependent that lands before that cut puts its own schema-dependent tests in its own prepared commit, which the same cut lands after the upstream one (chunk protocol step 8). The cut assembles its branch before the rehearsal: the prepared commits in packet order, each migration renumbered to the next free number, except one that a rollback reverted, which keeps its number and bytes (below), one commit regenerating baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, then the activation commit; the deactivation commit reverts all of them. Step 6 lands the whole sequence with one land_commit on the activation SHA, because land_commit refuses a landing that changes migrations, baseline.sql or assets.rs without src/gobby/storage/schema_expected_identity.json (src/gobby/tasks/landing_policy.py:76-91). If the cut's promotion refuses after they landed, the session lands the deactivation commit under the freeze before clearing it, so every session's restart passes again (ruling 15). From CP-RUNNER-CUT on, every retained generation accepts a hub ahead by expand-only receipts (SCHEMA-WINDOW), so a rollback across an expand step is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, which reverts the cut's schema inputs so that the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, with no data loss; a later cut re-lands the same migration file in its step 6 (the retry after Josh's reassessment, or the next cut that needs it), whose receipt then matches. Drops, and every other step outside the expand set, are destructive migrations, carrying the -- gobby:destructive directive and the filename marker that SCHEMA-WINDOW pairs with it and lints for. They happen only at CP-FINAL-CUT and POST-CLEAN, each an irreversible step with its own go from Josh, and rollback there is that cut's backup restore. The other rules stay: each migration transactional, with no transaction control, inside the 5 s lock and 60 s statement limits (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:56-92); numbers taken serially at landing, each above both the checkout's highest migration and the highest receipt on the live hub (SELECT max(version) FROM schema_migrations), because an expand migration that a rollback reverted keeps its receipt; such a migration keeps its number and bytes for good: it is re-landed byte for byte even if its direction is abandoned, and any correction is a new migration; applied migrations never edited, except that the deep rollback to Python replaces each drop migration with a no-op of the same number on a restored backup that predates it (CP-PREDELETE-REVIEW); tests run with GOBBY_TEST_GDAEMON=checkout; the pin generated from a real build (src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:113-131); the catalog manifest regenerated (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:238-270). Nobody stops and starts to get around a restart refusal. Node-commands contract versions take the next free version at landing, so no Stage 2 plan chains onto a Stage 4 version. From S3-DELETE on, this regeneration commit has no Python generator and changes less. Numbered migrations apply above baseline@420 and leave baseline.sql as it is (crates/gcore/src/schema/assets.rs:480), so the commit does not touch it; the catalog manifest regenerates through UPDATE_GCORE_SCHEMA_MANIFEST (crates/gcore/tests/catalog_manifest_freshness.rs:398); and the pin stays at src/gobby/storage/schema_expected_identity.json, the one file S3-DELETE leaves under src/gobby, written by gdaemon schema version --json | jq -S ., which produces the bytes src/gobby/storage/schema_identity_pin.py:79-81 writes today. S3-DELETE deletes SCHEMA-WINDOW's preflight edit (D4) with src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py.
decisions.rationale: Josh: 'each rust cutover should include a database backup, in case we're making changes that can't be easily rolled back (like removing a lot of dead tables/columns from the database found as tech debt during the port)'. On rollback versus migrations (2026-11-03): 'We should probably figure out a workaround'; on promotion: 'promote binaries on checkpoints right? we don't want to run a full rust recompile every time a binary is updated'. Expand-only keeps Python working on the migrated schema. Before SCHEMA-WINDOW, every older gdaemon refuses a migrated hub, because gdaemon checks the schema identity exactly (crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:276-297; crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:153-169), so a rollback across any schema step would need the backup restore and lose the writes made since; SCHEMA-WINDOW narrows that refusal to destructive receipts, so only the drops keep that cost, and they keep their own go. Landing schema inputs only inside cuts, after the backup, keeps every session's restart and hub-backup working between cuts and puts each schema change under a rehearsal, a window and a recipe. Ruling 20's 'a schema-carrying chunk lands in its checkpoint's cut' is met by the chunk's schema inputs. Its dormant code lands and closes at its own landing, because a chunk that waited for its cut would block its own dependents (B0-CLOSE needs B0-WRITE, CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW needs B0-CLOSE, and CP-WAVE1-REVIEW needs SKILLS, CRON, PLANS and PROJ-2), and gport start admits only dependencies that are closed as done.
decisions.status: Resolved.

decisions.question: How many chunk sessions run at once?
decisions.recommended_default: At most 2 chunk sessions until CP-TEMPLATE-CUT closes, not counting the one review or cutover session that holds the current checkpoint. The runner, gateway and pilot paths share those 2. The second session starts only after P0-RECORD lands, so the registration protocol is in force before it starts. After CP-TEMPLATE-CUT, up to 4, set from CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW's measured provider quota, landing-lock wait, and code-reviewer throughput (Josh's 2026-11-03 rule puts that seat on every candidate), plus security-auditor throughput (protocol step 7, D115), and re-set at CP-WAVE3-REVIEW. The 18 CPUs, 128 GiB and 4.7 TiB free measured for this map are A's. The port runs on P (ruling 18), so CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW also measures P's CPUs, memory and free disk, and the cap stays within them. Landing stays serialized by the landing lock. While a cutover holds the landing freeze, other sessions keep building but do not land. The port dispatcher applies the cap (D116). A session that a stop message holds does not count (D116).
decisions.rationale: Each session runs up to 16 subagents, the pilot must measure one chunk's cost cleanly, and the real bottlenecks are quota, the landing lock and the review seats, not hardware.

decisions.question: Where does Stage 4 run relative to Python's retirement?
decisions.recommended_default: After CP-FINAL-CUT. All eight S4-* chunks depend on CP-FINAL-CUT, land dormant on 0.9.0 (ruling 15), bump gdaemon at landing and are first promoted by CP-NODE-CUT's activation (D39), and go live together at CP-NODE-CUT, a checkpoint this map adds for Stage 4, whose review waits on S4-PROOF. POST-CLEAN follows CP-NODE-CUT. Fallback if Josh wants node work live sooner: activate each S4 chunk at a checkpoint of its own instead of CP-NODE-CUT.
decisions.rationale: Decision 26 orders Stage 4 after Python retirement, which this keeps. One Stage 4 checkpoint keeps the live node on its existing gdaemon until the whole node path is proven on isolated daemons (S4-PROOF). Ruling 15 removes the hand re-port window that a merge into 0.5.0 would have opened.

decisions.question: Where does Josh's A1 (#21559 P4 #24452-#24457 and P5 #24458-#24473) run, and does #21560 keep its edge on #21559?
decisions.recommended_default: Before B0, as A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG and A1-SECRETS (#24452 in SEAM-CALLERS), so Josh's pilot order holds: Phase 0, then A1, then B0, then the soak. The #21560 to #21559 edge stays (ROADMAP S2.4a after S2.3, kept in Josh's 2026-10-18 split). The seam wave is renamed SEAM-FAMILY, SEAM-CALLERS and SEAM-WS, so 'A1' means Josh's A1 only.
decisions.rationale: #25341 D1 defines A1 this way, and review calls the edge an ordering choice for map approval. The cost is three chunks on the pilot path; CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW then calibrates on config and tasks together.

decisions.question: How does the MCP gateway route tools while families port one at a time?
decisions.recommended_default: Per tool: every server:tool has its own backend (Native, Compare or Proxy). gcore's ToolRegistry composes several family crates into one server and rejects only duplicate tool names. A2 splits into GW-1 (native /mcp, routing, composition, discovery, leases) and GW-2 (REST tool routes, per-tool Compare, the preflight op and the compatibility endpoint). Option (a), the default and the contract's choice: the gateway owns the single policy pass (docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md:82, 86-88). GW-2 adds a dormant, loopback-only, secret-bound Python compatibility endpoint that dispatches each Proxy tool against Python with no policy pass, listed under D4. Proxy tools route to it, and whenever the gateway serves /mcp (in the harness, and live from CP-MCP-CUT's activation) it runs GW-2's preflight worker op for every tool until HOOK-3's joint flip (D27). Option (b), the fallback if Josh refuses the endpoint: the gateway runs the preflight op only for Native and Compare tools, Proxy keeps Python's /mcp and its own pass, CP-MCP-CUT says 'the policy pass for Native tools moves to the gateway', and GW-1 amends docs/contracts/internal-mcp.md:86-88. Map approval approves the #24841 plan as amended against runner-first, which settles its criterion 3. The endpoint answers for every Proxy tool, which includes external servers through Python's MCPClientManager until CP-WAVE5-CUT moves them to MUX-1's Backend, and the gobby namespace's Python tools until their chunks flip; it still runs no policy pass and exposes no external configuration route (GW-2). S3-DELETE deletes the compatibility endpoint.
decisions.rationale: ToolRegistry::new returns DuplicateServer when a second family names the same server (gcore mcp.rs:191-195), so per-server routing cannot soak the tasks tools while agents, plans and team tools on shared servers stay Python. At ~15K lines A2 was also too large for one session. Option (a) is the contract's own design: one policy pass, in the gateway, for every tool, so no call skips the pass or runs it twice; forwarding Proxy tools to Python's own /mcp would run Python's pass on top of the gateway's.
decisions.status: Default (a). It adds a dormant Python endpoint, so Josh approves it with D4 at map approval; (b) is the fallback.

decisions.question: When do hook-time rule passes and MCP tool-call rule passes move to Rust?
decisions.recommended_default: Together, in HOOK-3, under s2-11's hooks_mcp_split guard: one CLI session's hook passes and tool-call passes share one engine and one FIFO (leaf 7.15.5). GW-2's preflight worker op stays until then, and RULE-2 no longer switches preflight on its own. In the map that guard is one compiled default that drives hook ingress and the gateway's tool-call rule-pass engine together, with a test that no build exposes them apart; 7.15.5's start refusal keyed on front_door.routes values is not built (D37), and GW-2's op carries the after phase until the same flip (D82).
decisions.rationale: A split flip would run two engines over one session's FIFO and break the ordering s2-11 requires (plan :87, :3159-3179).

decisions.question: Which comms adapters ship in 1.0? The registry loads seven: slack, telegram, discord (652 lines), teams (348), email (600), sms (274) and gobby_chat (205).
decisions.recommended_default: One gobby-comms adapter contract in Rust that every adapter implements (connect, inbound, outbound, attachments, identity), defined by COMMS-1 and implemented by COMMS-2. Telegram, Slack, Teams, email and SMS ship in 1.0. Each existing Python adapter is verified first against a real test account (a send, an inbound message and an attachment) before its recording can serve as an oracle; an adapter that verifies is ported as-is, and one that fails is ported from its provider's published API contract instead. Teams reverses #24173's Teams drop. Discord ships in 1.0 if its stated test passes: a live round trip on a test guild covering connect, an inbound message, an outbound message, reconnect after a gateway disconnect, and an attachment; otherwise its move to after 1.0 is recorded as a deferral: a post-1.0 task filed after the friction queue (ruling 10), with Discord's recorded fixtures and test-guild script kept. iMessage is after 1.0. gobby_chat is dropped: its sends deliver nothing (docs/reviews/comms-integrations.md:83-84), the web UI already hides it (web/src/components/activity/integrations/IntegrationsTabModel.ts:54; web/src/components/activity/integrations/channelMetadata.ts:3), and its seeded channel rows stay inert until CP-FINAL-CUT can delete them. P0-LOWTRAFFIC fakes every shipped adapter at the network edge.
decisions.rationale: Josh: 'The goal is to have a unified gobby-comms interface that works with Telegram, Slack, Teams, email, SMS, iMessage, etc. Not sure what gobby_chat is or how it's used currently. Might be legacy code.' and 'Discord if we can make it work, otherwise defer to after 1.0.' He does not know whether the adapters work, so verification comes before porting. The ledger has no adapter rows, so the coverage check passes whatever is decided, and an unported adapter would silently vanish at S3-DELETE.

decisions.question: Who owns the session mailbox (messages, attachments, waits)?
decisions.recommended_default: AG-3 owns messages and attachments (including the unclassified get_attachment and send_attachment rows) and delivered-mailbox retention; AG-WAIT owns waits and the completion registry. Comms and cron consume AG-3's family API, and gcron never deletes inter_session_messages rows itself (#25033, which closes as superseded by CRON's task under D31), and R4's registry schedules that retention until AG-3's native job replaces the op. One interim exception before AG-3 activates: A1-RUNTIME's adapter writes the capability_expired agent_recovery row, a single shared-row insert under D19, until CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation commit replaces it with AG-3's writer.
decisions.rationale: #24173 criterion 8, tasks-family and agents-family all claim the mailbox, and the cron plan's 2026-10-24 ruling assumed #22340 was still parked. One owner per table API follows crates/AGENTS.md.

decisions.question: Who runs the cutover?
decisions.recommended_default: Each cutover chunk's own session, a default agent (ruling 11), running as an unspawned, operator-opened root interactive session: a spawned agent is refused (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32), a CLI run from a linked worktree is refused (src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153), and a headless spawned run cannot register wait_for_coordination for the window (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:64-69). It runs the main checkout's CLI with --path at the main checkout. Its brief carries the nine cutover steps: the global announcement; the restart timing, with project_policy.quiet_hours read live at that moment, never restated, and a 200 protected-runs answer that lists no run; the hold, the pin and the landing freeze bound to its task; the verified backup; the rollback rehearsal; the activation commit with its version bumps; the window; the decision; and the recipe.
decisions.rationale: Josh: 'we're not building this with runbook agents, so a default agent (like you) would handle it'. The session constraints come from the code: activation refuses spawned agents, the CLI refuses linked worktrees, and the window needs a live wait. Quiet hours are policy that changes, so the brief reads them live instead of copying a window that can go stale. #25718 gives restarts and cutovers on A a dedicated seat, at the Orchestrator's direction. On P this ruling stands: the guard and the rule refuse only a spawned agent (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32; src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/no-daemon-management.yaml:5-6, 18).

decisions.question: How is the map applied to the 447 open #21542 nodes?
decisions.recommended_default: At chunk-task creation on P (start gate item 10) every open node is dispositioned (python3 -I scripts/port/check_dispositions.py docs/port/open-nodes.json docs/port/map-v2.json docs/port/dispositions/*.json exits 0): a node owned by a chunk closes as superseded by that chunk's task, or done where its criterion is already met (#25582, #25577, and #22340 under D2); map-root containers close; and every old blocked_by edge among them is dropped, because the chunk DAG replaces them. Named consequences: #23275 to #24359 is deleted; #24711 moves to CP-FINAL-CUT and #24712 re-anchors on #24708; the nodes of the earlier map's end-of-port cutover move to the cutovers that now hold their work (#25475 to CP-RUNNER-CUT, #24882 and #24886 to CP-MCP-CUT), #24474 to CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT, #25521 to CP-TEMPLATE-CLOSE-CUT and #25467 to R-RETIRE; #25024's edge on #21563 is replaced by MEM-3's re-binding; #21566 3.1's edge on #25207 is cut; #24576 and #24863 close as superseded. Dropping edges reverses some approved ones (#25460's #23275 to #25468, #25460 D6's #24149 edges, ROADMAP uses-edges, #24657's N1 edge), which map approval confirms. Ownership moves the same way for #24703 and #24704 (to S4-CIX), #25557 (to MEM-3, which completes it) and #24707, #25559 and #25111 (to CP-WAVE3-CUT, whose activation commit carries their flips over dormant builds, D37). Closes at chunk-task creation run leaves first. Closing a node's last open child also tries the node with that child's close reason (close_eligible_parent_chain, src/gobby/storage/tasks/_close.py:170-220). The closure policy leaves the node open when it carries a hold label (needs-decision, needs-planning or clean-window) or epic-devteam, is claimed, escalated or on hold, or is a non-epic with its own validation criteria (closure-preserves-reserved-ancestors, src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/general.yaml:14-28), and on a superseded try unless the node already holds an approved disposition attestation with that reason and a reference (:54-75), so each node the cascade skips is closed explicitly after its children. A done try needs no implementation attestation (:30-43), so a done child that closes last takes an unreserved parent with it as done, whatever the parent's disposition; among one parent's children, done closes therefore run before superseded ones. In the 2026-11-04 snapshot the hold-labeled nodes with open children are #21546, #21560, #21562, #21563, #21564, #21566, #21567, #21570, #21573, #21586, #21588, #21592, #23276, #24149, #24151, #24657, #24841, #25070, #25467, #25468 and #25486. #23275 closes only after #24359 closes and #24360 moves out of its subtree (D6). Linked commits do not block superseded: 727cd66893 removed that refusal with src/gobby/tasks/close_invariants.py, so the no-legal-close note in #22340's escalation_reason is out of date, and where a disposition's rationale still says linked commits make a node's close done, this sentence wins. Of the open nodes with linked commits, #22340 closes done under D2, and #23275, #24657, #24841, #25252, #25254, #25577 and #25582 have met their criteria and close done, with the approved implementation attestation that an explicit done close needs (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/general.yaml:30-43). #20202, #21559, #21565, #21571, #21575, #21586, #23277, #24148, #24359, #24603, #24659, #25253 and #25255 to #25259 have not, and they close as superseded by their owning chunks' tasks, as any other owned node does. Three done closes fall outside that pass, as their owners' text says: #25577 before the cut (start gate item 3), #25582 in R0's session and #22340 at COMMS-1's landing, with its SHA (D2). While #25582 and #22340 stay open, closure-requires-closed-children (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/general.yaml:45-52) keeps their ancestors open too, so R0's session closes #25468 after #25582, R-RETIRE closes #25467 (its goal), and #21544 closes with whichever of #22340 and #25467 closes last: the cascade takes it on a done close, and that session closes it explicitly otherwise. Closing an epic also archives the plan record rooted at it, at any close reason, explicitly or through the cascade: the plan's file moves to .gobby/plans/completed/ in the project's main checkout and its coverage manifest is deleted, both left uncommitted (src/gobby/storage/tasks/_close.py:211-219; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle_close_finalization.py:107-119; src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_plan.py:13-36; src/gobby/storage/plans.py:278-342). In the 2026-11-04 snapshot those epics are #20202, #21559, #21560, #21563, #21565, #21575, #21580, #21582, #21585, #21587, #23277, #24148 and #24657. Briefs and cutover sessions cite those plans at their live paths, so when these closes finish, before the first chunk claim, Josh runs git restore -- .gobby/plans and git clean -f -- .gobby/plans/completed from his own shell in P's main checkout, where nothing else is at work yet, because no-destructive-git-interactive refuses git clean -f in the unspawned session that ran them (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/no-destructive-git-interactive.yaml:17) and the task gate refuses it a whole-directory git restore without a claim (src/gobby/workflows/enforcement/blocking.py:697-753), and commits neither the moves nor the deletions. Chunk tasks are direct children of #21542, so it stays open through this pass as the port epic, and POST-CLEAN's close as done closes it. Four open nodes are no chunk's work (D2, D6), so this pass settles them first, because an open child keeps its parent open: closure-requires-closed-children refuses an explicit close of #21544, and the cascade swallows that refusal with no error (src/gobby/storage/tasks/_close.py:207-208), so POST-CLEAN's close would leave #21542 open. #22075, #19652 and #24360 move out of the #21542 tree into D6's post-1.0 backlog with update_task and an empty parent_task_id (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_crud.py:552-569). #22075 carries the protected deferred-by-user label (.gobby/project.json:8-12), and update_task refuses that label to a spawned or seated session whatever the escalation state (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_authorization.py:139-159), so this pass runs in an unspawned, operator-opened session. #25597 closes as wont_do, with an approved disposition attestation whose evidence.reason is wont_do and that cites D2 (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/general.yaml:54-65). A node whose disposition names a decision and that a chunk owns (#21576, #21583, #24173, #25201, #25269 and #25328) closes as superseded by that chunk's task, as any other chunk-owned node does, once Josh accepts that decision's default. An epic's archive move also leaves its plan's path dirty in the main checkout, and closure-preserves-attributed-work (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/general.yaml:5-12) then refuses any later close whose linked commits touch that path: #24148 and #24657 touch hub-mode.md, rooted at #21575, and #25254 touches gdaemon-ai-providers-family.md, rooted at #21587. On that refusal the session restores that one plan file with git restore -- <its path>, which the task gate lets through because it names a .md under .gobby (src/gobby/workflows/enforcement/blocking.py:421-445, 747), and retries, and it never commits the move.
decisions.rationale: Parent-chain readiness (_queries.py:408-443) turns the old edges into ready-queue deadlocks once nodes move, and claim_task checks no blockers, so the chunk DAG is the only ordering that holds: at chunk-task creation it becomes one blocks edge per depends_on entry among the chunk tasks under the port epic, and gport start refuses a chunk until every depends_on task has closed as done and, except for a review, its commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD.

decisions.question: Code-index P8 removes code_index.nightly_repair_timeout_seconds and leaves the native nightly repair with no per-project timeout; no approval is recorded.
decisions.recommended_default: Port the timeout as-is in CIX-2 and keep the config key. #24713 loses that key's removal and keeps its code deletions in S3-DELETE, and CP-FINAL-CUT's activation commit removes its other key, code_index.maintenance_log_file (D65).
