decisions.rationale: CP-WAVE5-CUT is the first cut at which every message type has a native owner, because MUX-1's tool_call is the last to leave Python, and it gives the path a 12-hour window with Python still present and a recipe back to the leg. Flipping at commit A was rejected: S3-FREEZE would then assert a path that had never carried live traffic, and a failure would land in the cut with the most to undo. A separate chunk was rejected: the public transports and ping are already SEAM-WS's rows, and the work needs nothing later than SEAM-CALLERS, since the events and the conversation-ids port are bound by their owners and the settings by the activation commit. The new edge from SEAM-WS to SEAM-CALLERS delays nothing that matters, because SEAM-WS's consumers TERM-1 and CHAT-2 already reach SEAM-CALLERS. With that edge the Admitted value and the confinement gate sit in SEAM-WS rather than with the first claimer, because the path's replay needs them at this chunk's landing.

decisions.question: TERM-1's activation (CP-WAVE1-CUT) moves terminal attachments, holders, generations and write admission to Rust's lease registry, while Python's host manager, composer ledger and write coordinator stay the single owner until CP-WAVE5-CUT. How does a native WS operator write reach the host? Python's coordinator refuses an operator origin whose attachment and generation do not match Python's own registry, which then holds no WS attachment (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:575-580, 649-665). Any other origin changes behavior: daemon latches two rows per keystroke and records non-human text in the composer ledger (:853-863; src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:78), attention passes the attention gate (write_coordinator.py:573-574), and automatic reads the quarantine (:215-223). So a one-line registration on coordinator.write cannot serve it.
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it adds a Python worker op beyond D4's list.
decisions.recommended_default: One allow-listed worker op that TERM-1 registers as its Rust caller, terminal_operator_write(terminal_id, attachment_id, action_key, kind, payload), with a small shim in R0's worker package bound to the worker's write coordinator; the shim is why it does not fit D4's one-line clause. Rust's lease registry has already admitted the write against its holder and generation, so the shim does not revalidate. On the event loop that owns the coordinator, it takes lease_registry.lock(terminal_id), builds a WriteRequest with origin operator, calls _dispatch, which records the composer ledger's human provenance and keeps hub-mode's remote branch (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:759-767, 801-802, 811; D21), and on Delivered releases the automatic-write quarantine (:609-610), which the native coordinator's own row release cannot do alone, because Python also keeps that quarantine in process (:741-747; crates/gterminals/src/write.rs:407-411). The shim binds no caller, so _dispatch's machine-owned check passes (:837-850), and TERM-1's ownership check at attach stands in for it, as Python's lease vouch does (:769-790). The native coordinator holds its per-terminal lock across the Runtime call (crates/gterminals/src/write.rs:361), so a terminal's writes reach the op one at a time and in order, though R0 runs domain ops concurrently. It cannot reuse _write_locked, which revalidates unconditionally (:575), and it latches nothing, as Python's operator write does not (:853-863). The row comes from one read per attachment_id, kept for that attachment as Python's lease record keeps it, so a keystroke does not queue for a worker thread (:213-214, 715-721). Its answers are _deliver_operator_write's outcomes and reasons (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_write.py:155-195), and a lost reply is indeterminate_backend, never retried (R0). This op serves only the native WS operator write: _revalidate_lease returns at once for every other origin (write_coordinator.py:649-665), so send_keys' write and the automatic writers stay one-line registrations on the coordinator under D4. TERM-1 lands it dormant, CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation commit starts calling it, Rust stops calling it at CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation, when TERM-HOST's Coordinator writes to the native host, and S3-DELETE deletes it. Alternative with no Python edit: the terminal routes stay on Proxy until CP-WAVE5-CUT, the fallback CP-WAVE1-CUT's risks already name, so TERM-1 and TERM-2 activate with TERM-HOST and neither D105's op nor TERM-2's two ops are built. The cost is that the terminal family's 40 rows get no live window until wave 5, and from CP-WAVE2-CUT every Python workspace read can sweep AG-1's unbound pane, because Python's sweep cannot see a native reservation.
decisions.rationale: D19 keeps the coordinator, its per-terminal lock and the composer ledger in Python until their last in-process caller moves, so the write has to cross into Python, and the crossing must not repeat a lease check that only Rust can now answer. The shim reuses Python's dispatch, so the ledger, the quarantine and the remote branch stay as they are.

decisions.question: A1-CONFIG's casefold needs two packages the lock lacks. gdaemon-runtime-family plan 5.7 ports str.casefold with icu_casemap 2.1.1's CaseMapper::fold_string on its compiled data icu_casemap_data 2.1.1 (.gobby/plans/gdaemon-runtime-family.md:83, 3592, 3604-3609); neither is in Cargo.lock, and icu_properties 2.1.2 already is. No map decision approves them, and the map treats every new crate as Josh's call (D76).
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it adds two third-party crates.
decisions.recommended_default: Add icu_casemap 2.1.1 and icu_casemap_data 2.1.1 exactly as the plan pins them, in A1-CONFIG's landing with Cargo.lock, and add no other package. crates.io, checked 2026-11-04: both 2.1.1 releases date from 2025-10-28 and are not yanked, the licence is Unicode-3.0, the owners are sffc and the team github:unicode-org:icu4x-release, the repository is unicode-org/icu4x, total downloads are about 7.9 million, and the newest release is 2.4.0 from 2026-10-22. The pin stays on 2.1.1 to match the locked icu_properties 2.1.2. Alternative with no new crate: a full case-fold table generated from Unicode's CaseFolding.txt and committed as Rust source, with a test against Python's str.casefold over every code point, which leaves that table to keep in step with Python's Unicode version.
decisions.rationale: The crates are actively released by the Unicode project and the same family as a crate already locked. A hand-kept table adds code that the port would own for no behavior gain.

decisions.question: Python's comms wake holds while the operator has a pane focused: WakeDispatcher reads focus_held from the lease registry and records the hold, and the registry's focus observer releases it (src/gobby/events/wake.py:119, 230-245, 830-836; src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:468-496; src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:144-145). From CP-WAVE1-CUT the holder and its focus report live in Rust's registry, so Python's focus_held is always false and a comms wake clears the composer and types into the pane under the operator's hands (wake.py:837-840), until TERM-HOST binds the hold natively at CP-WAVE5-CUT. AG-3's live-wake ops run the same read. How does the hold keep working?
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it adds a Python worker op beyond D4's list.
decisions.recommended_default: One allow-listed worker op that TERM-1 registers as its Rust caller, terminal_focus_changed(terminal_id, focused), with a small shim in R0's worker package; the shim is why it does not fit D4's one-line clause. The shim keeps the set of focused terminal ids in an object with the focus_held method of wake's Protocol (src/gobby/events/wake.py:119) and installs it through wake_dispatcher.set_lease_registry on its first call, so nothing changes while it is dormant. True adds the id. False removes it and calls wake_dispatcher.release_focus_hold(terminal_id), as the focus observer does (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:490-496). TERM-1's native registry keeps the holder's focus flag with Python's rules: only the holder's report counts, and take, release and finalize clear it (leases.py:149-150, 481-496, 544, 572, 637). The family calls the op on each change of the holder's focus, one call at a time per terminal, and re-sends its focused holders on each new worker generation, from a step in R3's order, which runs at each start and respawn, because the set is process memory. The op is idempotent, so a failed call or a lost reply logs and that terminal's current value goes with its next change or the next worker generation; a wake in that gap reads the last value delivered. TERM-1 lands it dormant, CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation commit starts calling it, Rust stops calling it at CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation, when TERM-HOST binds the hold to its registry, and S3-DELETE deletes it. Alternative with no Python edit: no op. Each wave review's packet through CP-WAVE5-REVIEW then records as a known regression that a comms wake replaces the text in a pane the operator is typing in.
decisions.rationale: The wake dispatcher stays Python's until TERM-HOST, because Python's completion registry, coordination delivery and replay still call it in process (AG-3), and Python never calls Rust (D19), so the focus report has to cross from Rust into Python. Without it the operator loses typed text on every comms wake for four waves on a live daemon.

decisions.question: How does a chunk session on P clear the security gates its landing meets? Landing and closure refuse a candidate that carries the security-review label or touches a project_policy.security_paths entry until a definition declaring approve_security_review records an approved security-review attestation on its exact SHA (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/security.yaml:27-63, selected by src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/default.yaml:126; .gobby/workflows/rules/project-operating-policy.yaml:35-86, which lists crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/**). Plans add that gate on their admission or landing leaves, most after an Orchestrator applies the label (.gobby/plans/gdaemon-ai-providers-family.md:1172-1181; .gobby/plans/gdaemon-skills-family.md:85-88, 1834-1846; .gobby/plans/gdaemon-cron-family.md:1564-1568; .gobby/plans/tasks-family.md:2042-2050; .gobby/plans/memory-family.md:2294-2307; .gobby/plans/s2-11-hub-hooks-rules.md:2896-2899; .gobby/plans/sessions-family.md:216-225; .gobby/plans/hub-mode.md:448-454; .gobby/plans/hook-envelope-file-facts.md:314-317), and A1-RUNTIME's risks require that review for #25068. No chunk task has an Orchestrator, protocol step 7 sends nothing to the auditor on A, and a spawned default-agent session cannot spawn the seat: default's spawn scope is every definition, so spawn-capability-authority compares capabilities, and default lacks approve_security_review (src/gobby/workflows/condition_helpers_spawn.py:90-112).
decisions.status: Default. It follows D115's answer and takes no separate word.
decisions.recommended_default: D115's seat serves every gated chunk. A gated chunk is one whose brief cites this decision, one whose family plan gates its work on a security review, or one whose candidate touches a security path. Its session adds the security-review label with gobby-tasks:add_label right after its claim, in place of the plans' Orchestrator step, or as soon as it sees that its candidate touches a security path. After protocol step 8's merge and version bump, and before land_commit, it finds the seat with gobby-agents:list_running_agents, sends it the task ref and the resulting commit's full SHA, and waits with wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<seat>, reply=true, timeout=3600), registered again after every timeout. The seat reads the candidate by that SHA, which the shared object store holds, and records the attestation itself, with the full SHA as its git reference (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/security-auditor.yaml). The rules compare that exact SHA, so a later merge or fix gets a renewed run, and a rejected candidate is fixed and sent again. With no seat running, a chunk session escalates its task to Josh and lands nothing, and a cutover session follows its step 3 (D115). A plan's activation or admission record names this label and attestation, and no pre-dispatch check exists. The next review packet lists each attestation by SHA. Alternative with no standing seat: Josh opens each gated chunk's session himself, so that operator session, which passes spawn-capability-authority because it is unspawned (src/gobby/workflows/agent_resolver.py:61-63), spawns the seat as step 7 spawns the code-reviewer, which gives up spawned sessions for those chunks.
decisions.rationale: The rules and the seat exist and need no code, and an independent authorized approval of the exact SHA is what the plans' gates ask for: only who applies the label and who opens the seat change. The claimant may add the label: add_label checks only claim authority (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle_labels.py:22-35; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_authorization.py:87-116), and block-update-task names only update_task and is not among default's selectors. Protocol step 7's rule against sending to A stays (D40 item 5). Without the seat a gated landing is refused and its session can do nothing about it.

decisions.question: D9 leaves VOICE's engine to Josh, and its default (the current engine behind a trait, no Crane TTS) cannot be built: the current speech-to-text is the faster-whisper Python package (src/gobby/voice/stt.py:31-44; pyproject.toml:54), the default text-to-speech is chatterbox-tts on torch (pyproject.toml:76-79; src/gobby/config/voice.py:79), VOICE edits no Python, and S3-DELETE deletes Python. Which engines does VOICE build?
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: VOICE builds these engines in a new crate, crates/gvoice (package gobby-voice, publish = false), behind one speech-to-text trait and one text-to-speech trait. Speech-to-text: whisper-rs, exact-pinned at 0.16.0 and only in that crate, with its metal feature on macOS, serves the reserved whisper provider: transcribe and translate, with whisper_prompt and whisper_vocabulary as the initial prompt and segments in Python's result shape (src/gobby/voice/stt.py:116-226). It is a cfg(unix) target dependency, because Windows stays post-1.0 (83a9445f) and MUX-1's compile-only Windows clippy job cross-lints gobby-daemon from ubuntu-latest, where a native C or C++ build finds no MSVC headers, as .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml:152-154 records for libghostty-vt; a Windows build has no whisper engine and its probe returns false. voice.whisper_device set to cpu turns the GPU off and any other value leaves it on; voice.whisper_compute_type has no whisper.cpp meaning, so native ignores it. Ports of src/gobby/ai/audio.py's capability service, adapters and builder (:107-362) take each audio binding from crates/gai's capability snapshot, and the port of OpenAICompatibleAudioAdapter (:278-334) serves voice.openai_compatible_audio's bindings. whisper_model_size names the whisper.cpp ggml model, stored as <gobby_home>/models/whisper/ggml-<size>.bin and downloaded from huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp on first load, as faster-whisper fetches its model today. Audio of Python's accepted types (src/gobby/voice/stt.py:168-176) decodes to 16 kHz mono PCM through the ffmpeg binary, which Telegram voice notes already run (src/gobby/communications/tts_voice.py:64), so no decoder crate enters. #25072's probe returns whether ffmpeg resolves, because the engine is compiled in and a missing model downloads on first load, just as Python's probe reports only that its runtime is installed (src/gobby/voice/stt.py:228-234). Criterion 1 stands, criterion 3 is the contract change D50 names, and the reason crates/gai reports on false changes from Python's faster-whisper text (src/gobby/ai/registry_builder.py:242) to 'ffmpeg is not installed.' through the Found Work AI-1B's risks allow. Text-to-speech: a port of src/gobby/voice/tts_crane.py, over HTTP to voice.tts_crane_url with its v1/audio/speech PCM16 stream and ready check. Crane stays a process the operator runs (docs/guides/crane-tts.md), any server with that contract works, and gdaemon links no Crane code and no candle. chatterbox is dropped: native reads voice.tts_provider's chatterbox value as crane, and any other unknown value keeps Python's unknown-provider status (src/gobby/voice/providers.py:24-27). Python's voice classes stay unedited in the worker for Python's Telegram path until CP-WAVE5-CUT, and S3-DELETE deletes them with the faster-whisper and chatterbox-tts dependencies. CP-FINAL-CUT sets voice.tts_provider's default to crane and removes voice.whisper_compute_type and the four keys only Chatterbox reads, as it removes code_index.maintenance_log_file. If Josh declines whisper-rs, speech-to-text goes only through voice.openai_compatible_audio, with crane-serve's POST /v1/audio/transcriptions as the default binding: pure Rust with no C++ in gdaemon's build, but no built-in engine, so the whisper provider reports unavailable. If he wants Crane in process inside gobby-voice, that is a further implementation of the same trait after 1.0.
decisions.rationale: Josh on #21588: 'The STT engine should be rust-based' (2026-10-25) and 'I want to replace chatterbox and any other TTS with our own implementation of crane' (2026-10-23); on #23768: 'we need to replace chatterbox with crane'. The default follows PB11 (.gobby/plans/task-25341.md:67-70: whisper-rs, any OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint, Crane or any /v1/audio/speech endpoint, chatterbox dropped), whose operator origin Josh confirms with this answer. Crate check on crates.io, 2026-11-04: whisper-rs 0.16.0, published 2026-03-12 (0.15.1 on 2025-09-10), Unlicense, repository codeberg.org/tazz4843/whisper-rs, one publisher (tazz4843), about 1.0M recent downloads, a metal feature and no declared rust_version; it wraps whisper-rs-sys 0.15.0, which builds whisper.cpp from source with cmake and bindgen as build dependencies, so building gdaemon on macOS and Linux gains cmake, a C++ compiler and libclang, and 'rust-based' here means Rust bindings over C++. GobbyAI's Crane fork is MIT with its NOTICE.md, its model is Apache-2.0 and downloaded separately, and Python already speaks to it over HTTP, so this port borrows no Crane code and needs no licence step, which answers D9's licence question. ffmpeg rather than a decoder crate: browsers send webm and Telegram ogg, both usually opus; whisper.cpp takes PCM; and the binary is already a Telegram voice-note dependency. Rejected: Python's engines through a worker op, because S3-DELETE removes them and Josh asked for a Rust engine and for Crane; Crane in process now, because crane-core brings candle, tokenizers and its model stack into gdaemon's build for a call the HTTP client already serves. The two traits keep each choice inside the crate.

decisions.question: #22143 asks for a decision-complete plan for focused-session speech in gclient once #21588's API exists, with no terminal speech implementation, and the map said only that it follows D9's answer. What does VOICE deliver for it, and does terminal speech ship in 1.0?
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: VOICE's last checkpoint writes the plan, .gobby/plans/terminal-speech.md, against its delivered API. #22143's criteria are its acceptance (concrete targets, protocol decisions, playback dependency and platform support, controls, queue, cancellation and reconnect semantics, provider transcript behavior, and tests for focus switching, interruption, reconnection and simultaneous listeners); the Workflow's adversarial design review is its review, with no gobby-plan step or stamp (rulings 1 and 5). VOICE writes no gclient code and adds no playback dependency. #22143 closes superseded by VOICE's task (D31). The implementation it plans is not a 1.0 deliverable: no parity-ledger row needs it, family chunks add no gclient verbs (D16) and ruling 10 allows no scope addition, so after 1.0 the plan becomes a task on Josh's word. If Josh wants terminal speech in 1.0, its implementation becomes a new chunk after VOICE and V1A, built from this plan.
decisions.rationale: #22143's own text keeps implementation out ('no terminal speech implementation in this task') and ties the planning to the delivered API ('Resume detailed terminal planning when that API is ready'), and #21588 designs the API with the terminal consumer now. The session that delivers the API is the plan's best author, and the plan costs part of one checkpoint. Rejected: a separate planning chunk, which adds mechanism for one document; leaving #22143 open past VOICE, which D31 does not allow for a node the map owns; and adding terminal speech to VOICE, which D16 and #22143's own text both refuse.

decisions.question: voice_mode_toggle goes native at CP-WAVE3-CUT, but Python's message processor keeps feeding attached-session speech until CP-WAVE4-CUT, and that feed and the stop hook's turn flush read Python's own voice-mode map (src/gobby/servers/websocket/voice_attached.py:53; src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_agent.py:654), which nothing sets from CP-WAVE3-CUT on. What happens to attached-session speech between those cuts?
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: Accept the gap and name it. From CP-WAVE3-CUT's activation until CP-WAVE4-CUT's, a web client in voice mode on an attached CLI session hears no speech for that session's replies. The replies' text still reaches the client, web chat speech works, and voice input to the attached session works. CP-WAVE3-REVIEW's packet states the gap for Josh's go, it is no rollback trigger in CP-WAVE3-CUT's window, and HOOK-3's composition ends it at CP-WAVE4-CUT. Alternative if Josh wants no gap: VOICE's feed also reads the session_message frames that Python's processor already publishes over the WS bridge (src/gobby/sessions/processor_stats.py:91-99; crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/publish.rs), from CP-WAVE3-CUT's activation until CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation commit removes that read, with no Python edit and no worker op. Then the end of a reply can wait for that session's next message, because Python's turn flush stays off.
decisions.rationale: Ruling 9 keeps transitional mechanism only where it is the cheapest way to keep correctness evidence, and this gap costs no evidence: VOICE's and SES-3B's cases prove the feed offline, HOOK-3's proves its binding, and CP-WAVE4-CUT activates it. D19 rules out Python reading native's toggle. Rejected: a worker op with which native's toggle sets Python's map, because Python's speech engines would keep speaking through a second pipeline that native's tts_stop cannot cancel, and it adds a Python edit outside D4's list for one wave; and holding voice_mode_toggle in Python until CP-WAVE4-CUT, because CHAT-2's speech port needs the mode natively from CP-WAVE3-CUT.

decisions.question: Does gdaemon keep its crates.io publish? .github/workflows/release-gdaemon.yml:136-153 runs cargo publish -p gobby-daemon and its release job needs that job (:156), so a failed publish leaves no gdaemon release and no node bundles, and CP-NODE-CUT's update of the live node waits on that release. The publish cannot pass: crates/gdaemon/Cargo.toml's gobby-runtime and gobby-terminals are path-only dependencies on publish = false crates, every daemon family crate is publish = false by rule (crates/AGENTS.md:93), and gdaemon embeds files outside its directory (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/waivers.rs:12; crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/repair.rs:41; crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/verify.rs:62). No plan or decision names this job.
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: Drop it. S4-RELEASE removes the publish job and the release job's need on it, sets publish = false in crates/gdaemon/Cargo.toml, drops the pin at crates/gdaemon/tests/release_workflow.rs:15 and changes docs/guides/release-guide.md:13 to GitHub binaries. gdaemon ships through its GitHub release, which node install and D60's Homebrew resources read, and gclient, gcode, ghook, gmcp, gterm and gobby-core keep their crates.io publish. Alternative: keep the publish, which means publishing gobby-runtime, gobby-terminals, gobby-assets and every family crate, with a version on each path dependency and a crate-local copy of every embedded file, the template tree included, and tagging each of them ahead of gdaemon in every release.
decisions.rationale: crates.io holds no gobby-daemon (checked 2026-11-04), and nothing in the repository installs it from there: Python's installer builds it from the checkout (src/gobby/cli/install_setup_gdaemon.py:84-92), and the job, its test pin and the release guide's row are the only places that name it with crates.io. The release guide already says a crate publishes only after its dependencies are indexed, so the alternative turns one release into a tag per family crate for a crate with no consumer. No other chunk removes the job, so without this decision the first gdaemon-v* tag stops at CP-NODE-CUT.

decisions.question: Who gives the independent security approval on the port machine? land_commit and close_task both refuse a candidate whose paths match project_policy.security_paths, or whose task carries the security-review label, until a session holding approve_security_review that neither authored nor claimed the work has approved that exact SHA (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/security.yaml:27-63; a landing evaluates with reason done, src/gobby/tasks/closure_snapshot.py:104, src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:583-589). Only the security-auditor definition holds that capability (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/security-auditor.yaml:9), a spawned default-agent session cannot spawn it, because its capabilities are not contained in the caller's (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/tool-hygiene/spawn-capability-authority.yaml:5-26; src/gobby/workflows/condition_helpers_spawn.py:56-116), and protocol step 7 keeps the auditor on A unless Josh opens a seat on P.
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: Josh opens the one static security-auditor seat on P before the first chunk claim, with gobby pipelines run support -i workspace=<workspace> -i project_path=<P's main checkout> -i seats=security-auditor -i report_to=<his own session ref> (docs/guides/runbooks.md:55-65), and it stays open through POST-CLEAN; a rerun of that command replaces the seat after a crash or a backup restore, because the runbook launches only a seat that is not live. A chunk or cutover session whose candidate those rules name, or whose brief names a security review, sends that seat the task ref and the full SHA and waits with wait_for_coordination until the seat records its security-review attestation on that SHA; each changed SHA needs its own approval. With no live seat a chunk session escalates its task to Josh, who reruns the command, and lands nothing, and once Josh says the seat is live it runs de_escalate_task and claim_task and resumes at the send. A cutover session instead reruns the command itself, because it is operator-opened, and asks Josh in its own terminal if that fails, and it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (its step 3). Any other candidate sends the seat nothing, because one seat that reviewed every candidate would queue the gated ones behind the rest, and each longer wait invites a moved tip and a new SHA to approve; Josh may widen that to every candidate in his answer, as his 2026-11-03 rule has it on A. A cutover does this for each land_commit once anything a linked commit lands matches, because the path scope covers every linked commit (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:388-404). P's project_policy keeps security_paths unchanged, and nothing goes to A (D40 item 5). This takes no Python or template edit. If Josh declines the standing seat, D106's alternative applies. The seat starts on the provider project_policy.agent_model_defaults names, grok today, so that CLI must be on P (D119).
decisions.rationale: With no approver on P, the first candidate that touches those paths stops at land_commit with no way forward: SEAM-WS's crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/ modules; a pick of a fix in src/gobby/communications/; RULE-1A's prepared rewrite of the lookbehind patterns in src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/tool-hygiene/workflow-cli-authority.yaml:21 and src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/roles/seat-spawn-policy.yaml:67, in the cut that lands it, and the deactivation commit that reverts it; and S3-DELETE's deletion of the Python files on that list (.gobby/workflows/rules/project-operating-policy.yaml:35-86). R6, SEAM-CALLERS, A1-RUNTIME, SES-1 and SES-2 already name a security review as part of the chunk, and CP-RUNNER-REVIEW's packet lists its record, with no seat to produce it. A seat per candidate was rejected, because D39 lets chunk sessions be spawned and a spawned session cannot launch this definition. Emptying security_paths on P was rejected, because it removes a protected check from the admission code that most needs it. Waiting for A's auditor was rejected, because no chunk depends on cross-machine messaging (D40 item 5).

decisions.question: How does a hub-local native launch reach Python's terminal host until TERM-HOST? AG-1 goes live at CP-WAVE2-CUT and TERM-HOST at CP-WAVE5-CUT. TERM-1's spawn op on spawn_web_terminal (src/gobby/terminals/web_spawn.py:73-116) cannot carry an agent launch: it takes no agent_run_id, title, machine_id, auth_cli or theme source, cannot retry an existing pending row and takes no in-doubt claim (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:143-186; src/gobby/agents/spawn_placed.py:39-79, 204-242). AG-1's python_edits named no other op.
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it adds a Python worker op with a shim beyond D4's one-line clause.
decisions.recommended_default: One allow-listed worker op that AG-1 registers as its Rust caller, agent_runtime_spawn, with a small shim in R0's worker package over src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py::_runtime_spawn (:54-140), Python's sole owner of the pending row, the prepare and the promote. The native launch path computes the provider command, environment and sandbox wrapping, and passes them with the project, machine, child session, parent session, agent run, title, auth_cli, working directory and timeout. The parent session is the theme source's input: _runtime_spawn reads it through spawner_theme_source (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:33-51), which gives no source for a spawner with no live native pane. The timeout fills SpawnRequest.timeout_seconds, because without it the prepare wait has no bound (src/gobby/agents/spawn_placed.py:278-282), and the op call's own timeout stays above it, so a slow spawn answers spawn_timeout and does not become an unknown outcome. No agent launch sets cancel_event today (src/gobby/agents/spawn_models.py:88; only web_spawn has its own, src/gobby/terminals/web_spawn.py:85), so the shim leaves it unset. The shim rebuilds SpawnRequest (src/gobby/agents/spawn_models.py:27-94) and ProviderSpawnPlan (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_providers.py:61-73), binds the worker's terminal manager and runtime registry (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor.py:91-106), and passes a SandboxLaunch that wraps nothing (src/gobby/agents/srt_runtime.py:113), because the native path has already wrapped the command. It passes no session manager and no run manager, so Python writes no session or agent_runs row (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor.py:243-247; src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:519); the native launch records them through AG-1's run-state store and gsessions' services, committing both rows before the op, because the pending row's foreign keys need them (crates/gcore/assets/schema/baseline.sql:5772, 5781), and it records the pid and terminal id from the result, which Python's update_runtime would have written. It returns SpawnResult's fields. A placed spawn has no Python binder to pass across the op, so AG-1 writes the pending row natively (crates/gterminals/src/repository.rs:84) with the columns create_pending sets (src/gobby/agents/spawn_placed.py:204-214: project, backend, ownership gobby, spawn key, machine, session, agent run and title), binds the pane through TERM-2's workspace operation, and passes that row's id as retry_terminal_id, which takes Python's in-doubt claim and generation bump (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:99-125; src/gobby/agents/spawn_placed.py:48-58, 197-200). Hub-local launches call it from CP-WAVE2-CUT until TERM-HOST's activation (CP-WAVE5-CUT), and S3-DELETE deletes it. A lost reply is an unknown outcome under R0's rule: the run reports spawn_in_doubt, and the launch is not retried blind. A refusal that returns before the attempt owns the row (a missing service, an unavailable host, terminal_in_doubt or retry_generation_cas_failed; src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:66-97; src/gobby/agents/spawn_placed.py:58-66, 223) leaves AG-1's own row pending, so AG-1 fails that row and compensates its placement. Past that point cleanup stays on the worker: _settle_native_spawn_failure fails the row and kills by spawn key (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor.py:109-133), and after a timeout _schedule_timeout_cleanup's done-callback or in-doubt owner settles it as a task on the op's event loop, after the op has returned (:330-392). None of them writes a session or agent_runs row, so AG-1 ends the run from the returned result and then calls deliver_completion (D71). Codex's deferred prompt sits outside _runtime_spawn (src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_codex.py:30-81), so the native launch schedules it after a successful op, through crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/codex_prompt.rs and TERM-1's write op. Alternative: hub-local launches stay on Python's whole spawn path until CP-WAVE5-CUT.
decisions.rationale: _runtime_spawn is the one place that owns a spawn's row, claim, prepare and promote, so the shim stays small. It does not fit D4's one-line clause because SpawnRequest and the plan are plain dataclasses that hold service objects only the worker has. Widening TERM-1's spawn_web_terminal op would change terminal_create's op for one caller. The alternative gives AG-1's hub store no live window until wave 5, the cut that also removes TERM-1's ops.

decisions.question: Who starts the chunk sessions? Protocol step 1 runs in a default-agent session, 'spawned or operator-opened' (D39), and D23 caps how many run, but no text says who spawns them or applies the cap. A closing chunk session cannot start the next one for long, because each spawn deepens the chain and AGENTS.md rule 11 stops it at depth 5. A spawned session also claims its task at spawn (spawn_agent's claim defaults to true), before step 1's gport start could run from the main checkout. The coordinator seat that start gate item 10 lets Josh open on P is named only as a place to send a SHA. Nor can a spawned session do protocol step 8's push or CI read, because spawn_agent runs it under managed SRT.
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: Josh opens one port dispatcher once start gate item 10's chunk tasks exist: a root, unspawned default-agent session in P's main checkout (AGENTS.md rule 15), in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), with the prompt 'Run the port dispatcher, D116 in docs/port/map-v2.md; spawn with model=<model> and reasoning_effort=<effort>', naming the model and effort its sessions run at. It claims no task and edits nothing. Its first turn sets session_lifecycle.stale_session_timeout_hours to 720 with gobby-config:patch_config_values, a live key, so that its row stays live through a review or a window with nothing to wake it. Each turn it calls list_ready_tasks(parent_task_id='#21542', limit=200), because the default limit of 10 can hide a ready checkpoint; skips an epic, because #21544 stays open as a container until R-RETIRE or COMMS-1 closes it (D31); and reads each other task once per context with get_task: its description's heading names its chunk and its Kind line gives its kind, both inside the preview of the offload envelope that a card over 15,000 characters comes back as, and that envelope shows labels only as a count (src/gobby/config/features.py:127-143; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/result_offload.py:300-315, 449), so it takes labels from list_tasks(parent_task_id='#21542', label=<label>, closed=False), one call for each of the three labels below. A claimed task is already running, so the dispatcher starts nothing on it, and it counts against D23's cap unless it is a review, a cutover or a chunk that a stop message holds, because a stopped session waits on fixes that need that room. That cap is 2 until CP-TEMPLATE-CUT closes, and after that the number Josh's go at CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW or CP-WAVE3-REVIEW set, which he names when he prompts it after that close. A checkpoint review, a cutover and a task labelled needs-decision, needs-planning or clean-window are Josh's: the dispatcher names each in its final message. He answers a labelled task himself and opens the unspawned session a review or a cutover needs (start gate item 14), as he does for GEN-ROLLBACK, the first ready chunk, unless his prompt says he refused its drill (D38). A review's session runs in the main checkout with no task worktree; it is unspawned because Josh answers it in that terminal and its no-go fixes and its resizing call create_task, which a spawned session is refused (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-enforcement/block-native-task-tools.yaml:5-19). For any other chunk, while the cap has room, it runs gport start <chunk id> from the main checkout, as cargo run --locked -q -p gobby-port -- start <chunk id> (by hand with get_task until P0-RECORD lands); a refusal starts nothing and goes in its final message. Then it calls spawn_agent(agent='default', task_id=<the task>, provider='claude', model=<model>, reasoning_effort=<effort>, checkout_mode='worktree', base_branch='0.9.0', prompt='Follow docs/port/protocol.md for chunk <chunk id> from step 2; your brief is this task's description.'). The three settings are required, because an unpinned spawn of default is refused (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_launch_settings.py:97-106), and the provider is claude because protocol step 4's Workflow is a Claude Code tool and a headless provider cannot hold step 5's waits (src/gobby/agents/provider_capabilities.py:39-48; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/headless_waits.py:34-68). When get_worktree_by_task finds a worktree left by a session that died, worktree_id replaces checkout_mode and base_branch and the prompt says to resume under step 1; a task whose replacement also dies goes in the final message for Josh instead of a third spawn. A task with no chunk heading is a task outside the map, which starts the same way with no gport start (protocol step 3), its prompt naming the task in place of a chunk. A spawned session cannot push or read CI, because spawn_agent runs it under managed SRT with no git network and no git or gh credentials (src/gobby/agents/sandbox_gate.py:22-33; docs/guides/sandboxing.md:245-249), and a test that launches an agent under SRT fails inside it (tests/e2e/conftest.py:416-424). So when one sends a landed SHA (protocol step 8), the dispatcher runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, because the pre-push hook's 1,800-second timeout (.gobby/project.json) outlasts a foreground tool call, then watches that commit's CI in the background so that its turn can end, and replies with the result, which is the hook's output when the pre-push hook refuses the push, or with superseded when a later push cancelled the run (D85); and when one sends a test command and its worktree path (protocol step 6), it runs that command bare in that worktree and replies with the result. A refusal that comes from web/node_modules behind web/package-lock.json is the dispatcher's own to fix, because no chunk session can: it runs npm ci in web and pushes again. A push that fails on the network, with GitHub down, is no result, so it sends no reply, and the session's resend after its next timeout retries it; a resend is safe, because the push then changes nothing and gh run list --commit <sha> finds the run. Several landed SHAs waiting take one push: the tip's run answers the tip, and each older SHA, which has no run of its own, gets superseded with the tip's SHA (D85). A run whose terminal reason is provider_error or provider_quota_exhausted (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/models.py:298-303), which is how a spawned session at a usage limit or in a provider outage usually ends, does not count toward the replacement limit above: the dispatcher spawns nothing more, names it in its final message, and lists again when Josh prompts it after the reset or the outage. A usage limit also holds this session's own pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands (src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_misc.py:80-84, 377-378), so after a reset Josh submits a prompt in its pane first, and then in each review's and cut's. It runs nothing else a session sends. A red result is that session's to fix: when the found-work gate holds the dispatcher's stop over it (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:35-56), it edits nothing and stops again, which that rule's attempt limit lets through. When a session reports the test hub down, it starts it as start gate item 15 says. A spawned session cannot create a task, so a finding it must file (AGENTS.md rule 4, its last rung) reaches the dispatcher through send_message(target='parent'), and the dispatcher files it as a child of #21542 with that rung's label. The dispatcher starts no chunk that a stop message names until the release message arrives. Then it ends its turn: each session it spawned wakes it on completion (spawn_agent's notify_parent_on_completion), and Josh prompts it when GEN-ROLLBACK's session, a review or a cut closes, a review's no-go files fixes or he closes a task he answered himself, as those sessions' final messages ask him to, because nothing else wakes it: a close outside its children sends it no wake, and DAEMON BACK does not wake an idle session with no claim (AGENTS.md rule 12). During a daemon hold it starts nothing. Near the context limit it calls set_handoff(clear_session=false), never true, so that its session ref stays the one its children wake: a completion wake goes to the ref its subscriber row names and a terminal ref refuses it (src/gobby/events/wake.py:537-668; src/gobby/events/live_wake.py:99), and only the mailbox follows a clear successor (src/gobby/sessions/mailbox.py:485-500). That handoff carries its prompt's model and effort, the cap, any stop in force, each SHA or test command it owes a reply and each task whose replacement died, and it fetches its tools' schemas again afterwards. It holds no other state, so after a crash Josh opens a new one with the same prompt, naming any stop still in force and the current cap. It reads the task tree and sends one project send_message with wake=true naming its session ref, which a running session then uses in place of target='parent'; sessions the old one spawned cannot wake it, so Josh prompts it as they end. This takes no code or template edit. Alternative: Josh opens every chunk session himself, which D39 allows, and applies D23's cap by hand.
decisions.rationale: The fleet stops at the first closed chunk without this: nothing else reads the ready list. One root session has the spawn authority that a spawned one may lack (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/tool-hygiene/spawn-capability-authority.yaml:5-26), never reaches the depth limit, and sits in the main checkout, where gport start runs. It needs no new seat definition, because the default agent already holds spawnable_agents ['*'] (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/default.yaml). A chain of closing sessions was rejected for the depth limit. A coordinator seat was rejected because the port does not run runbook seats (rulings 3 and 11). Josh decides because it adds one session to the ones he opens. A spawned review session was rejected, because it cannot file the tasks its no-go and its resizing need, and routing them through the dispatcher adds a path for no gain when Josh answers a review in its terminal anyway. Giving spawned sessions a git credential was rejected, because a credential a managed run can read is open to every tool in it (docs/guides/sandboxing.md:245-249), and the bundled push rule's own text is to let the parent session push (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/no-push.yaml:6). Running a session's test command for it crosses the sandbox on purpose, for the few checks that prove nothing inside it, as a coordinator already does for a worker's process evidence (docs/guides/gterminal-development-guide.md:455-456). The setting is there because this session ends its turn with no timed wait, and a session with no activity for 24 hours is marked expired (src/gobby/storage/session_lifecycle.py, whose tmux exemption #25486's Decision 12 removes), even in a live pane. A wake to an expired session is declined (src/gobby/events/live_wake.py), a message to it answers sent_recipient_not_live, a reply wait on it returns owner_ended at once, and a day later Josh's prompt no longer revives the row (src/gobby/storage/sessions/_constants.py:98-104), so every session it spawned would stall at protocol step 6 or 8 with no sign to him. A liveness check still expires a session whose pane has gone (src/gobby/sessions/liveness_monitor.py), so the longer bound leaves only rows with a live pane in place. An hourly self-wake was rejected, because it spends a full uncached turn every hour for the whole port.

decisions.question: What makes the port 1.0, and which chunk ships it? No chunk sets a 1.0 version: the gobby binary is the client at 0.1.107 (crates/gclient/Cargo.toml:3), and D55 only raises the tap formula's version_scheme above the Python releases. CP-NODE-CUT publishes the promoted versions, then POST-CLEAN bumps again, publishes nothing and closes #21542, so the port's last commit never ships. GitHub's default branch, main, still sits at 'Release v0.4.9' (45b0ea0e6a). CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] has no owner, because S3-DELETE keeps that file as a historical record. README.md:320 still promises a 0.6.0 Rust port release and README.md:352 calls Gobby pre-1.0, FEATURES.md:3 names the pre-port codebase and docs/guides/release-guide.md:8-17 lists versions from before the port. Installable today are PyPI 0.4.6, Homebrew 0.4.4 and standalone gcode 1.5.0 and ghook 0.7.2; v0.4.9 was tagged but never packaged.
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: POST-CLEAN ships it, under CP-NODE-REVIEW's go (A16-POSTCLEAN). The product version is the gobby binary's: POST-CLEAN's activation commit sets crates/gclient/Cargo.toml's version to 1.0.0 in place of its patch bump, with Cargo.lock and the managed pins (V1A's version pins), and its tag is gclient-v1.0.0 (D55). Every other binary keeps its own version line and takes its ordinary bump. Any client change after the activation commit's promotion, an outcome-2 fix or a retry's, takes the next patch version (D39), and the release names that version. The same commit turns CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] into [1.0.0] with its date and adds the upgrade note: Python and the PyPI package are gone, and PyPI stays at 0.4.6 (D55); Homebrew's gobby formula now installs the Rust set (D60) and conflicts with gobby-code and gobby-hooks, so a Homebrew user uninstalls those first (D127); and nothing reads or migrates a 0.4.x install's SQLite hub (AGENTS.md rule 10), so it reinstalls from README.md's Install section and starts a fresh hub. It also makes README.md's 'What shipped in 0.4.x' (:155), 'Where it's going' (:298-349) and 'Status and contributing' (:352), FEATURES.md:3, ROADMAP.md's 'Where we are' (:12) and docs/guides/release-guide.md's Current Release Set (:8-17) state what ships. After the cut's clean window, and before it pushes its port/POST-CLEAN tag or clears the freeze, the hold and the pin, which it first extends to cover the publication and the live node's update, Josh fast-forwards origin/main to the commit the cut last promoted with git push origin <that SHA>:refs/heads/main: his admin role bypasses main's ruleset, which otherwise requires a pull request and the Merge Gate check, and a fast-forward keeps that commit at main's head. origin/main is an ancestor of the pre-cut branch today, so of 0.9.0, and CP-NODE-REVIEW's packet rechecks that with git merge-base --is-ancestor. He then pushes a release tag for each member whose manifest version differs from its last published tag, in the release guide's Tag Order, each tag in its own push, as at CP-NODE-CUT. The session checks each release as CP-NODE-CUT does, then that the client's release is marked latest, that crates.io holds gobby-client at that version and, once the tap's update job has run and Josh has merged the pull request it opens (D127), that GobbyAI/homebrew-tap's gobby formula names it and Tap CI's run on main passes, and sets the client release's notes from CHANGELOG.md's section with gh release edit --notes-file, because the workflow generates its own (.github/workflows/release-gclient.yml:196). The hub's release target then offers the new gdaemon to the live node through CP-NODE-CUT's path, and once gobby node status there reports healthy at that version, within the bound CP-NODE-CUT's window plan recorded, the session tags the last commit the cut promoted as port/POST-CLEAN, because an earlier tag would leave a release fix with no tag of its own (D40 item 4), pushes the tag, clears the freeze, the hold and the pin and closes the cut; a failure there is this cut's named trigger, under its trigger table. A release job that failed on a GitHub or crates.io outage is rerun with gh run rerun <id> --failed on the same tag, which is no outcome. Any other failed release job takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) with the next patch version, a new release tag and main fast-forwarded to it, and a pushed tag never moves. Alternatives: publish CP-NODE-CUT's client tag as 1.0.0 and leave POST-CLEAN's drops to a 1.0.1, which calls a build 1.0 while it still carries the old USER.md paths and the tables POST-CLEAN drops; or give every binary 1.0.0, which moves gcode, at 1.9.103, below its own floor and below gobby-code 1.5.0, which crates.io already holds.
decisions.rationale: Josh's word on #25279 is 'When we finish 1.0 there will be no python', and #21542 is titled Gobby 1.0 (ROADMAP.md:10), yet no text gives any binary that number or publishes the last commit. POST-CLEAN can own it with no new chunk: it is the last cut, it closes #21542, its go already carries public steps, and only its clean window proves the commit that gets the number. One number on the binary users run leaves each member's version line and release guard as they are. main has to move because it is what the repository shows and what a clone gets; it takes no merge, because it has no commit of its own since v0.4.9 (git rev-list HEAD..origin/main is empty). Josh decides because a version number, a tag and a default branch are public and irreversible.

decisions.question: The git guard's reference-transaction hook runs python3 for its policy read and its ghook payload (src/gobby/cli/installers/git_hooks.py:76-240). What runs those two steps at 1.0, when V1A drops Python from the dependency contract and the daemon runs no Python?
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it changes a guard every checkout installs and widens ghook's surface.
decisions.recommended_default: V1B moves both snippets into ghook: one mode reads the committed allow_direct_integration_commits policy with its three exits, and one builds the payload from the branch and the staged paths and runs the same verdict mapping. The guard stays POSIX sh and calls only git and ghook. The new ghook ships in CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A (D39), commit A cites the install golden's changed lines as an accepted change (D84), and a guard installed earlier keeps python3 until the next gobby install. Alternative with no Rust: V1B writes the guard unchanged, V1A keeps python3 as a required dependency row, docs/guides/system-requirements.md keeps it, and S4-PROOF's python3 tripwire exempts git hooks.
decisions.rationale: On a host with no python3 the guard refuses every update of the checked-out protected branch outside land_commit, with python3 is not on PATH, and a reference-transaction hook cannot be skipped with --no-verify, so a Python-free 1.0 install could make no permitted direct commit. The alternative keeps a Python dependency at 1.0, against V1A's dropped runtime row and S4-PROOF.

decisions.question: From CP-WAVE4-CUT native PIPE-2 runs pipeline steps, and a step's tool can stay Python's until CP-WAVE5-CUT. Python's operator gate reads daemon-owned execution and the pipeline execution id from context variables that a GW-2 compatibility call does not set (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/communications.py:153-170, 250). How does the archivist digest's send_operator_attachment keep working in that window?
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it adds calls to GW-2's endpoint beyond D4's listed clause.
decisions.recommended_default: GW-2's endpoint request also carries daemon-owned execution and the pipeline execution id, accepted only from SEAM-CALLERS' internal caller class, and the endpoint sets the existing context variables around the call (src/gobby/utils/session_context.py:134-154), with no new module, no longer called at CP-WAVE5-CUT and deleted by S3-DELETE. Alternative with no Python edit: the digest's delivery refuses from CP-WAVE4-CUT to CP-WAVE5-CUT, and CP-WAVE4-REVIEW's packet records it as a known regression.
decisions.rationale: With no scope the call takes the installed caller's path and refuses, because a step's bound caller has no operator_messaging of its own, so the daily digest stops for one cut's span. The marker adds one condition to an endpoint that already exists and serves only the internal class.

decisions.question: Who writes and exports spans once S3-DELETE removes Python's tracer? The map owns the two trace routes and the span cleanup job, and names no writer.
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it drops a documented operator surface from 1.0 and defers a plan he approved.
decisions.recommended_default: 1.0 writes no spans and exports none. OBS serves the two trace routes and the cleanup job over the rows that exist until retention empties them. Python's span sites, GobbySpanExporter and the OTLP, console and LLM instrumentors are not ported. CP-FINAL-CUT removes the keys and settings rows that would then do nothing and says so in the docs. Prometheus metrics and the file log surfaces stay. #18996, whose written OTLP plan Josh approved on 2026-09-29, stays open for after 1.0 and lands on the native stack. Alternatives: (a) port the span sites and the private store with no OTLP; (b) land #18996 natively before 1.0 with opentelemetry-otlp, which needs a new crate decision and a chunk.
decisions.rationale: #18996's description records the 2026-09-29 approval and docs/guides/observability.md:207-209 still reads paused; that plan has not landed, sits outside #21542, and replaces the private span store and routes on Python's stack. No 0.x release carries this surface (AGENTS rule 10), the Activity panel hides the Traces tab (docs/guides/observability.md:194-211), and the default configuration exports nowhere. A writer and exporter means every span site (src/gobby/hooks/hook_manager.py:244; src/gobby/workflows/engine/core.py:254) plus opentelemetry crates. Leaving the settings rows drawn would make controls that do nothing (AGENTS rule 4).

decisions.question: Who carries a cut when its session stops? From step 3 on, a cut session holds the task the landing freeze is bound to, the only copy of the hold token, which is in its transcript, and the observation window's watch. A dead pane, a usage limit or a provider outage stops it, and no text says who resumes it, where the token comes from or what happens if a trigger fires meanwhile. A rollback at CP-WAVE5-CUT can also take the pane that runs it, when the rehearsal measured that open panes do not survive the hand-back.
decisions.status: Default. Josh confirms it at map approval.
decisions.recommended_default: Nothing rolls back by itself. A usage limit or a provider outage leaves the pane and the claim, because the session stays live (src/gobby/storage/tasks/_automation.py:89), and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches it. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu with automatic input blocked, so no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset, and a session cannot release its own composer (src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_misc.py:80-84, 377-378; src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:603-612). Either way the session then reads the whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. When the pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14). It takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, because the freeze admits the bound task's claim holder (GEN-ROLLBACK); reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each; resumes at the step the task's attestations show; registers the watch and its waits again; and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it (src/gobby/tasks/attestations.py:268-275). If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's gobby rollback restore from his own shell, and the replacement finishes the recipe. This takes no code or template edit. Alternative: a watchdog that restores the pinned generation on a health failure when no session answers, which needs new daemon code, cannot apply the trigger table Josh approved and could fire during a fix-forward.
decisions.rationale: The hold and the freeze already outlive their session: a hold carries an expiry, Josh can clear it with gobby rollback hold clear, and the freeze binds to the task rather than to one session (GEN-ROLLBACK). So a second session can carry on from the task record once that record holds the token. Protocol step 1 already resumes a dead chunk session this way; a cut had no such text. The token guards against a promotion by mistake, not against a reader, and every session on P is Josh's, so an attestation is a fair place for it. Josh decides because this names him as the one who wakes for a dead cut session or one at its usage limit, and the live daemon can sit on an activated build until he does.

decisions.recommended_default: Josh puts the Codex and Grok CLIs on P beside Claude Code, before item 17's first gobby install so that it writes their hooks (src/gobby/cli/install.py:352-365), and logs in to both with the provider logins item 17 already leaves to him. The seats then run as the policy names them, chunk sessions stay on Claude (D116), and a candidate's reviewer stays a different vendor from its author, as on A. No code, template or policy edit. Alternative: P's policy commit (start gate item 12) sets both agent_model_defaults entries to provider claude with a Claude model, so step 7's call and D115's command stay as written, which needs no new CLI or login but loses a second vendor's eye on every landing.

Provider arguments on each spawn were rejected for the alternative, because every session and D115's command would then carry a model literal that one policy entry already decides. Josh decides because this adds credentials to a second machine and spends on two more vendors, or trades away a different vendor's review.

decisions.question: Differential replay never sends an attack, so a Python trust check that no brief names passes every oracle when a port leaves it out, and reqwest and axum defaults differ silently from httpx and Starlette. What binds a session porting a module that holds such a check, what do its native HTTP clients, body reads and child processes default to, and who renders the bundled prompts that delimit untrusted text before the rules crate exists?
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval on its prompt clause only: an override of expansion/user or features/server_description with other Jinja syntax refuses natively, where Python renders it.
decisions.recommended_default: (1) A chunk that ports a Python module ports every check in it that refuses, bounds, redacts or confines untrusted input, named in its brief or not, and replays the Python negative tests that pin the check as native cases. A check it cannot carry is a Found Work gap, never a silent difference. (2) A native HTTP client keeps the policy of the Python client it replaces. httpx follows no redirect unless that client sets follow_redirects=True and reqwest follows ten by default, so each client states redirect::Policy::none() or Python's rule, keeping Python's same-origin rule where it has one (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/transports/http.py:25-40). trust_env=False becomes .no_proxy(), as crates/gcore/src/loopback.rs:137 does. (3) A native route that reads a body states its limit, because axum's Bytes, Json, String and Multipart extractors stop at DefaultBodyLimit's 2 MiB and Starlette has no limit: Python's limit where it has one, otherwise one at least as large as the largest recorded use. (4) PLANS adds a subset render with the untrusted filter to crates/gruntime/src/prompts.rs, on the refusal that .gobby/plans/memory-family.md Decision 12 and SES-3B already set, so no template engine enters outside the rules crate (D76), and MUX-2 reuses it. Hook prompts render through RULE-1B's engine, which HOOK-2 reaches. chunk_protocol's note carries (1) to (3), (5) and (6). Alternative for (4): minijinja in the plans crate too, which renders any override and takes D76's exception and an earlier first consumer for the pin. (5) A native child whose Python spawn passes env= starts with env_clear() and that map, because Python's env= replaces the environment and Rust's Command inherits gdaemon's, secrets included. (6) A chunk that reuses existing native code lists Python's steps on that path against the native code's before its oracle runs, and ports each missing step or reports it under Found Work, because an oracle that compares native output with native output proves nothing about parity. AG-1's launch path lacked four of Python's steps, found only because one review compared them; the other reused paths have not been compared.
decisions.rationale: A corpus records real traffic, so an absent signature check, Host check, redaction or body cap replays equal. The guards found without a chunk's words include /mcp's Host and Origin policy, the login limiter, Argon2id, the sign-in link, the webhook SSRF transport, comms verification and access, the terminal output redactor, the prompt delimiter and the pipeline environment filter; each now has an owner, and the rule covers what that sweep did not sample. No crate in the workspace sets a redirect policy, and the Python clients take both values (src/gobby/ai/decisions.py:587; src/gobby/communications/attachments.py:47). PLANS lands before RULE-1B and RULE-1B reaches PLANS, so PLANS cannot call the rules crate, and expansion/user's six | untrusted expressions must render with their delimiter (tests/prompts/test_untrusted_content_prompts.py:56). A port that only copies an env= map keeps gdaemon's environment in the child, which undoes a deliberate minimal one (src/gobby/adapters/acp_terminal.py:50-69, 148; src/gobby/agents/srt_monitor.py:329), as crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/monitor.rs:204 already avoids.

decisions.question: The guard ports need crates that Cargo.lock lacks: argon2 for AUTH's password hash, lettre and async-imap for COMMS-2's email adapter, and reqwest's socks feature, which adds tokio-socks, for its Telegram proxy. Teams' RS256 check could add jsonwebtoken. The cron, backup and skills plans also name croner with chrono-tz, tar and zip, which no map decision records, and SKILLS and AG-1 need tar before the backup chunk does. May they enter, and at which pins?
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: new third-party crates.
decisions.recommended_default: Yes. Each is exact-pinned at its newest release that is at least two weeks old when its first consumer starts (AUTH for argon2, COMMS-2 for lettre, async-imap and the socks feature, CRON for croner and chrono-tz, SKILLS for zip and tar, with AG-1's Zig mirror and V1A taking tar after it), only in the crate that needs it, as D8 and D76 place theirs. argon2 stays out of gclient, gcode and ghook. Teams' RS256 and Discord's Ed25519 use ring directly, which Cargo.lock already holds at 0.17.14, with the check's alg fixed at RS256, so jsonwebtoken does not enter. The cron plan's croner 4.0.1 yields to this pin rule, and the Skills plan's zip, its single authorized library, gains tar, because the GitHub topic hub unpacks the tarball it downloads. Alternatives: jsonwebtoken 11.1.0 for Teams, which also needs a crypto backend choice; moving email after 1.0 instead of taking its two crates, which reverses D28's list.
decisions.rationale: crates.io on 2026-11-05. argon2 0.6.0, 2026-08-27, MIT OR Apache-2.0, msrv 1.85, owners newpavlov and github:rustcrypto:kdfs, 71.8M downloads. lettre 0.11.23, 2026-08-03, MIT, msrv 1.85, owners amousset and github:lettre:release, 23.1M. async-imap 0.12.0, 2026-09-30, MIT OR Apache-2.0, msrv 1.88, owners dignifiedquire and link2xt, 2.16M; the older imap crate is synchronous and its last release, 3.0.0-alpha.15, dates from 2025-02-08, so it is rejected. tokio-socks 0.5.3, 2026-05-29, MIT, owner sticnarf, 24.9M. jsonwebtoken 11.1.0, 2026-09-16, MIT, msrv 1.88, owner Keats, 234M. croner 4.0.3, 2026-11-04, then 4.0.2, 2026-10-21, and 4.0.1, 2026-10-02, MIT, owner Hexagon, 12.2M, so the pin is 4.0.2 or newer by CRON's start. chrono-tz 0.10.4, 2025-07-11, MIT OR Apache-2.0, msrv 1.65, owners quodlibetor and github:chronotope:release-manager, 190.4M, which the cron plan names beside croner. tar 0.4.46, 2026-05-18, MIT OR Apache-2.0, msrv 1.63, owner cgwalters, 278.6M. zip 9.3.0, 2026-11-03, MIT, msrv 1.88, owners Plecra and Pr0methean, 331.7M, with three releases in the last three days, which the pin rule already waits out. All clear the workspace's 1.88 floor (D76). Stored password rows hold Argon2id hashes (src/gobby/identity.py), so the crate is not optional, and ring already provides both signature checks, so a JWT crate adds a dependency tree for one fixed algorithm. SKILLS needs tar first because Python's topic hub downloads /tarball/<sha> and unpacks it (src/gobby/skills/hubs/github_topic.py:128, 476), and AG-1's Zig mirror unpacks tarball entries (src/gobby/agents/zig_packages.py:44-57). ring is the workspace's one crypto backend (crates/gdaemon/Cargo.toml:39).

decisions.question: Who writes GobbyAI/homebrew-tap's formula change? D55 and D60 say the tap makes it before the first gclient-v* tag after commit B, and CP-NODE-REVIEW had Josh confirm it is merged, but no chunk or person is named to write it, and a spawned session cannot reach github.com.
decisions.status: Default. Needs Josh's word at map approval: it has a session write to a repository outside this one under his login.
decisions.recommended_default: CP-NODE-REVIEW's session opens the pull request on GobbyAI/homebrew-tap while it builds its packet, through gh api and gh pr create with no local clone, because it is unspawned and holds P's git and gh logins (start gate item 17). The pull request makes D55's and D60's changes: the gobby formula installs the client archive with its version_scheme raised and carries the member binaries as D60 decides, and the tap's update job waits until every member's archive at those versions exists. The change goes in the tap's .github/scripts/update_formulae.py as well as the formula, because the update job rewrites Formula/gobby.rb from that script's template on every dispatch, and the job loses its brew update-python-resources step, which only a Python formula can take. The template's test block changes with it: it asserts 'gobby, version <version>' from gobby --version and runs --version on gcode, ghook, gloc and gsqz, so it would fail on the client that CP-NODE-CUT's tag releases. It asserts the version alone, as the script's helper template already does, which also holds through POST-CLEAN's rename, and its loop names the binaries the formula provides. Tap CI's Homebrew install step takes the flags the native install verb takes. The script's four helpers go with their formulae and depends_on lines, gobby-local and gobby-squeeze having already left this workspace (crates/CHANGELOG.md:676), and the gobby formula declares conflicts_with for gobby-code and gobby-hooks, because each links the same bin/gcode or bin/ghook. The packet names the pull request, and Josh merges it before CP-NODE-CUT's gclient tag, the first after commit B, which dispatches to it. The update job ends by opening a pull request of its own and merges nothing, so after each gclient tag Josh merges that one too; until he does, the formula does not name the release. A request the job opens with the default token starts no run of its own, so Tap CI's run on main after the merge is the check. Nothing in this repository changes. Alternative: Josh writes and merges the change himself, and the packet only reminds him.
decisions.rationale: The tap's formula change is a deliverable that CP-NODE-CUT's tag and POST-CLEAN's release check both need, and it had no author, so the first reader to notice would have been the review that needs it merged. No earlier chunk can write it: S3-NAME and S4-RELEASE run spawned, with no route to GitHub (D116), so neither can read the tap's formula or its update job. A new chunk would add a task for one pull request in another repository, with no oracle in this one. Josh decides because the session writes to a repository outside this one under his login.

Resolved (D39, option B as amended): landings bump gdaemon and never promote, so no landing waits for a restart, active hours or a protected-runs answer. The cost moves to the checkpoint cuts: each promotes everything landed since the previous cut at once, under its rehearsal, window and recipe, and a dormant landing's first live run is its cut's activation (D37).

Landing-freeze throughput: each cutover freezes all landing but its own from step 3 to its close (8 hours to a full day, plus any fix-forward up to its bound), so other sessions' finished chunks queue; the owner-bound freeze closes the race in which another session's commit slipped in around a fix, and the HEAD check still guards it.

No code reads project_policy.quiet_hours, but a project rule repeats its windows and refuses gobby start, stop, restart and cutover in every hooked session during them; gobby rollback and gobby hub-backup pass, and Josh's own shell is outside it (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:3-7, 15-25). So an emergency rollback during quiet hours needs a standing ruling, which every review packet asks for until Josh gives one. Default until he does: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure runs the recipe at once, even in quiet hours, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message; any other outcome-3 trigger that fires in quiet hours waits for them to end, with the hold and the pin extended.
